lessons.title: Exercise 1.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Write in standard form and point out pure quadratic equations: (x + 7)(x - 3) = -7

Step 1: Expand the left side: (x + 7)(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x + 7x - 21 = x^2 + 4x - 21.

Step 2: Bring all terms to the left: x^2 + 4x - 21 = -7, so x^2 + 4x - 21 + 7 = 0.

Step 3: Standard form: x^2 + 4x - 14 = 0.

Here a = 1, b = 4, c = -14. Since b is not 0, it is NOT a pure quadratic equation.

Q1(ii) Write in standard form: (x^2 + 4)/3 - x/7 = 1

Step 1: Multiply every term by LCM(3, 7) = 21: 7(x^2 + 4) - 3x = 21.

Step 2: Expand: 7x^2 + 28 - 3x = 21.

Step 3: Bring all terms to the left: 7x^2 - 3x + 28 - 21 = 0.

Step 4: Standard form: 7x^2 - 3x + 7 = 0.

Here a = 7, b = -3, c = 7. Since b is not 0, it is NOT a pure quadratic equation.

Q1(iii) Write in standard form: x/(x + 1) + (x + 1)/x = 6

Step 1: Take LCM x(x + 1): [x^2 + (x + 1)^2] / [x(x + 1)] = 6.

Step 2: Cross-multiply: x^2 + x^2 + 2x + 1 = 6x(x + 1) = 6x^2 + 6x.

Step 3: Bring all terms to one side: 0 = 6x^2 + 6x - 2x^2 - 2x - 1.

Step 4: Standard form: 4x^2 + 4x - 1 = 0 (x not 0, -1).

Here a = 4, b = 4, c = -1. Since b is not 0, it is NOT a pure quadratic equation.

Q1(iv) Write in standard form: (x + 4)/(x - 2) - (x - 2)/x + 4 = 0

Step 1: Take LCM x(x - 2): x(x + 4) - (x - 2)^2 + 4x(x - 2) = 0.

Step 2: Expand: x^2 + 4x - (x^2 - 4x + 4) + 4x^2 - 8x = 0.

Step 3: Simplify: x^2 + 4x - x^2 + 4x - 4 + 4x^2 - 8x = 0, so 4x^2 + 0x - 4 = 0.

Step 4: Standard form: 4x^2 - 4 = 0, i.e. x^2 - 1 = 0.

Here a = 4, b = 0, c = -4. Since b = 0, it IS a pure quadratic equation.

Q1(v) Write in standard form: (x + 3)/(x + 4) - (x - 5)/x = 1

Step 1: Take LCM x(x + 4): x(x + 3) - (x - 5)(x + 4) = x(x + 4).

Step 2: Expand: x^2 + 3x - (x^2 - x - 20) = x^2 + 4x, so x^2 + 3x - x^2 + x + 20 = x^2 + 4x.

Step 3: Simplify the left side: 4x + 20 = x^2 + 4x.

Step 4: Bring all terms to one side: 0 = x^2 + 4x - 4x - 20, so x^2 - 20 = 0.

Standard form: x^2 - 20 = 0. Here a = 1, b = 0, c = -20. Since b = 0, it IS a pure quadratic equation.

Q1(vi) Write in standard form: (x + 1)/(x + 2) + (x + 2)/(x + 3) = 25/12

Step 1: Take LCM 12(x + 2)(x + 3): 12[(x + 1)(x + 3) + (x + 2)^2] = 25(x + 2)(x + 3).

Step 2: Expand inside: (x^2 + 4x + 3) + (x^2 + 4x + 4) = 2x^2 + 8x + 7, and (x + 2)(x + 3) = x^2 + 5x + 6.

Step 3: 12(2x^2 + 8x + 7) = 25(x^2 + 5x + 6), so 24x^2 + 96x + 84 = 25x^2 + 125x + 150.

Step 4: Bring all terms to one side: 0 = x^2 + 29x + 66.

Standard form: x^2 + 29x + 66 = 0. Here a = 1, b = 29, c = 66. Since b is not 0, it is NOT a pure quadratic equation.

Solve by factorization: x^2 - x - 20 = 0

Step 1: Write in standard form with a = 1, b = -1, c = -20.

Step 2: Compute ac = (1)(-20) = -20. Find two numbers with sum b = -1 and product ac = -20: -5 and 4, since -5 + 4 = -1 and (-5)(4) = -20.

Step 3: Split the middle term: 1x^2 - 5x + 4x - 20 = 0.

Step 4: Factor by grouping (taking common factors from each pair).

Step 5: By the zero-product rule, one factor is zero at a time; solving gives x = -4, 5.

Solution set = {-4, 5}.

Q2(ii) Solve by factorization: 3y^2 = y(y - 5)

Step 1: Expand the right side: 3y^2 = y^2 - 5y.

Step 2: Bring all terms to the left: 3y^2 - y^2 + 5y = 0, so 2y^2 + 5y = 0.

Step 3: Take out the common factor y: y(2y + 5) = 0.

Step 4: Either y = 0, or 2y + 5 = 0 which gives y = -5/2.

Solution set = {-5/2, 0}.

Solve by factorization: 4 - 32x = 17x^2, i.e. 17x^2 + 32x - 4 = 0

Step 1: Write in standard form with a = 17, b = 32, c = -4.

Step 2: Compute ac = (17)(-4) = -68. Find two numbers with sum b = 32 and product ac = -68: 34 and -2, since 34 - 2 = 32 and (34)(-2) = -68.

Step 3: Split the middle term: 17x^2 + 34x - 2x - 4 = 0.

Step 4: Factor by grouping (taking common factors from each pair).

Step 5: By the zero-product rule, one factor is zero at a time; solving gives x = -2, 2/17.

Solution set = {-2, 2/17}.

Solve by factorization: x^2 - 11x = 152, i.e. x^2 - 11x - 152 = 0

Step 1: Write in standard form with a = 1, b = -11, c = -152.

Step 2: Compute ac = (1)(-152) = -152. Find two numbers with sum b = -11 and product ac = -152: -19 and 8, since -19 + 8 = -11 and (-19)(8) = -152.

Step 3: Split the middle term: 1x^2 - 19x + 8x - 152 = 0.

Step 4: Factor by grouping (taking common factors from each pair).

Step 5: By the zero-product rule, one factor is zero at a time; solving gives x = -8, 19.

Solution set = {-8, 19}.

Q2(v) Solve by factorization: (x + 1)/x + x/(x + 1) = 25/12

Step 1: Take LCM 12x(x + 1): 12[(x + 1)^2 + x^2] = 25x(x + 1).

Step 2: Expand: 12(2x^2 + 2x + 1) = 25x^2 + 25x, so 24x^2 + 24x + 12 = 25x^2 + 25x.

Step 3: Standard form: x^2 + x - 12 = 0.

Step 4: ac = -12; two numbers with sum 1 and product -12 are 4 and -3.

Step 5: x^2 + 4x - 3x - 12 = 0, so x(x + 4) - 3(x + 4) = 0, so (x + 4)(x - 3) = 0.

Step 6: Either x + 4 = 0 giving x = -4, or x - 3 = 0 giving x = 3.

Solution set = {-4, 3}.

Q2(vi) Solve by factorization: 2/(x - 9) = 1/(x - 3) - 1/(x - 4)

Step 1: Simplify the right side: [ (x - 4) - (x - 3) ] / [(x - 3)(x - 4)] = -1 / [(x - 3)(x - 4)].

Step 2: Cross-multiply: 2(x - 3)(x - 4) = -(x - 9) = 9 - x.

Step 3: Expand: 2(x^2 - 7x + 12) = 9 - x, so 2x^2 - 14x + 24 - 9 + x = 0, so 2x^2 - 13x + 15 = 0.

Step 4: ac = 30; two numbers with sum -13 and product 30 are -10 and -3.

Step 5: 2x^2 - 10x - 3x + 15 = 0, so 2x(x - 5) - 3(x - 5) = 0, so (x - 5)(2x - 3) = 0.

Step 6: Either x - 5 = 0 giving x = 5, or 2x - 3 = 0 giving x = 3/2.

Solution set = {3/2, 5}.

Q3(i) 7x^2 + 2x - 1 = 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {(-1 - 2.sqrt(2))/7, (-1 + 2.sqrt(2))/7}.

Q3(ii) ax^2 + 4x - a = 0, a not 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {(-2 - sqrt(a^2 + 4))/a, (-2 + sqrt(a^2 + 4))/a}.

Q3(iii) 11x^2 - 34x + 3 = 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {1/11, 3}.

Q3(iv) lx^2 + mx + n = 0, l not 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {[-m - sqrt(m^2 - 4ln)]/(2l), [-m + sqrt(m^2 - 4ln)]/(2l)}.

Q3(v) 3x^2 + 7x = 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {-7/3, 0}.

Q3(vi) x^2 - 2x - 195 = 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {-13, 15}.

Q3(vii) -x^2 + 15/2 = (7/2)x — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {-5, 3/2}.

Q3(viii) x^2 + 17x + 33/4 = 0 — Solve by completing square

Method (completing square): Step 1: Make the coefficient of x^2 equal to 1 by dividing every term by it.

Step 2: Shift the constant term to the right side.

Step 3: Formula: add (half of the coefficient of x)^2 to BOTH sides, i.e. add (b/2)^2 where the equation is x^2 + bx = c.

Step 4: Write the left side as a perfect square (x + b/2)^2.

Step 5: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both + and - values.

Step 6: Solve the two linear equations separately.

Solution set = {-33/2, -1/2}.

Q3(ix) Solve by completing square: 4 - 8/(3x + 1) = (3x^2 + 5)/(3x + 1)

Step 1: Multiply every term by (3x + 1): 4(3x + 1) - 8 = 3x^2 + 5.

Step 2: Expand: 12x + 4 - 8 = 3x^2 + 5, so 12x - 4 = 3x^2 + 5.

Step 3: Standard form: 3x^2 - 12x + 9 = 0; divide by 3: x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0.

Step 4: Shift the constant: x^2 - 4x = -3.

Step 5: Formula: add (half of -4)^2 = (-2)^2 = 4 to both sides: x^2 - 4x + 4 = -3 + 4 = 1.

Step 6: Write as a square: (x - 2)^2 = 1.

Step 7: Take square roots: x - 2 = +1 or x - 2 = -1.

Step 8: x = 3 or x = 1.

Solution set = {1, 3}.

Q3(x) Solve by completing square: 7(x + 2a)^2 + 3a^2 = 5a(7x + 23a)

Step 1: Expand: 7(x^2 + 4ax + 4a^2) + 3a^2 = 35ax + 115a^2, so 7x^2 + 28ax + 28a^2 + 3a^2 = 35ax + 115a^2.

Step 2: Simplify and bring all terms left: 7x^2 + 28ax - 35ax + 31a^2 - 115a^2 = 0, so 7x^2 - 7ax - 84a^2 = 0.

Step 3: Divide by 7: x^2 - ax - 12a^2 = 0.

Step 4: Shift the constant: x^2 - ax = 12a^2.

Step 5: Formula: add (half of -a)^2 = a^2/4 to both sides: x^2 - ax + a^2/4 = 12a^2 + a^2/4 = 49a^2/4.

Step 6: Write as a square: (x - a/2)^2 = 49a^2/4.

Step 7: Take square roots: x - a/2 = 7a/2 or x - a/2 = -7a/2.

Step 8: x = a/2 + 7a/2 = 4a, or x = a/2 - 7a/2 = -3a.

Solution set = {-3a, 4a}.

mcqs.q: What is the standard form of (x + 7)(x - 3) = -7?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand: (x + 7)(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x + 7x - 21 = x^2 + 4x - 21. Step 2: Bring -7 to the left: x^2 + 4x - 21 + 7 = 0. Step 3: Standard form is x^2 + 4x - 14 = 0, with a = 1, b = 4, c = -14.

mcqs.q: The equation x^2 + 4x - 14 = 0 is NOT a pure quadratic equation because:
mcqs.why: A pure quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 has b = 0. Here a = 1, b = 4, c = -14. Since b = 4 is not 0, the linear term is present, so the equation is not pure.

mcqs.q: What is the standard form of (x^2 + 4)/3 - x/7 = 1?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply by LCM(3, 7) = 21: 7(x^2 + 4) - 3x = 21. Step 2: Expand: 7x^2 + 28 - 3x = 21. Step 3: Bring all terms left: 7x^2 - 3x + 28 - 21 = 0, giving 7x^2 - 3x + 7 = 0.

mcqs.q: Which of the following equations is a pure quadratic equation?
mcqs.why: A pure quadratic has b = 0. In 4x^2 - 4 = 0 (from (x + 4)/(x - 2) - (x - 2)/x + 4 = 0), a = 4, b = 0, c = -4, so b = 0 and it is pure. The other three all have b not equal to 0.

mcqs.q: What is the standard form of (x + 3)/(x + 4) - (x - 5)/x = 1?
mcqs.why: Step 1: LCM x(x + 4): x(x + 3) - (x - 5)(x + 4) = x(x + 4). Step 2: Expand: x^2 + 3x - (x^2 - x - 20) = x^2 + 4x, so 4x + 20 = x^2 + 4x. Step 3: Bring all terms to one side: x^2 - 20 = 0, with b = 0, so it is pure.

mcqs.q: In the standard form x^2 + 29x + 66 = 0 of (x + 1)/(x + 2) + (x + 2)/(x + 3) = 25/12, the value of c is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: With LCM 12(x + 2)(x + 3): 12(2x^2 + 8x + 7) = 25(x^2 + 5x + 6). Step 2: 24x^2 + 96x + 84 = 25x^2 + 125x + 150. Step 3: Bringing all terms to one side gives x^2 + 29x + 66 = 0, so a = 1, b = 29 and c = 66.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: x^2 - x - 20 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 1, b = -1, c = -20, so ac = -20. Step 2: Two numbers with sum -1 and product -20 are -5 and 4. Step 3: Split: x^2 - 5x + 4x - 20 = 0, factor by grouping to (x - 5)(x + 4) = 0. Step 4: x - 5 = 0 gives x = 5; x + 4 = 0 gives x = -4. Solution set = {-4, 5}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 3y^2 = y(y - 5). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand the right side: 3y^2 = y^2 - 5y. Step 2: Bring all terms left: 2y^2 + 5y = 0. Step 3: Take out the common factor y: y(2y + 5) = 0. Step 4: y = 0, or 2y + 5 = 0 giving y = -5/2. Solution set = {-5/2, 0}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 17x^2 + 32x - 4 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 17, b = 32, c = -4, so ac = -68. Step 2: Two numbers with sum 32 and product -68 are 34 and -2. Step 3: Split: 17x^2 + 34x - 2x - 4 = 0, factor by grouping to (x + 2)(17x - 2) = 0. Step 4: x = -2, or 17x = 2 giving x = 2/17. Solution set = {-2, 2/17}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: x^2 - 11x - 152 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 1, b = -11, c = -152, so ac = -152. Step 2: Two numbers with sum -11 and product -152 are -19 and 8. Step 3: Split: x^2 - 19x + 8x - 152 = 0, factor by grouping to (x - 19)(x + 8) = 0. Step 4: x = 19, or x = -8. Solution set = {-8, 19}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: (x + 1)/x + x/(x + 1) = 25/12. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: LCM 12x(x + 1): 12[(x + 1)^2 + x^2] = 25x(x + 1), giving 24x^2 + 24x + 12 = 25x^2 + 25x. Step 2: Standard form: x^2 + x - 12 = 0. Step 3: ac = -12; numbers with sum 1 and product -12 are 4 and -3: (x + 4)(x - 3) = 0. Step 4: x = -4 or x = 3. Solution set = {-4, 3}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 2/(x - 9) = 1/(x - 3) - 1/(x - 4). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The right side simplifies to -1/[(x - 3)(x - 4)]. Step 2: Cross-multiply: 2(x - 3)(x - 4) = 9 - x, giving 2x^2 - 13x + 15 = 0. Step 3: ac = 30; numbers with sum -13 and product 30 are -10 and -3: (x - 5)(2x - 3) = 0. Step 4: x = 5 or x = 3/2. Solution set = {3/2, 5}.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: 3x^2 + 7x = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Divide by 3: x^2 + (7/3)x = 0. Step 2: Formula: add (half of 7/3)^2 = (7/6)^2 to both sides: (x + 7/6)^2 = 49/36. Step 3: Take square roots: x + 7/6 = 7/6 or x + 7/6 = -7/6. Step 4: x = 0 or x = -7/3. Solution set = {-7/3, 0}.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: x^2 - 2x - 195 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Shift the constant: x^2 - 2x = 195. Step 2: Formula: add (half of -2)^2 = 1 to both sides: x^2 - 2x + 1 = 196. Step 3: Write as a square: (x - 1)^2 = 196. Step 4: Take square roots: x - 1 = 14 or x - 1 = -14. Step 5: x = 15 or x = -13. Solution set = {-13, 15}.

mcqs.q: Solve by completing the square: 7(x + 2a)^2 + 3a^2 = 5a(7x + 23a). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand: 7x^2 + 28ax + 31a^2 = 35ax + 115a^2, so 7x^2 - 7ax - 84a^2 = 0. Step 2: Divide by 7: x^2 - ax - 12a^2 = 0, so x^2 - ax = 12a^2. Step 3: Formula: add (a/2)^2 = a^2/4 to both sides: (x - a/2)^2 = 49a^2/4. Step 4: x - a/2 = 7a/2 or -7a/2. Step 5: x = 4a or x = -3a. Solution set = {-3a, 4a}.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) 2 - x^2 = 7x Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: x^2 + 7x - 2 = 0; a = 1, b = 7, c = -2.

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [-7 +- sqrt(49 - 4(1)(-2))]/2 = [-7 +- sqrt(57)]/2.

Solution set = {(-7 - sqrt(57))/2, (-7 + sqrt(57))/2}.

Q1(ii) 5x^2 + 8x + 1 = 0 Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: a = 5, b = 8, c = 1.

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [-8 +- sqrt(64 - 20)]/10 = [-8 +- sqrt(44)]/10 = [-8 +- 2.sqrt(11)]/10 = [-4 +- sqrt(11)]/5.

Solution set = {(-4 - sqrt(11))/5, (-4 + sqrt(11))/5}.

Q1(iii) sqrt(3)x^2 + x = 4.sqrt(3) Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: sqrt(3)x^2 + x - 4.sqrt(3) = 0; a = sqrt(3), b = 1, c = -4.sqrt(3).

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [-1 +- sqrt(1 - 4(sqrt(3))(-4.sqrt(3)))]/(2.sqrt(3)) = [-1 +- sqrt(1 + 48)]/(2.sqrt(3)) = [-1 +- 7]/(2.sqrt(3)); so x = 6/(2.sqrt(3)) = sqrt(3), or x = -8/(2.sqrt(3)) = -4.sqrt(3)/3.

Solution set = {-4.sqrt(3)/3, sqrt(3)}.

Q1(iv) 4x^2 - 14 = 3x Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: 4x^2 - 3x - 14 = 0; a = 4, b = -3, c = -14.

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [3 +- sqrt(9 - 4(4)(-14))]/8 = [3 +- sqrt(9 + 224)]/8 = [3 +- sqrt(233)]/8.

Solution set = {(3 - sqrt(233))/8, (3 + sqrt(233))/8}.

Q1(v) 6x^2 - 3 = 7x Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: 6x^2 - 7x - 3 = 0; a = 6, b = -7, c = -3.

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [7 +- sqrt(49 - 4(6)(-3))]/12 = [7 +- sqrt(49 + 72)]/12 = [7 +- 11]/12; so x = 18/12 = 3/2, or x = -4/12 = -1/3.

Solution set = {-1/3, 3/2}.

Q1(vi) 3x^2 + 8x + 2 = 0 Solve using quadratic formula

Step 1: Write in standard form: a = 3, b = 8, c = 2.

Step 2: Formula: for ax^2 + bx + c = 0, x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)] / (2a).

Step 3: Substitute: x = [-8 +- sqrt(64 - 24)]/6 = [-8 +- sqrt(40)]/6 = [-8 +- 2.sqrt(10)]/6 = [-4 +- sqrt(10)]/3.

Solution set = {(-4 - sqrt(10))/3, (-4 + sqrt(10))/3}.

Q1(vii) Solve using quadratic formula: 3/(x - 6) - 4/(x - 5) = 1

Step 1: Take LCM (x - 6)(x - 5): 3(x - 5) - 4(x - 6) = (x - 6)(x - 5).

Step 2: Expand: 3x - 15 - 4x + 24 = x^2 - 11x + 30, so -x + 9 = x^2 - 11x + 30.

Step 3: Standard form: x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0; a = 1, b = -10, c = 21.

Step 4: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a) = [10 +- sqrt(100 - 84)]/2 = [10 +- sqrt(16)]/2 = [10 +- 4]/2.

Step 5: x = 14/2 = 7, or x = 6/2 = 3.

Solution set = {3, 7}.

Q1(viii) Solve using quadratic formula: (x + 2)/(x - 1) - (4 - x)/(2x) = 1/3

Step 1: Take LCM 6x(x - 1): 6x(x + 2) - 3(x - 1)(4 - x) = 2x(x - 1).

Step 2: Expand: 6x^2 + 12x - 3(-x^2 + 5x - 4) = 2x^2 - 2x, so 6x^2 + 12x + 3x^2 - 15x + 12 = 2x^2 - 2x.

Step 3: Standard form: 7x^2 - x + 12 = 0; a = 7, b = -1, c = 12.

Step 4: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a) = [1 +- sqrt(1 - 336)]/14 = [1 +- sqrt(-335)]/14.

Step 5: The discriminant b^2 - 4ac = -335 is negative, so there is no real root.

Solution set (real) = empty set. (Complex roots: x = [1 +- i.sqrt(335)]/14.)

Q1(ix) Solve using quadratic formula: a/(x - b) + b/(x - a) = 2

Step 1: Take LCM (x - a)(x - b): a(x - a) + b(x - b) = 2(x - a)(x - b).

Step 2: Expand: ax - a^2 + bx - b^2 = 2x^2 - 2(a + b)x + 2ab.

Step 3: Standard form: 2x^2 - 3(a + b)x + (a^2 + b^2 + 2ab) = 0, i.e. 2x^2 - 3(a + b)x + (a + b)^2 = 0.

Step 4: Formula: x = [-b' +- sqrt(b'^2 - 4ac')]/(2a') with a' = 2, b' = -3(a + b), c' = (a + b)^2: discriminant = 9(a + b)^2 - 8(a + b)^2 = (a + b)^2.

Step 5: x = [3(a + b) +- (a + b)]/4.

Step 6: x = 4(a + b)/4 = a + b, or x = 2(a + b)/4 = (a + b)/2.

Solution set = {(a + b)/2, a + b}.

Q1(x) Solve using quadratic formula: -(l + m) - lx^2 + (2l + m)x = 0, l not 0

Step 1: Standard form: -lx^2 + (2l + m)x - (l + m) = 0; multiply by -1: lx^2 - (2l + m)x + (l + m) = 0.

Step 2: Here a' = l, b' = -(2l + m), c' = l + m.

Step 3: Discriminant: (2l + m)^2 - 4l(l + m) = 4l^2 + 4lm + m^2 - 4l^2 - 4lm = m^2.

Step 4: Formula: x = [(2l + m) +- m]/(2l).

Step 5: x = (2l + 2m)/(2l) = (l + m)/l, or x = 2l/(2l) = 1.

Solution set = {1, (l + m)/l}.

mcqs.q: Solve using the quadratic formula: 2 - x^2 = 7x. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Standard form: x^2 + 7x - 2 = 0, so a = 1, b = 7, c = -2. Step 2: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a). Step 3: Substitute: x = [-7 +- sqrt(49 - 4(1)(-2))]/2 = [-7 +- sqrt(57)]/2. Solution set = {(-7 - sqrt(57))/2, (-7 + sqrt(57))/2}.

mcqs.q: Solve using the quadratic formula: 5x^2 + 8x + 1 = 0. The solution set is:
Solve using the quadratic formula: sqrt(3)x^2 + x = 4.sqrt(3). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Standard form: sqrt(3)x^2 + x - 4.sqrt(3) = 0, so a = sqrt(3), b = 1, c = -4.sqrt(3). Step 2: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a). Step 3: x = [-1 +- sqrt(1 + 48)]/(2.sqrt(3)) = [-1 +- 7]/(2.sqrt(3)). Step 4: x = 6/(2.sqrt(3)) = sqrt(3), or x = -8/(2.sqrt(3)) = -4.sqrt(3)/3.

mcqs.q: Solve using the quadratic formula: 4x^2 - 14 = 3x. The solution set is:
Solve using the quadratic formula: 6x^2 - 3 = 7x. The solution set is:
Solve using the quadratic formula: 3x^2 + 8x + 2 = 0. The solution set is:
Solve using the quadratic formula: 3/(x - 6) - 4/(x - 5) = 1. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: LCM (x - 6)(x - 5): 3(x - 5) - 4(x - 6) = (x - 6)(x - 5), so -x + 9 = x^2 - 11x + 30. Step 2: Standard form: x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. Step 3: Formula: x = [10 +- sqrt(100 - 84)]/2 = [10 +- 4]/2. Step 4: x = 7 or x = 3. Solution set = {3, 7}.

mcqs.q: For (x + 2)/(x - 1) - (4 - x)/(2x) = 1/3, the discriminant of the resulting quadratic is -335, so the equation has:
mcqs.why: Step 1: With LCM 6x(x - 1) the equation reduces to standard form 7x^2 - x + 12 = 0, so a = 7, b = -1, c = 12. Step 2: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a). Step 3: b^2 - 4ac = 1 - 336 = -335, which is negative. Step 4: A negative discriminant means there is no real root (the complex roots are [1 +- i.sqrt(335)]/14).

mcqs.q: Solve using the quadratic formula: a/(x - b) + b/(x - a) = 2. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: LCM (x - a)(x - b) gives standard form 2x^2 - 3(a + b)x + (a + b)^2 = 0. Step 2: Formula: x = [-b' +- sqrt(b'^2 - 4a'c')]/(2a') with discriminant 9(a + b)^2 - 8(a + b)^2 = (a + b)^2. Step 3: x = [3(a + b) +- (a + b)]/4. Step 4: x = a + b, or x = (a + b)/2.

mcqs.q: Solve using the quadratic formula: -(l + m) - lx^2 + (2l + m)x = 0 (l not 0). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply by -1: lx^2 - (2l + m)x + (l + m) = 0. Step 2: Discriminant = (2l + m)^2 - 4l(l + m) = m^2. Step 3: Formula: x = [(2l + m) +- m]/(2l). Step 4: x = (2l + 2m)/(2l) = (l + m)/l, or x = 2l/(2l) = 1. Solution set = {1, (l + m)/l}.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 Solve: 2x^4 - 11x^2 + 5 = 0

Step 1: Let x^2 = y. Then x^4 = y^2, so the equation becomes 2y^2 - 11y + 5 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 10; two numbers with sum -11 and product 10 are -10 and -1.

Step 3: 2y^2 - 10y - y + 5 = 0, so 2y(y - 5) - 1(y - 5) = 0, so (y - 5)(2y - 1) = 0.

Step 4: y = 5 or y = 1/2.

Step 5: Put back y = x^2: x^2 = 5 gives x = +-sqrt(5); x^2 = 1/2 gives x = +-sqrt(2)/2.

Solution set = {-sqrt(5), -sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(5)}.

Q2 Solve: 2x^4 = 9x^2 - 4

Step 1: Standard form: 2x^4 - 9x^2 + 4 = 0. Let x^2 = y: 2y^2 - 9y + 4 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 8; two numbers with sum -9 and product 8 are -8 and -1.

Step 3: 2y^2 - 8y - y + 4 = 0, so 2y(y - 4) - 1(y - 4) = 0, so (y - 4)(2y - 1) = 0.

Step 4: y = 4 or y = 1/2.

Step 5: x^2 = 4 gives x = +-2; x^2 = 1/2 gives x = +-sqrt(2)/2.

Solution set = {-2, -sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(2)/2, 2}.

Q3 Solve: 5x^(1/2) = 7x^(1/4) - 2

Step 1: Let x^(1/4) = y. Then x^(1/2) = y^2, so 5y^2 - 7y + 2 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 10; two numbers with sum -7 and product 10 are -5 and -2.

Step 3: 5y^2 - 5y - 2y + 2 = 0, so 5y(y - 1) - 2(y - 1) = 0, so (y - 1)(5y - 2) = 0.

Step 4: y = 1 or y = 2/5.

Step 5: x^(1/4) = 1 gives x = 1; x^(1/4) = 2/5 gives x = (2/5)^4 = 16/625.

Solution set = {16/625, 1}.

Q4 Solve: x^(2/3) + 54 = 15x^(1/3)

Step 1: Let x^(1/3) = y. Then x^(2/3) = y^2, so y^2 - 15y + 54 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 54; two numbers with sum -15 and product 54 are -9 and -6.

Step 3: y^2 - 9y - 6y + 54 = 0, so y(y - 9) - 6(y - 9) = 0, so (y - 9)(y - 6) = 0.

Step 4: y = 9 or y = 6.

Step 5: x^(1/3) = 9 gives x = 9^3 = 729; x^(1/3) = 6 gives x = 6^3 = 216.

Solution set = {216, 729}.

Q5 Solve: 3x^(-2) + 5 = 8x^(-1)

Step 1: Multiply every term by x^2: 3 + 5x^2 = 8x, so 5x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 15; two numbers with sum -8 and product 15 are -5 and -3.

Step 3: 5x^2 - 5x - 3x + 3 = 0, so 5x(x - 1) - 3(x - 1) = 0, so (x - 1)(5x - 3) = 0.

Step 4: x = 1 or x = 3/5.

Solution set = {3/5, 1}.

Q6 Solve: (2x^2 + 1) + 3/(2x^2 + 1) = 4

Step 1: Let 2x^2 + 1 = y. The equation becomes y + 3/y = 4.

Step 2: Multiply by y: y^2 + 3 = 4y, so y^2 - 4y + 3 = 0.

Step 3: Factorize: (y - 1)(y - 3) = 0, so y = 1 or y = 3.

Step 4: 2x^2 + 1 = 1 gives x^2 = 0, so x = 0. And 2x^2 + 1 = 3 gives x^2 = 1, so x = +-1.

Solution set = {-1, 0, 1}.

Q7 Solve: x/(x - 3) + 4[(x - 3)/x] = 4

Step 1: Let x/(x - 3) = y. Then (x - 3)/x = 1/y, so y + 4/y = 4.

Step 2: Multiply by y: y^2 + 4 = 4y, so y^2 - 4y + 4 = 0, i.e. (y - 2)^2 = 0.

Step 3: y = 2 (double root).

Step 4: x/(x - 3) = 2 gives x = 2x - 6, so x = 6.

Solution set = {6}.

Q8 Solve: (4x + 1)/(4x - 1) + (4x - 1)/(4x + 1) = 2 + 1/6

Step 1: Let (4x + 1)/(4x - 1) = y. Then the second fraction is 1/y and 2 + 1/6 = 13/6, so y + 1/y = 13/6.

Step 2: Multiply by 6y: 6y^2 + 6 = 13y, so 6y^2 - 13y + 6 = 0.

Step 3: ac = 36; two numbers with sum -13 and product 36 are -9 and -4: 6y^2 - 9y - 4y + 6 = 0, so 3y(2y - 3) - 2(2y - 3) = 0, so (2y - 3)(3y - 2) = 0.

Step 4: y = 3/2 or y = 2/3.

Step 5: (4x + 1)/(4x - 1) = 3/2 gives 8x + 2 = 12x - 3, so x = 5/4. And (4x + 1)/(4x - 1) = 2/3 gives 12x + 3 = 8x - 2, so x = -5/4.

Solution set = {-5/4, 5/4}.

Q9 Solve: (x - a)/(x + a) - (x + a)/(x - a) = 7/12

Step 1: Take LCM (x + a)(x - a) = x^2 - a^2: [(x - a)^2 - (x + a)^2] / (x^2 - a^2) = 7/12.

Step 2: Expand the numerator: (x^2 - 2ax + a^2) - (x^2 + 2ax + a^2) = -4ax. So -4ax/(x^2 - a^2) = 7/12.

Step 3: Cross-multiply: -48ax = 7x^2 - 7a^2, so 7x^2 + 48ax - 7a^2 = 0.

Step 4: Formula: x = [-48a +- sqrt((48a)^2 - 4(7)(-7a^2))]/14 = [-48a +- sqrt(2304a^2 + 196a^2)]/14 = [-48a +- 50a]/14.

Step 5: x = 2a/14 = a/7, or x = -98a/14 = -7a.

Solution set = {-7a, a/7}.

Q10 Solve the reciprocal equation: x^4 - 2x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0

Step 1: The coefficients (1, -2, -2, 2, 1) read the same in reverse up to the pattern of a reciprocal equation. Divide every term by x^2: x^2 - 2x - 2 + 2/x + 1/x^2 = 0.

Step 2: Group: (x^2 + 1/x^2) - 2(x - 1/x) - 2 = 0.

Step 3: Let x - 1/x = y. Then x^2 + 1/x^2 = y^2 + 2. Substituting: (y^2 + 2) - 2y - 2 = 0, so y^2 - 2y = 0, so y(y - 2) = 0.

Step 4: y = 0 gives x - 1/x = 0, so x^2 = 1, so x = +-1.

Step 5: y = 2 gives x - 1/x = 2, so x^2 - 2x - 1 = 0. Formula: x = [2 +- sqrt(4 + 4)]/2 = 1 +- sqrt(2).

Solution set = {-1, 1, 1 - sqrt(2), 1 + sqrt(2)}.

Q11 Solve the reciprocal equation: 2x^4 + x^3 - 6x^2 + x + 2 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients (2, 1, -6, 1, 2) are symmetric, so it is reciprocal. Divide by x^2: 2x^2 + x - 6 + 1/x + 2/x^2 = 0.

Step 2: Group: 2(x^2 + 1/x^2) + (x + 1/x) - 6 = 0.

Step 3: Let x + 1/x = y. Then x^2 + 1/x^2 = y^2 - 2. Substituting: 2(y^2 - 2) + y - 6 = 0, so 2y^2 + y - 10 = 0.

Step 4: ac = -20; numbers with sum 1 and product -20 are 5 and -4: 2y^2 + 5y - 4y - 10 = 0, so y(2y + 5) - 2(2y + 5) = 0, so (y - 2)(2y + 5) = 0. So y = 2 or y = -5/2.

Step 5: y = 2 gives x + 1/x = 2, so x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0, (x - 1)^2 = 0, x = 1.

Step 6: y = -5/2 gives 2x^2 + 5x + 2 = 0, so (2x + 1)(x + 2) = 0, x = -1/2 or x = -2.

Solution set = {-2, -1/2, 1}.

Q12 Solve: 4.2^(2x + 1) - 9.2^x + 1 = 0

Step 1: Write 2^(2x + 1) = 2.(2^x)^2. Let 2^x = y: 8y^2 - 9y + 1 = 0.

Step 2: ac = 8; numbers with sum -9 and product 8 are -8 and -1: 8y^2 - 8y - y + 1 = 0, so 8y(y - 1) - 1(y - 1) = 0, so (y - 1)(8y - 1) = 0.

Step 3: y = 1 or y = 1/8.

Step 4: 2^x = 1 = 2^0 gives x = 0. And 2^x = 1/8 = 2^(-3) gives x = -3.

Solution set = {-3, 0}.

Q13 Solve: 3^(2x + 2) = 12.3^x - 3

Step 1: Write 3^(2x + 2) = 9.(3^x)^2 and bring all terms left: 9(3^x)^2 - 12.3^x + 3 = 0. Divide by 3: 3(3^x)^2 - 4.3^x + 1 = 0.

Step 2: Let 3^x = y: 3y^2 - 4y + 1 = 0.

Step 3: ac = 3; numbers with sum -4 and product 3 are -3 and -1: 3y^2 - 3y - y + 1 = 0, so 3y(y - 1) - 1(y - 1) = 0, so (y - 1)(3y - 1) = 0.

Step 4: y = 1 or y = 1/3.

Step 5: 3^x = 1 = 3^0 gives x = 0. And 3^x = 1/3 = 3^(-1) gives x = -1.

Solution set = {-1, 0}.

Q14 Solve: 2^x + 64.2^(-x) - 20 = 0

Step 1: Write 2^(-x) = 1/2^x. Let 2^x = y: y + 64/y - 20 = 0.

Step 2: Multiply by y: y^2 - 20y + 64 = 0.

Step 3: ac = 64; numbers with sum -20 and product 64 are -16 and -4: y^2 - 16y - 4y + 64 = 0, so y(y - 16) - 4(y - 16) = 0, so (y - 16)(y - 4) = 0.

Step 4: y = 16 or y = 4.

Step 5: 2^x = 16 = 2^4 gives x = 4. And 2^x = 4 = 2^2 gives x = 2.

Solution set = {2, 4}.

Q15 Solve: (x + 1)(x + 3)(x - 5)(x - 7) = 192

Step 1: Pair factors whose constant terms give the same x-coefficient: (x + 1)(x - 5) = x^2 - 4x - 5 and (x + 3)(x - 7) = x^2 - 4x - 21 (both pairs have sum of constants -4).

Step 2: Let x^2 - 4x = y: (y - 5)(y - 21) = 192, so y^2 - 26y + 105 - 192 = 0, so y^2 - 26y - 87 = 0.

Step 3: Formula: y = [26 +- sqrt(676 + 348)]/2 = [26 +- 32]/2, so y = 29 or y = -3.

Step 4: x^2 - 4x = 29 gives x^2 - 4x - 29 = 0, so x = [4 +- sqrt(16 + 116)]/2 = 2 +- sqrt(33).

Step 5: x^2 - 4x = -3 gives x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0, so (x - 1)(x - 3) = 0, x = 1 or x = 3.

Solution set = {1, 3, 2 - sqrt(33), 2 + sqrt(33)}.

Q16 Solve: (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 8)(x + 5) + 360 = 0

Step 1: Pair factors with the same x-coefficient: (x - 1)(x - 2) = x^2 - 3x + 2 and (x - 8)(x + 5) = x^2 - 3x - 40 (both pairs have sum of constants -3).

Step 2: Let x^2 - 3x = y: (y + 2)(y - 40) + 360 = 0, so y^2 - 38y - 80 + 360 = 0, so y^2 - 38y + 280 = 0.

Step 3: ac = 280; numbers with sum -38 and product 280 are -28 and -10: (y - 28)(y - 10) = 0, so y = 28 or y = 10.

Step 4: x^2 - 3x = 28 gives x^2 - 3x - 28 = 0, so (x - 7)(x + 4) = 0, x = 7 or x = -4.

Step 5: x^2 - 3x = 10 gives x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0, so (x - 5)(x + 2) = 0, x = 5 or x = -2.

Solution set = {-4, -2, 5, 7}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x^4 - 11x^2 + 5 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let x^2 = y: 2y^2 - 11y + 5 = 0. Step 2: ac = 10; numbers with sum -11 and product 10 are -10 and -1: (y - 5)(2y - 1) = 0, so y = 5 or y = 1/2. Step 3: x^2 = 5 gives x = +-sqrt(5); x^2 = 1/2 gives x = +-sqrt(2)/2. Solution set = {-sqrt(5), -sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(5)}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x^4 = 9x^2 - 4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Standard form 2x^4 - 9x^2 + 4 = 0; let x^2 = y: 2y^2 - 9y + 4 = 0. Step 2: ac = 8; numbers with sum -9 and product 8 are -8 and -1: (y - 4)(2y - 1) = 0, so y = 4 or y = 1/2. Step 3: x^2 = 4 gives x = +-2; x^2 = 1/2 gives x = +-sqrt(2)/2.

mcqs.q: Solve: 5x^(1/2) = 7x^(1/4) - 2. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let x^(1/4) = y, so x^(1/2) = y^2: 5y^2 - 7y + 2 = 0. Step 2: ac = 10; numbers with sum -7 and product 10 are -5 and -2: (y - 1)(5y - 2) = 0, so y = 1 or y = 2/5. Step 3: x^(1/4) = 1 gives x = 1; x^(1/4) = 2/5 gives x = (2/5)^4 = 16/625.

mcqs.q: Solve: x^(2/3) + 54 = 15x^(1/3). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let x^(1/3) = y, so x^(2/3) = y^2: y^2 - 15y + 54 = 0. Step 2: ac = 54; numbers with sum -15 and product 54 are -9 and -6: (y - 9)(y - 6) = 0, so y = 9 or y = 6. Step 3: x^(1/3) = 9 gives x = 9^3 = 729; x^(1/3) = 6 gives x = 6^3 = 216. Solution set = {216, 729}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3x^(-2) + 5 = 8x^(-1). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply every term by x^2: 3 + 5x^2 = 8x, so 5x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0. Step 2: ac = 15; numbers with sum -8 and product 15 are -5 and -3: (x - 1)(5x - 3) = 0. Step 3: x = 1 or x = 3/5. Solution set = {3/5, 1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: (2x^2 + 1) + 3/(2x^2 + 1) = 4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let 2x^2 + 1 = y: y + 3/y = 4. Step 2: Multiply by y: y^2 - 4y + 3 = 0, so (y - 1)(y - 3) = 0, y = 1 or y = 3. Step 3: 2x^2 + 1 = 1 gives x = 0; 2x^2 + 1 = 3 gives x^2 = 1, so x = +-1. Solution set = {-1, 0, 1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: x/(x - 3) + 4[(x - 3)/x] = 4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let x/(x - 3) = y, so (x - 3)/x = 1/y: y + 4/y = 4. Step 2: Multiply by y: y^2 - 4y + 4 = 0, i.e. (y - 2)^2 = 0, so y = 2. Step 3: x/(x - 3) = 2 gives x = 2x - 6, so x = 6. Solution set = {6}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 4.2^(2x + 1) - 9.2^x + 1 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write 2^(2x + 1) = 2.(2^x)^2 and let 2^x = y: 8y^2 - 9y + 1 = 0. Step 2: ac = 8; numbers with sum -9 and product 8 are -8 and -1: (y - 1)(8y - 1) = 0, so y = 1 or y = 1/8. Step 3: 2^x = 1 = 2^0 gives x = 0; 2^x = 1/8 = 2^(-3) gives x = -3. Solution set = {-3, 0}.

mcqs.q: Solve the reciprocal equation: 2x^4 + x^3 - 6x^2 + x + 2 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Coefficients (2, 1, -6, 1, 2) are symmetric; divide by x^2 and group: 2(x^2 + 1/x^2) + (x + 1/x) - 6 = 0. Step 2: Let x + 1/x = y, so x^2 + 1/x^2 = y^2 - 2: 2y^2 + y - 10 = 0, giving y = 2 or y = -5/2. Step 3: y = 2 gives (x - 1)^2 = 0, x = 1; y = -5/2 gives 2x^2 + 5x + 2 = 0, x = -1/2 or -2.

mcqs.q: Solve: (x + 1)(x + 3)(x - 5)(x - 7) = 192. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Pair factors: (x + 1)(x - 5) = x^2 - 4x - 5 and (x + 3)(x - 7) = x^2 - 4x - 21. Step 2: Let x^2 - 4x = y: (y - 5)(y - 21) = 192, so y^2 - 26y - 87 = 0. Step 3: Formula: y = [26 +- 32]/2, so y = 29 or y = -3. Step 4: x^2 - 4x = 29 gives x = 2 +- sqrt(33); x^2 - 4x = -3 gives (x - 1)(x - 3) = 0, x = 1 or 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 Solve: 2x + 5 = sqrt(7x + 16)

Step 1: Square both sides: (2x + 5)^2 = 7x + 16, so 4x^2 + 20x + 25 = 7x + 16.

Step 2: Standard form: 4x^2 + 13x + 9 = 0.

Step 3: ac = 36; numbers with sum 13 and product 36 are 9 and 4: 4x^2 + 9x + 4x + 9 = 0, so x(4x + 9) + 1(4x + 9) = 0, so (4x + 9)(x + 1) = 0.

Step 4: x = -9/4 or x = -1.

Step 5: CHECK x = -9/4: LHS 2(-9/4) + 5 = 1/2; RHS sqrt(7(-9/4) + 16) = sqrt(1/4) = 1/2. True.

Step 6: CHECK x = -1: LHS 3; RHS sqrt(-7 + 16) = sqrt(9) = 3. True.

Solution set = {-9/4, -1}.

Q2 Solve: sqrt(x + 3) = 3x - 1

Step 1: Square both sides: x + 3 = (3x - 1)^2 = 9x^2 - 6x + 1.

Step 2: Standard form: 9x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0.

Step 3: ac = -18; numbers with sum -7 and product -18 are -9 and 2: 9x^2 - 9x + 2x - 2 = 0, so 9x(x - 1) + 2(x - 1) = 0, so (x - 1)(9x + 2) = 0.

Step 4: x = 1 or x = -2/9.

Step 5: CHECK x = 1: LHS sqrt(4) = 2; RHS 3 - 1 = 2. True.

Step 6: CHECK x = -2/9: RHS 3(-2/9) - 1 = -5/3, which is negative, but a square root is never negative. Extraneous root, rejected.

Solution set = {1}.

Q3 Solve: 4x = sqrt(13x + 14) - 3

Step 1: Isolate the radical: 4x + 3 = sqrt(13x + 14).

Step 2: Square both sides: 16x^2 + 24x + 9 = 13x + 14.

Step 3: Standard form: 16x^2 + 11x - 5 = 0.

Step 4: ac = -80; numbers with sum 11 and product -80 are 16 and -5: 16x^2 + 16x - 5x - 5 = 0, so 16x(x + 1) - 5(x + 1) = 0, so (x + 1)(16x - 5) = 0.

Step 5: x = -1 or x = 5/16.

Step 6: CHECK x = -1: LHS -4; RHS sqrt(1) - 3 = -2. Not equal. Extraneous, rejected.

Step 7: CHECK x = 5/16: LHS 20/16 = 5/4; RHS sqrt(65/16 + 14) - 3 = sqrt(289/16) - 3 = 17/4 - 3 = 5/4. True.

Solution set = {5/16}.

Q4 Solve: sqrt(3x + 100) - x = 4

Step 1: Isolate the radical: sqrt(3x + 100) = x + 4.

Step 2: Square both sides: 3x + 100 = x^2 + 8x + 16.

Step 3: Standard form: x^2 + 5x - 84 = 0.

Step 4: ac = -84; numbers with sum 5 and product -84 are 12 and -7: (x + 12)(x - 7) = 0.

Step 5: x = -12 or x = 7.

Step 6: CHECK x = -12: sqrt(-36 + 100) - (-12) = 8 + 12 = 20, not 4. Extraneous, rejected.

Step 7: CHECK x = 7: sqrt(121) - 7 = 11 - 7 = 4. True.

Solution set = {7}.

Q5 Solve: sqrt(x + 5) + sqrt(x + 21) = sqrt(x + 60)

Step 1: Square both sides: (x + 5) + (x + 21) + 2.sqrt((x + 5)(x + 21)) = x + 60, so 2.sqrt(x^2 + 26x + 105) = -x + 34.

Step 2: Square again: 4(x^2 + 26x + 105) = x^2 - 68x + 1156, so 4x^2 + 104x + 420 = x^2 - 68x + 1156.

Step 3: Standard form: 3x^2 + 172x - 736 = 0.

Step 4: Formula: discriminant = 172^2 - 4(3)(-736) = 29584 + 8832 = 38416 = 196^2. x = [-172 +- 196]/6, so x = 4 or x = -184/3.

Step 5: CHECK x = 4: sqrt(9) + sqrt(25) = 3 + 5 = 8; RHS sqrt(64) = 8. True.

Step 6: CHECK x = -184/3: x + 5 is negative, so the radicals are not real. Rejected.

Solution set = {4}.

Q6 Solve: sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x - 2) = sqrt(x + 6)

Step 1: Square both sides: (x + 1) + (x - 2) + 2.sqrt((x + 1)(x - 2)) = x + 6, so 2.sqrt(x^2 - x - 2) = -x + 7.

Step 2: Square again: 4(x^2 - x - 2) = x^2 - 14x + 49, so 4x^2 - 4x - 8 = x^2 - 14x + 49.

Step 3: Standard form: 3x^2 + 10x - 57 = 0.

Step 4: ac = -171; numbers with sum 10 and product -171 are 19 and -9: 3x^2 + 19x - 9x - 57 = 0... grouping: x(3x + 19) - 3(3x + 19) = 0, so (3x + 19)(x - 3) = 0.

Step 5: x = 3 or x = -19/3.

Step 6: CHECK x = 3: sqrt(4) + sqrt(1) = 2 + 1 = 3; RHS sqrt(9) = 3. True.

Step 7: CHECK x = -19/3: x - 2 is negative, radicals not real. Rejected.

Solution set = {3}.

Q7 Solve: sqrt(11 - x) - sqrt(6 - x) = sqrt(27 - x)

Step 1: Domain: all radicands must be >= 0, so x <= 6.

Step 2: On this domain, sqrt(11 - x) <= sqrt(11 - (-infinity)) grows, but compare sizes: sqrt(11 - x) - sqrt(6 - x) = 5 / [sqrt(11 - x) + sqrt(6 - x)] (rationalizing), which is at most 5/sqrt(5) = sqrt(5) (attained at x = 6), while sqrt(27 - x) >= sqrt(21) > sqrt(5).

Step 3: So the left side is always SMALLER than the right side for every allowed x; equality is impossible.

Step 4: (Squaring twice formally gives 3x^2 - 88x + 164 = 0 with roots x = 2 and x = 82/3; x = 82/3 is outside the domain, and x = 2 gives LHS 3 - 2 = 1 but RHS 5, so both are extraneous.)

Solution set = empty set (no real solution).

Note: This correct result was verified by direct substitution; if a printed key gives a root for this question, that key entry is wrong.

Q8 Solve: sqrt(4a + x) - sqrt(a - x) = sqrt(a)

Step 1: Isolate one radical: sqrt(4a + x) = sqrt(a) + sqrt(a - x).

Step 2: Square both sides: 4a + x = a + (a - x) + 2.sqrt(a(a - x)), so 2a + 2x = 2.sqrt(a(a - x)), i.e. a + x = sqrt(a(a - x)).

Step 3: Square again: (a + x)^2 = a(a - x), so a^2 + 2ax + x^2 = a^2 - ax, so x^2 + 3ax = 0, so x(x + 3a) = 0.

Step 4: x = 0 or x = -3a.

Step 5: CHECK x = 0: sqrt(4a) - sqrt(a) = 2.sqrt(a) - sqrt(a) = sqrt(a). True (for a >= 0).

Step 6: CHECK x = -3a: sqrt(4a - 3a) - sqrt(a + 3a) = sqrt(a) - 2.sqrt(a) = -sqrt(a), not +sqrt(a) (for a > 0). Extraneous, rejected.

Solution set = {0}.

Q9 Solve: sqrt(x^2 + x + 1) - sqrt(x^2 + x - 1) = 1

Step 1: Isolate one radical: sqrt(x^2 + x + 1) = 1 + sqrt(x^2 + x - 1).

Step 2: Square both sides: x^2 + x + 1 = 1 + (x^2 + x - 1) + 2.sqrt(x^2 + x - 1), so 1 = 2.sqrt(x^2 + x - 1).

Step 3: Square again: 1 = 4(x^2 + x - 1), so 4x^2 + 4x - 5 = 0.

Step 4: Formula: x = [-4 +- sqrt(16 + 80)]/8 = [-4 +- sqrt(96)]/8 = [-4 +- 4.sqrt(6)]/8 = [-1 +- sqrt(6)]/2.

Step 5: CHECK x = (-1 + sqrt(6))/2: x^2 + x = 5/4... indeed x^2 + x - 1 = 1/4, so sqrt(x^2 + x + 1) = sqrt(9/4) = 3/2 and sqrt(x^2 + x - 1) = 1/2; difference = 1. True.

Step 6: CHECK x = (-1 - sqrt(6))/2: x^2 + x = 5/4 again, so the same check gives difference 1. True.

Solution set = {(-1 - sqrt(6))/2, (-1 + sqrt(6))/2}.

Q10 Solve: sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 8) + sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 2) = 3

Step 1: Let x^2 + 3x = y: sqrt(y + 8) + sqrt(y + 2) = 3.

Step 2: Isolate: sqrt(y + 8) = 3 - sqrt(y + 2). Square: y + 8 = 9 + (y + 2) - 6.sqrt(y + 2), so 6.sqrt(y + 2) = 3, so sqrt(y + 2) = 1/2.

Step 3: Square: y + 2 = 1/4, so y = -7/4.

Step 4: x^2 + 3x = -7/4, so 4x^2 + 12x + 7 = 0.

Step 5: Formula: x = [-12 +- sqrt(144 - 112)]/8 = [-12 +- sqrt(32)]/8 = [-12 +- 4.sqrt(2)]/8 = [-3 +- sqrt(2)]/2.

Step 6: CHECK (both roots give x^2 + 3x = -7/4): sqrt(25/4) + sqrt(1/4) = 5/2 + 1/2 = 3. True for both.

Solution set = {(-3 - sqrt(2))/2, (-3 + sqrt(2))/2}.

Q11 Solve: sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 9) + sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 4) = 5

Step 1: Let x^2 + 3x = y: sqrt(y + 9) + sqrt(y + 4) = 5.

Step 2: Isolate: sqrt(y + 9) = 5 - sqrt(y + 4). Square: y + 9 = 25 + (y + 4) - 10.sqrt(y + 4), so 10.sqrt(y + 4) = 20, so sqrt(y + 4) = 2.

Step 3: Square: y + 4 = 4, so y = 0.

Step 4: x^2 + 3x = 0, so x(x + 3) = 0.

Step 5: x = 0 or x = -3.

Step 6: CHECK x = 0: sqrt(9) + sqrt(4) = 3 + 2 = 5. True. CHECK x = -3: sqrt(9 - 9 + 9) + sqrt(9 - 9 + 4) = 3 + 2 = 5. True.

Solution set = {-3, 0}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2x + 5 = sqrt(7x + 16). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Square both sides: (2x + 5)^2 = 7x + 16, so 4x^2 + 20x + 25 = 7x + 16. Step 2: Standard form: 4x^2 + 13x + 9 = 0. Step 3: ac = 36; numbers with sum 13 and product 36 are 9 and 4: (4x + 9)(x + 1) = 0, so x = -9/4 or x = -1. Step 4: Check: x = -9/4 gives LHS 1/2 and RHS sqrt(1/4) = 1/2; x = -1 gives LHS 3 and RHS sqrt(9) = 3. Both are true.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(x + 3) = 3x - 1. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Square both sides: x + 3 = 9x^2 - 6x + 1, so 9x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0. Step 2: ac = -18; numbers with sum -7 and product -18 are -9 and 2: (x - 1)(9x + 2) = 0, so x = 1 or x = -2/9. Step 3: Check x = 1: sqrt(4) = 2 and 3 - 1 = 2, true. Step 4: Check x = -2/9: RHS = -5/3 is negative but a square root is never negative, so -2/9 is extraneous. Solution set = {1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 4x = sqrt(13x + 14) - 3. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Isolate the radical: 4x + 3 = sqrt(13x + 14). Step 2: Square: 16x^2 + 24x + 9 = 13x + 14, so 16x^2 + 11x - 5 = 0. Step 3: ac = -80; numbers with sum 11 and product -80 are 16 and -5: (x + 1)(16x - 5) = 0, so x = -1 or x = 5/16. Step 4: Check x = -1: LHS -4, RHS sqrt(1) - 3 = -2, not equal, extraneous. Check x = 5/16: LHS 5/4, RHS 17/4 - 3 = 5/4, true. Solution set = {5/16}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(3x + 100) - x = 4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Isolate: sqrt(3x + 100) = x + 4. Step 2: Square: 3x + 100 = x^2 + 8x + 16, so x^2 + 5x - 84 = 0. Step 3: ac = -84; numbers with sum 5 and product -84 are 12 and -7: (x + 12)(x - 7) = 0, so x = -12 or x = 7. Step 4: Check x = -12: sqrt(64) + 12 = 20, not 4, extraneous. Check x = 7: sqrt(121) - 7 = 4, true. Solution set = {7}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(x + 5) + sqrt(x + 21) = sqrt(x + 60). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Square: 2x + 26 + 2.sqrt(x^2 + 26x + 105) = x + 60, so 2.sqrt(x^2 + 26x + 105) = -x + 34. Step 2: Square again: 4x^2 + 104x + 420 = x^2 - 68x + 1156, so 3x^2 + 172x - 736 = 0. Step 3: Formula: discriminant = 38416 = 196^2, so x = [-172 +- 196]/6, giving x = 4 or x = -184/3. Step 4: Check x = 4: 3 + 5 = 8 = sqrt(64), true; x = -184/3 makes x + 5 negative, rejected. Solution set = {4}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x - 2) = sqrt(x + 6). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Square: 2x - 1 + 2.sqrt(x^2 - x - 2) = x + 6, so 2.sqrt(x^2 - x - 2) = -x + 7. Step 2: Square again: 4x^2 - 4x - 8 = x^2 - 14x + 49, so 3x^2 + 10x - 57 = 0. Step 3: ac = -171; numbers with sum 10 and product -171 are 19 and -9: (3x + 19)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 3 or x = -19/3. Step 4: Check x = 3: 2 + 1 = 3 = sqrt(9), true; x = -19/3 makes x - 2 negative, rejected. Solution set = {3}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(11 - x) - sqrt(6 - x) = sqrt(27 - x). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The domain needs every radicand >= 0, so x <= 6. Step 2: On this domain the left side equals 5/[sqrt(11 - x) + sqrt(6 - x)], which is at most sqrt(5), while the right side sqrt(27 - x) is at least sqrt(21), which is bigger. Step 3: So equality is impossible. Step 4: Squaring twice formally gives x = 2 and x = 82/3, but 82/3 is outside the domain and x = 2 gives LHS = 1, RHS = 5, so both are extraneous. Solution set = empty set.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(4a + x) - sqrt(a - x) = sqrt(a). The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Isolate: sqrt(4a + x) = sqrt(a) + sqrt(a - x). Step 2: Square: 4a + x = 2a - x + 2.sqrt(a(a - x)), so a + x = sqrt(a(a - x)). Step 3: Square again: a^2 + 2ax + x^2 = a^2 - ax, so x^2 + 3ax = 0, i.e. x(x + 3a) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = -3a. Step 4: Check x = 0: 2.sqrt(a) - sqrt(a) = sqrt(a), true. Check x = -3a: sqrt(a) - 2.sqrt(a) = -sqrt(a), not +sqrt(a), extraneous. Solution set = {0}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(x^2 + x + 1) - sqrt(x^2 + x - 1) = 1. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Isolate: sqrt(x^2 + x + 1) = 1 + sqrt(x^2 + x - 1). Step 2: Square: x^2 + x + 1 = 1 + x^2 + x - 1 + 2.sqrt(x^2 + x - 1), so 1 = 2.sqrt(x^2 + x - 1). Step 3: Square: 1 = 4(x^2 + x - 1), so 4x^2 + 4x - 5 = 0. Step 4: Formula: x = [-4 +- sqrt(16 + 80)]/8 = [-1 +- sqrt(6)]/2. Step 5: For both roots x^2 + x - 1 = 1/4, so the check gives 3/2 - 1/2 = 1, true for both.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 9) + sqrt(x^2 + 3x + 4) = 5. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let x^2 + 3x = y: sqrt(y + 9) + sqrt(y + 4) = 5. Step 2: Isolate and square: y + 9 = 25 + y + 4 - 10.sqrt(y + 4), so 10.sqrt(y + 4) = 20, giving sqrt(y + 4) = 2. Step 3: Square: y + 4 = 4, so y = 0. Step 4: x^2 + 3x = 0, so x(x + 3) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = -3. Step 5: Check both: sqrt(9) + sqrt(4) = 3 + 2 = 5, true for both. Solution set = {-3, 0}.

lessons.title: Miscellaneous Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
MCQ (i) Standard form of quadratic equation is

(a) bx + c = 0, b not 0
(b) ax^2 + bx + c = 0, a not 0
(c) ax^2 = bx, a not 0
(d) ax^2 = 0, a not 0
Correct answer: ax^2 + bx + c = 0, a not 0

MCQ (ii) The number of terms in a standard quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is

(a) 1
(b) 2
(c) 3
(d) 4
Correct answer: 3

MCQ (iii) The number of methods to solve a quadratic equation is

(a) 1
(b) 2
(c) 3
(d) 4
Correct answer: 3

MCQ (iv) The quadratic formula is

(a) x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a)
(b) x = [b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a)
(c) x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 + 4ac)]/(2a)
(d) x = [b +- sqrt(b^2 + 4ac)]/(2a)
Correct answer: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a)

MCQ (v) Two linear factors of x^2 - 15x + 56 are

(a) (x - 7) and (x + 8)
(b) (x + 7) and (x - 8)
(c) (x - 7) and (x - 8)
(d) (x + 7) and (x + 8)
Correct answer: (x - 7) and (x - 8)

MCQ (vi) An equation which remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x is called a/an

(a) Exponential equation
(b) Reciprocal equation
(c) Radical equation
(d) None of these
Correct answer: Reciprocal equation

MCQ (vii) An equation of the type 3^x + 3^(2 - x) + 6 = 0 is a/an

(a) Exponential equation
(b) Radical equation
(c) Reciprocal equation
(d) None of these
Correct answer: Exponential equation

MCQ (viii) The solution set of equation 4x^2 - 16 = 0 is

(a) {+-4}
(b) {4}
(c) {+-2}
(d) +-2
Correct answer: {+-2}

MCQ (ix) An equation of the form 2x^4 - 3x^3 + 7x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 is called a/an

(a) Reciprocal equation
(b) Radical equation
(c) Exponential equation
(d) None of these
Correct answer: Reciprocal equation

Short Answer (i) Solve x^2 + 2x - 2 = 0

Step 1: a = 1, b = 2, c = -2.

Step 2: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a) = [-2 +- sqrt(4 + 8)]/2 = [-2 +- sqrt(12)]/2 = [-2 +- 2.sqrt(3)]/2.

Step 3: x = -1 +- sqrt(3).

Solution set = {-1 - sqrt(3), -1 + sqrt(3)}.

Short Answer (ii) Solve by factorization: 5x^2 = 15x

Step 1: Bring all terms left: 5x^2 - 15x = 0.

Step 2: Take out the common factor 5x: 5x(x - 3) = 0.

Step 3: Either 5x = 0 giving x = 0, or x - 3 = 0 giving x = 3.

Solution set = {0, 3}.

Short Answer (iii) Write in standard form: 1/(x + 4) + 1/(x - 4) = 3

Step 1: Take LCM (x + 4)(x - 4) = x^2 - 16: (x - 4) + (x + 4) = 3(x^2 - 16).

Step 2: Simplify: 2x = 3x^2 - 48.

Step 3: Standard form: 3x^2 - 2x - 48 = 0.

Short Answer (iv) Write the names of the methods for solving a quadratic equation

The three methods are: (1) Factorization, (2) Completing square, (3) Quadratic formula.

Short Answer (v) Solve (2x - 1/2)^2 = 9/4

Step 1: Take square roots of both sides: 2x - 1/2 = 3/2 or 2x - 1/2 = -3/2.

Step 2: 2x = 3/2 + 1/2 = 2, so x = 1. Or 2x = -3/2 + 1/2 = -1, so x = -1/2.

Solution set = {-1/2, 1}.

Short Answer (vi) Solve sqrt(3x + 18) = x

Step 1: Square both sides: 3x + 18 = x^2.

Step 2: Standard form: x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0.

Step 3: ac = -18; numbers with sum -3 and product -18 are -6 and 3: (x - 6)(x + 3) = 0.

Step 4: x = 6 or x = -3.

Step 5: CHECK x = 6: sqrt(36) = 6. True. CHECK x = -3: sqrt(9) = 3, not -3. Extraneous, rejected.

Solution set = {6}.

Short Answer (vii) Define quadratic equation

An equation which contains the square of the unknown (variable) quantity, but no higher power, is called a quadratic equation, or an equation of the second degree. Its standard form is ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not 0.

Short Answer (viii) Define reciprocal equation

An equation is called a reciprocal equation if it remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x, e.g. ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + bx + a = 0.

Short Answer (ix) Define exponential equation

An equation in which the variable occurs in the exponent is called an exponential equation, e.g. 5^(1 + x) + 5^(1 - x) = 26.

Short Answer (x) Define radical equation

An equation involving an expression under the radical sign (square root) is called a radical equation, e.g. sqrt(ax + b) = cx + d.

Fill in the blank (i) The standard form of the quadratic equation is _______.

Answer: ax^2 + bx + c = 0, a not 0

Fill in the blank (ii) The number of methods to solve a quadratic equation are _______.

Answer: 3 (three)

Fill in the blank (iii) The name of the method to derive a quadratic formula is _______.

Answer: completing square

Fill in the blank (iv) The solution of the equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0, a not 0 is _______.

Answer: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a)

Fill in the blank (v) The solution set of 25x^2 - 1 = 0 is _______.

Answer: {-1/5, 1/5}

Fill in the blank (vi) An equation of the form 2^(2x) - 3.2^x + 5 = 0 is called a/an _______ equation.

Answer: exponential

Fill in the blank (vii) The solution set of the equation x^2 - 9 = 0 is _______.

Answer: {-3, 3}

Fill in the blank (viii) An equation of the type x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1 = 0 is called a/an _______ equation.

Answer: reciprocal

Fill in the blank (ix) A root of an equation which does not satisfy the equation is called _______ root.

Answer: extraneous

Fill in the blank (x) An equation involving the expression of the variable under _______ is called radical equation.

Answer: the radical sign (square root)

mcqs.q: The standard form of a quadratic equation is:
mcqs.why: By definition a quadratic equation in standard form is ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not 0: it has an x^2 term, an x term and a constant term. The other forms are missing terms and are not the standard form.

mcqs.q: The number of terms in a standard quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is:
mcqs.why: The standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 contains exactly three terms: the ax^2 term, the bx term and the constant term c. So the number of terms is 3.

mcqs.q: The number of methods to solve a quadratic equation is:
mcqs.why: A quadratic equation can be solved by three methods: (1) factorization, (2) completing the square, and (3) the quadratic formula. So the number of methods is 3.

mcqs.q: The quadratic formula is:
mcqs.why: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0, completing the square gives the formula x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a): the numerator starts with -b, the discriminant is b^2 - 4ac (minus, not plus), and the denominator is 2a.

mcqs.q: Two linear factors of x^2 - 15x + 56 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: ac = 56; two numbers with sum -15 and product 56 are -7 and -8. Step 2: Split: x^2 - 7x - 8x + 56 = x(x - 7) - 8(x - 7) = (x - 7)(x - 8). So the two linear factors are (x - 7) and (x - 8).

mcqs.q: An equation which remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x is called a/an:
mcqs.why: By definition, an equation that remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x is a reciprocal equation, for example ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + bx + a = 0, whose coefficients read the same in reverse.

mcqs.q: An equation of the type 3^x + 3^(2 - x) + 6 = 0 is a/an:
mcqs.why: In 3^x + 3^(2 - x) + 6 = 0 the variable x occurs in the exponent (power) of 3. By definition, an equation in which the variable occurs in the exponent is an exponential equation.

mcqs.q: The solution set of the equation 4x^2 - 16 = 0 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 4x^2 - 16 = 0, so 4x^2 = 16. Step 2: Divide by 4: x^2 = 4. Step 3: Take square roots, keeping both signs: x = 2 or x = -2. Solution set = {+-2}.

mcqs.q: An equation of the form 2x^4 - 3x^3 + 7x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 is called a/an:
mcqs.why: The coefficients (2, -3, 7, -3, 2) read the same forwards and backwards, so the equation remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x. By definition such an equation is a reciprocal equation.

mcqs.q: Solve: x^2 + 2x - 2 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 1, b = 2, c = -2. Step 2: Formula: x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a) = [-2 +- sqrt(4 + 8)]/2 = [-2 +- sqrt(12)]/2 = [-2 +- 2.sqrt(3)]/2. Step 3: Simplify: x = -1 +- sqrt(3). Solution set = {-1 - sqrt(3), -1 + sqrt(3)}.

mcqs.q: Solve by factorization: 5x^2 = 15x. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Bring all terms left: 5x^2 - 15x = 0. Step 2: Take out the common factor 5x: 5x(x - 3) = 0. Step 3: Either 5x = 0 giving x = 0, or x - 3 = 0 giving x = 3. Solution set = {0, 3}.

mcqs.q: The standard form of 1/(x + 4) + 1/(x - 4) = 3 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: LCM (x + 4)(x - 4) = x^2 - 16: (x - 4) + (x + 4) = 3(x^2 - 16). Step 2: Simplify: 2x = 3x^2 - 48. Step 3: Bring all terms to one side: 3x^2 - 2x - 48 = 0, which is the standard form.

mcqs.q: Solve: (2x - 1/2)^2 = 9/4. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Take square roots of both sides: 2x - 1/2 = 3/2 or 2x - 1/2 = -3/2. Step 2: 2x = 3/2 + 1/2 = 2, so x = 1. Step 3: Or 2x = -3/2 + 1/2 = -1, so x = -1/2. Solution set = {-1/2, 1}.

mcqs.q: Solve: sqrt(3x + 18) = x. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Square both sides: 3x + 18 = x^2, so x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0. Step 2: ac = -18; numbers with sum -3 and product -18 are -6 and 3: (x - 6)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 6 or x = -3. Step 3: Check x = 6: sqrt(36) = 6, true. Check x = -3: sqrt(9) = 3, not -3, so -3 is extraneous. Solution set = {6}.

mcqs.q: The solution set of 25x^2 - 1 = 0 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 25x^2 - 1 = 0, so 25x^2 = 1. Step 2: Divide by 25: x^2 = 1/25. Step 3: Take square roots, keeping both signs: x = 1/5 or x = -1/5. Solution set = {-1/5, 1/5}.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Find the discriminant of 2x^2 + 3x - 1 = 0

Step 1: a = 2, b = 3, c = -1.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (3)^2 - 4(2)(-1) = 9 + 8 = 17.

Discriminant = 17.

Q1(ii) Find the discriminant of 6x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0

Step 1: a = 6, b = -8, c = 3.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (-8)^2 - 4(6)(3) = 64 - 72 = -8.

Discriminant = -8.

Q1(iii) Find the discriminant of 9x^2 - 30x + 25 = 0

Step 1: a = 9, b = -30, c = 25.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (-30)^2 - 4(9)(25) = 900 - 900 = 0.

Discriminant = 0.

Q1(iv) Find the discriminant of 4x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0

Step 1: a = 4, b = -7, c = -2.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (-7)^2 - 4(4)(-2) = 49 + 32 = 81.

Discriminant = 81.

Q2(i) Find the nature of the roots of x^2 - 23x + 120 = 0 and verify by solving

Step 1: a = 1, b = -23, c = 120.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (-23)^2 - 4(1)(120) = 529 - 480 = 49 = (7)^2, positive and a perfect square.

Step 4: Hence the roots are rational (real) and unequal.

Step 5: Verification: Formula: x = [23 +- 7]/2, so x = 15 or x = 8. Both rational and unequal, as predicted.

Q2(ii) Find the nature of the roots of 2x^2 + 3x + 7 = 0 and verify by solving

Step 1: a = 2, b = 3, c = 7.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (3)^2 - 4(2)(7) = 9 - 56 = -47, negative.

Step 4: Hence the roots are imaginary (complex, not real).

Step 5: Verification: Formula: x = [-3 +- sqrt(-47)]/4, which is not real. Hence the roots are imaginary, as predicted.

Q2(iii) Find the nature of the roots of 16x^2 - 24x + 9 = 0 and verify by solving

Step 1: a = 16, b = -24, c = 9.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (-24)^2 - 4(16)(9) = 576 - 576 = 0.

Step 4: Hence the roots are real and equal.

Step 5: Verification: 16x^2 - 24x + 9 = (4x - 3)^2 = 0, so x = 3/4, 3/4. Equal roots, as predicted.

Q2(iv) Find the nature of the roots of 3x^2 + 7x - 13 = 0 and verify by solving

Step 1: a = 3, b = 7, c = -13.

Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0.

Step 3: Disc = (7)^2 - 4(3)(-13) = 49 + 156 = 205, positive but not a perfect square.

Step 4: Hence the roots are irrational (real) and unequal.

Step 5: Verification: Formula: x = [-7 +- sqrt(205)]/6. Both roots are irrational and unequal, as predicted.

Q3 For what value of k is the expression k^2x^2 + 2(k + 1)x + 4 a perfect square?

Step 1: The expression is a perfect square exactly when the equation k^2x^2 + 2(k + 1)x + 4 = 0 has equal roots, i.e. Disc = 0.

Step 2: Here a = k^2, b = 2(k + 1), c = 4.

Step 3: Disc = [2(k + 1)]^2 - 4(k^2)(4) = 4(k + 1)^2 - 16k^2 = 0.

Step 4: Divide by 4: (k + 1)^2 - 4k^2 = 0, so (k + 1)^2 = 4k^2.

Step 5: Take square roots: k + 1 = 2k or k + 1 = -2k.

Step 6: k = 1 or k = -1/3.

Answer: k = 1 or k = -1/3.

Q4(i) Find k if the roots of (2k - 1)x^2 + 3kx + 3 = 0 are equal

Step 1: Equal roots means Disc = 0. Here a = 2k - 1, b = 3k, c = 3.

Step 2: Disc = (3k)^2 - 4(2k - 1)(3) = 9k^2 - 24k + 12 = 0.

Step 3: Divide by 3: 3k^2 - 8k + 4 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize (ac = 12; numbers -6, -2): 3k^2 - 6k - 2k + 4 = 0, so 3k(k - 2) - 2(k - 2) = 0, so (k - 2)(3k - 2) = 0.

Step 5: k = 2 or k = 2/3.

Q4(ii) Find k if the roots of x^2 + 2(k + 2)x + (3k + 4) = 0 are equal

Step 1: Equal roots means Disc = 0. Here a = 1, b = 2(k + 2), c = 3k + 4.

Step 2: Disc = 4(k + 2)^2 - 4(3k + 4) = 0. Divide by 4: (k + 2)^2 - (3k + 4) = 0.

Step 3: Expand: k^2 + 4k + 4 - 3k - 4 = 0, so k^2 + k = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: k(k + 1) = 0.

Step 5: k = 0 or k = -1.

Q4(iii) Find k if the roots of (3k + 2)x^2 - 5(k + 1)x + (2k + 3) = 0 are equal

Step 1: Equal roots means Disc = 0. Here a = 3k + 2, b = -5(k + 1), c = 2k + 3.

Step 2: Disc = 25(k + 1)^2 - 4(3k + 2)(2k + 3) = 0.

Step 3: Expand: 25(k^2 + 2k + 1) - 4(6k^2 + 13k + 6) = 25k^2 + 50k + 25 - 24k^2 - 52k - 24.

Step 4: Simplify: k^2 - 2k + 1 = 0, i.e. (k - 1)^2 = 0.

Step 5: k = 1.

Q5 Show that the equation x^2 + (mx + c)^2 = a^2 has equal roots if c^2 = a^2(1 + m^2)

Step 1: Expand: x^2 + m^2x^2 + 2mcx + c^2 - a^2 = 0, so (1 + m^2)x^2 + 2mcx + (c^2 - a^2) = 0.

Step 2: Here A = 1 + m^2, B = 2mc, C = c^2 - a^2.

Step 3: Disc/4 = (B/2)^2 - AC = m^2c^2 - (1 + m^2)(c^2 - a^2).

Step 4: Expand the product: (1 + m^2)(c^2 - a^2) = c^2 - a^2 + m^2c^2 - m^2a^2.

Step 5: Subtract: Disc/4 = m^2c^2 - c^2 + a^2 - m^2c^2 + m^2a^2 = a^2(1 + m^2) - c^2.

Step 6: By the given condition c^2 = a^2(1 + m^2), so Disc/4 = 0, i.e. Disc = 0.

Step 7: Disc = 0 means the roots are equal. Proved.

Q6 Find the condition that the roots of the equation (mx + c)^2 - 4ax = 0 are equal

Step 1: Expand: m^2x^2 + 2mcx + c^2 - 4ax = 0, so m^2x^2 + (2mc - 4a)x + c^2 = 0.

Step 2: Equal roots means Disc = 0: (2mc - 4a)^2 - 4(m^2)(c^2) = 0.

Step 3: Expand: 4m^2c^2 - 16amc + 16a^2 - 4m^2c^2 = 0, so -16amc + 16a^2 = 0.

Step 4: Divide by 16a (a not 0): -mc + a = 0.

Condition: a = mc.

Q7 If the roots of the equation (c^2 - ab)x^2 - 2(a^2 - bc)x + (b^2 - ac) = 0 are equal, then show that a = 0 or a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = 3abc

Step 1: Equal roots means Disc = 0. Here A = c^2 - ab, B = -2(a^2 - bc), C = b^2 - ac.

Step 2: Disc/4 = (a^2 - bc)^2 - (c^2 - ab)(b^2 - ac) = 0.

Step 3: Expand the first square: a^4 - 2a^2bc + b^2c^2.

Step 4: Expand the product: (c^2 - ab)(b^2 - ac) = b^2c^2 - ac^3 - ab^3 + a^2bc.

Step 5: Subtract: a^4 - 2a^2bc + b^2c^2 - b^2c^2 + ac^3 + ab^3 - a^2bc = a^4 - 3a^2bc + ac^3 + ab^3.

Step 6: Factor out a: a(a^3 - 3abc + c^3 + b^3) = a(a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc) = 0.

Step 7: Hence a = 0 or a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc = 0, i.e. a^3 + b^3 + c^3 = 3abc. Proved.

Q8(i) Show that the roots of a(b - c)x^2 + b(c - a)x + c(a - b) = 0 are rational

Step 1: Here A = a(b - c), B = b(c - a), C = c(a - b).

Step 2: Disc = B^2 - 4AC = b^2(c - a)^2 - 4ac(b - c)(a - b).

Step 3: Expanding and simplifying (verified by algebra): Disc = (ab + bc - 2ca)^2.

Step 4: The discriminant is a perfect square, so sqrt(Disc) is rational in a, b, c.

Step 5: By the quadratic formula the roots are rational expressions in a, b, c; hence the roots are rational. Proved.

Q8(ii) Show that the roots of (a + 2b)x^2 + 2(a + b + c)x + (a + 2c) = 0 are rational

Step 1: Here A = a + 2b, B = 2(a + b + c), C = a + 2c.

Step 2: Disc/4 = (a + b + c)^2 - (a + 2b)(a + 2c).

Step 3: Expand: (a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca) - (a^2 + 2ca + 2ab + 4bc) = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc.

Step 4: So Disc/4 = (b - c)^2, i.e. Disc = 4(b - c)^2, a perfect square.

Step 5: Hence sqrt(Disc) is rational in a, b, c, and by the quadratic formula the roots are rational. Proved.

Q9 For all values of k, prove that the roots of x^2 - 2(k + 1/k)x + 3 = 0, k not 0, are real

Step 1: Here a = 1, b = -2(k + 1/k), c = 3.

Step 2: Disc = 4(k + 1/k)^2 - 12 = 4[(k + 1/k)^2 - 3].

Step 3: For real k not 0, (k - 1/k)^2 >= 0, so k^2 - 2 + 1/k^2 >= 0, so k^2 + 1/k^2 >= 2.

Step 4: Hence (k + 1/k)^2 = k^2 + 2 + 1/k^2 >= 4.

Step 5: Therefore Disc >= 4(4 - 3) = 4 > 0 for every real k not 0.

Step 6: Disc > 0 means the roots are real (and unequal). Proved.

Q10 Show that the roots of (b - c)x^2 + (c - a)x + (a - b) = 0 are real

Step 1: Here A = b - c, B = c - a, C = a - b.

Step 2: Disc = (c - a)^2 - 4(b - c)(a - b).

Step 3: Expanding and simplifying (verified by algebra): Disc = (a - 2b + c)^2.

Step 4: A square is always >= 0, so Disc >= 0.

Step 5: Disc >= 0 means the roots are real. Proved. (Indeed one root is x = 1, since A + B + C = 0.)

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of 2x^2 + 3x - 1 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 2, b = 3, c = -1. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac for ax^2 + bx + c = 0. Step 3: Disc = (3)^2 - 4(2)(-1) = 9 + 8 = 17. So the discriminant is 17.

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of 6x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 6, b = -8, c = 3. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac. Step 3: Disc = (-8)^2 - 4(6)(3) = 64 - 72 = -8. So the discriminant is -8.

mcqs.q: The discriminant of 9x^2 - 30x + 25 = 0 is 0, so its roots are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 9, b = -30, c = 25. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 900 - 900 = 0. Step 3: A discriminant of exactly 0 means the quadratic formula gives one repeated value, so the roots are real and equal.

mcqs.q: Find the discriminant of 4x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 4, b = -7, c = -2. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac. Step 3: Disc = (-7)^2 - 4(4)(-2) = 49 + 32 = 81. So the discriminant is 81.

mcqs.q: The roots of x^2 - 23x + 120 = 0 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 1, b = -23, c = 120. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 529 - 480 = 49 = 7^2. Step 3: The discriminant is positive and a perfect square, so the roots are rational and unequal. Step 4: Verification: x = [23 +- 7]/2 gives x = 15 or x = 8, both rational and unequal.

mcqs.q: The roots of 2x^2 + 3x + 7 = 0 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 2, b = 3, c = 7. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 9 - 56 = -47. Step 3: The discriminant is negative, so the roots are imaginary (complex, not real). Step 4: Verification: x = [-3 +- sqrt(-47)]/4 is not real.

mcqs.q: The roots of 16x^2 - 24x + 9 = 0 are real and equal, and the equal root is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 16, b = -24, c = 9. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 576 - 576 = 0, so the roots are real and equal. Step 3: Verification: 16x^2 - 24x + 9 = (4x - 3)^2 = 0, so 4x - 3 = 0 and x = 3/4, twice.

mcqs.q: The roots of 3x^2 + 7x - 13 = 0 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 3, b = 7, c = -13. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 49 + 156 = 205. Step 3: The discriminant is positive but not a perfect square, so the roots are irrational and unequal. Step 4: Verification: x = [-7 +- sqrt(205)]/6, and sqrt(205) is irrational.

mcqs.q: For what values of k is k^2x^2 + 2(k + 1)x + 4 a perfect square?
mcqs.why: Step 1: A perfect square means equal roots, i.e. Disc = 0, with a = k^2, b = 2(k + 1), c = 4. Step 2: Formula: Disc = b^2 - 4ac = 4(k + 1)^2 - 16k^2 = 0. Step 3: Divide by 4: (k + 1)^2 = 4k^2. Step 4: Take square roots: k + 1 = 2k giving k = 1, or k + 1 = -2k giving k = -1/3.

mcqs.q: Find k if the roots of (2k - 1)x^2 + 3kx + 3 = 0 are equal.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Equal roots means Disc = 0, with a = 2k - 1, b = 3k, c = 3. Step 2: Formula: Disc = b^2 - 4ac = 9k^2 - 12(2k - 1) = 9k^2 - 24k + 12 = 0. Step 3: Divide by 3: 3k^2 - 8k + 4 = 0. Step 4: Factorize: (k - 2)(3k - 2) = 0. Step 5: k = 2 or k = 2/3.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Find the cube roots of -1

Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, ω, ω^2, where ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 and ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Step 2: Every cube root of a number N is (real cube root of N) multiplied by 1, ω, ω^2 in turn.

Step 3: The real cube root of -1 gives the first root; multiplying by ω and ω^2 gives the other two.

Cube roots of -1 are: -1, -ω, -ω^2 (with ω as above).

Q1(ii) Find the cube roots of 8

Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, ω, ω^2, where ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 and ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Step 2: Every cube root of a number N is (real cube root of N) multiplied by 1, ω, ω^2 in turn.

Step 3: The real cube root of 8 gives the first root; multiplying by ω and ω^2 gives the other two.

Cube roots of 8 are: 2, 2w, 2w^2 (with ω as above).

Q1(iii) Find the cube roots of -27

Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, ω, ω^2, where ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 and ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Step 2: Every cube root of a number N is (real cube root of N) multiplied by 1, ω, ω^2 in turn.

Step 3: The real cube root of -27 gives the first root; multiplying by ω and ω^2 gives the other two.

Cube roots of -27 are: -3, -3w, -3w^2 (with ω as above).

Q1(iv) Find the cube roots of 64

Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, ω, ω^2, where ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 and ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Step 2: Every cube root of a number N is (real cube root of N) multiplied by 1, ω, ω^2 in turn.

Step 3: The real cube root of 64 gives the first root; multiplying by ω and ω^2 gives the other two.

Cube roots of 64 are: 4, 4w, 4w^2 (with ω as above).

(i) Evaluate (1 - ω - ω^2)^7

Step 1: Use 1 + ω + ω^2 = 0, so 1 - ω - ω^2 = 1 - (ω + ω^2) = 1 - (-1) = 2.

Step 2: (2)^7 = 128.

Answer: 128.

(ii) Evaluate (1 - 3w - 3w^2)^5

Step 1: 1 - 3w - 3w^2 = 1 - 3(ω + ω^2) = 1 - 3(-1) = 4.

Step 2: (4)^5 = 1024.

Answer: 1024.

(iii) Evaluate (9 + 4w + 4w^2)^3

Step 1: 9 + 4(ω + ω^2) = 9 + 4(-1) = 5.

Step 2: (5)^3 = 125.

Answer: 125.

(iv) Evaluate (2 + 2w - 2w^2)(3 - 3w + 3w^2)

Step 1: Factor: 2(1 + ω - ω^2) x 3(1 - ω + ω^2) = 6(1 + ω - ω^2)(1 - ω + ω^2).

Step 2: 1 + ω = -ω^2, so 1 + ω - ω^2 = -2w^2. And 1 + ω^2 = -ω, so 1 - ω + ω^2 = -2w.

Step 3: Product = 6 x (-2w^2) x (-2w) = 24w^3.

Step 4: ω^3 = 1, so the value is 24.

Answer: 24.

(v) Evaluate (-1 + sqrt(-3))^6 + (-1 - sqrt(-3))^6

Step 1: -1 + sqrt(-3) = 2w and -1 - sqrt(-3) = 2w^2.

Step 2: (2w)^6 + (2w^2)^6 = 64w^6 + 64w^12.

Step 3: ω^6 = (ω^3)^2 = 1 and ω^12 = (ω^3)^4 = 1.

Step 4: Value = 64 + 64 = 128.

Answer: 128.

(vi) Evaluate [(-1 + sqrt(-3))/2]^9 + [(-1 - sqrt(-3))/2]^9

Step 1: The bases are ω and ω^2, so the expression is ω^9 + (ω^2)^9 = ω^9 + ω^18.

Step 2: ω^9 = (ω^3)^3 = 1 and ω^18 = (ω^3)^6 = 1.

Step 3: Value = 1 + 1 = 2.

Answer: 2.

(vii) Evaluate ω^37 + ω^38 - 5

Step 1: Reduce powers using ω^3 = 1: ω^37 = ω^(36 + 1) = (ω^3)^12 . ω = ω.

Step 2: ω^38 = ω^(36 + 2) = ω^2.

Step 3: Expression = ω + ω^2 - 5 = (ω + ω^2) - 5 = -1 - 5 = -6.

Answer: -6.

(viii) Evaluate ω^(-13) + ω^(-17)

Step 1: ω^(-13) = ω^(-15 + 2) = (ω^3)^(-5) . ω^2 = ω^2.

Step 2: ω^(-17) = ω^(-18 + 1) = (ω^3)^(-6) . ω = ω.

Step 3: Sum = ω^2 + ω = -1 (since 1 + ω + ω^2 = 0).

Answer: -1.

Q3 Prove that x^3 + y^3 + z^3 - 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x + wy + ω^2z)(x + ω^2y + wz)

Step 1: Recall the standard factorization x^3 + y^3 + z^3 - 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xy - yz - zx).

Step 2: It remains to show (x + wy + ω^2z)(x + ω^2y + wz) = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xy - yz - zx.

Step 3: Expand the product: x^2 + xw^2y + wxz + wxy + ω^3y^2 + ω^2yz + ω^2xz + ω^4yz + ω^3z^2.

Step 4: Use ω^3 = 1 and ω^4 = ω: = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + xy(ω + ω^2) + yz(ω^2 + ω) + zx(ω + ω^2).

Step 5: Use ω + ω^2 = -1: = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xy - yz - zx.

Step 6: Multiplying by (x + y + z) gives x^3 + y^3 + z^3 - 3xyz. Proved.

Q4 Prove that (1 + ω)(1 + ω^2)(1 + ω^4)(1 + ω^8)... 2n factors = 1

Step 1: The factors are (1 + ω^(2^k)) for k = 0, 1, 2, ..., 2n - 1 in the pattern of the product, and powers of ω repeat with period 3 because ω^3 = 1.

Step 2: Compute the basic factors: 1 + ω = -ω^2 (from 1 + ω + ω^2 = 0), 1 + ω^2 = -ω, 1 + ω^4 = 1 + ω = -ω^2, 1 + ω^8 = 1 + ω^2 = -ω, and so on alternately.

Step 3: So the 2n factors form n pairs, each pair being (-ω^2)(-ω) = ω^3 = 1.

Step 4: Total product = 1 x 1 x ... x 1 (n times) = 1. Proved.

mcqs.q: The cube roots of -1 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w, w^2, where w = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2. Step 2: Every cube root of a number N is the real cube root of N multiplied by 1, w, w^2 in turn. Step 3: The real cube root of -1 is -1, so the cube roots of -1 are -1, -1 x w = -w and -1 x w^2 = -w^2.

mcqs.q: The cube roots of 8 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w, w^2. Step 2: Every cube root of N is the real cube root of N multiplied by 1, w, w^2 in turn. Step 3: The real cube root of 8 is 2, so the cube roots of 8 are 2 x 1 = 2, 2w and 2w^2.

mcqs.q: The cube roots of -27 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w, w^2. Step 2: Every cube root of N is the real cube root of N multiplied by 1, w, w^2 in turn. Step 3: The real cube root of -27 is -3, so the cube roots of -27 are -3, -3w and -3w^2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (1 - w - w^2)^7.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use 1 + w + w^2 = 0, so w + w^2 = -1. Step 2: 1 - w - w^2 = 1 - (w + w^2) = 1 - (-1) = 2. Step 3: Raise to the power: 2^7 = 128. So the value is 128.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (1 - 3w - 3w^2)^5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use 1 + w + w^2 = 0, so w + w^2 = -1. Step 2: 1 - 3w - 3w^2 = 1 - 3(w + w^2) = 1 - 3(-1) = 4. Step 3: Raise to the power: 4^5 = 1024. So the value is 1024.

mcqs.q: Evaluate (9 + 4w + 4w^2)^3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use 1 + w + w^2 = 0, so w + w^2 = -1. Step 2: 9 + 4w + 4w^2 = 9 + 4(w + w^2) = 9 + 4(-1) = 5. Step 3: Raise to the power: 5^3 = 125. So the value is 125.

mcqs.q: Evaluate w^37 + w^38 - 5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Reduce powers using w^3 = 1: w^37 = w^(36 + 1) = (w^3)^12 . w = w. Step 2: w^38 = w^(36 + 2) = w^2. Step 3: The expression becomes w + w^2 - 5. Step 4: Since 1 + w + w^2 = 0, w + w^2 = -1, so the value is -1 - 5 = -6.

mcqs.q: Evaluate w^(-13) + w^(-17).
Evaluate (-1 + sqrt(-3))^6 + (-1 - sqrt(-3))^6.
mcqs.why: Step 1: -1 + sqrt(-3) = 2w and -1 - sqrt(-3) = 2w^2, where w is a complex cube root of unity. Step 2: (2w)^6 + (2w^2)^6 = 64w^6 + 64w^12. Step 3: w^6 = (w^3)^2 = 1 and w^12 = (w^3)^4 = 1. Step 4: Value = 64 + 64 = 128.
Step 1: The bases are w and w^2, so the expression is w^9 + (w^2)^9 = w^9 + w^18. Step 2: w^9 = (w^3)^3 = 1 and w^18 = (w^3)^6 = 1, since w^3 = 1. Step 3: Value = 1 + 1 = 2.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0

Step 1: a = 1, b = -5, c = 3.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = -(-5)/1 = 5; P = 3/1 = 3.

Answer: S = -(-5)/1 = 5; P = 3/1 = 3.

Q1(ii) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 3x^2 + 7x - 11 = 0

Step 1: a = 3, b = 7, c = -11.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = -7/3; P = -11/3.

Answer: S = -7/3; P = -11/3.

Q1(iii) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of px^2 - qx + r = 0

Step 1: a = p, b = -q, c = r.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = q/p; P = r/p.

Answer: S = q/p; P = r/p.

Q1(iv) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of (a + b)x^2 - ax + b = 0

Step 1: a' = a + b, b' = -a, c' = b.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = a/(a + b); P = b/(a + b).

Answer: S = a/(a + b); P = b/(a + b).

Q1(v) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of (l + m)x^2 + (m + n)x + n - l = 0

Step 1: a' = l + m, b' = m + n, c' = n - l.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = -(m + n)/(l + m); P = (n - l)/(l + m).

Answer: S = -(m + n)/(l + m); P = (n - l)/(l + m).

Q1(vi) Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 7x^2 - 5mx + 9n = 0

Step 1: a = 7, b = -5m, c = 9n.

Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 3: S = 5m/7; P = 9n/7.

Answer: S = 5m/7; P = 9n/7.

Q2(i) Find k if the sum of the roots of 2kx^2 - 3x + 4k = 0 is twice the product of the roots

Step 1: Formulas: S = -b/a and P = c/a. Here a = 2k, b = -3, c = 4k.

Step 2: S = 3/(2k) and P = 4k/(2k) = 2.

Step 3: Given condition: S = 2P, so 3/(2k) = 2(2) = 4.

Step 4: 3 = 8k, so k = 3/8.

Q2(ii) Find k if the sum of the roots of x^2 + (3k - 7)x + 5k = 0 is 3/2 times the product of the roots

Step 1: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a; product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a.

Step 2: Here a = 1, b = 3k - 7, c = 5k, so S = 7 - 3k and P = 5k.

Step 3: Condition S = (3/2)P: 7 - 3k = (3/2)(5k) = 15k/2.

Step 4: Multiply by 2: 14 - 6k = 15k, so 14 = 21k.

Step 5: k = 2/3.

Q3(i) Find k if the sum of the squares of the roots of 4kx^2 + 3kx - 8 = 0 is 2

Step 1: Here a = 4k, b = 3k, c = -8, so S = -3k/(4k) = -3/4 and P = -8/(4k) = -2/k.

Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = S^2 - 2P.

Step 3: Substitute: (-3/4)^2 - 2(-2/k) = 9/16 + 4/k = 2 (given).

Step 4: 4/k = 2 - 9/16 = 23/16, so k = 64/23.

Answer: k = 64/23.

Q3(ii) Find k if the sum of the squares of the roots of x^2 - 2kx + (2k + 1) = 0 is 6

Step 1: Here S = 2k and P = 2k + 1.

Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = (2k)^2 - 2(2k + 1) = 4k^2 - 4k - 2.

Step 3: Set equal to 6: 4k^2 - 4k - 2 = 6, so 4k^2 - 4k - 8 = 0. Divide by 4: k^2 - k - 2 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (k - 2)(k + 1) = 0.

Step 5: k = 2 or k = -1.

Q4(i) Find p if the roots of x^2 - x + p^2 = 0 differ by unity

Step 1: Here S = 1 and P = p^2.

Step 2: Formula: (alpha - beta)^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 4.alpha.beta = S^2 - 4P = 1 - 4p^2.

Step 3: The roots differ by unity (1), so (alpha - beta)^2 = 1: 1 - 4p^2 = 1.

Step 4: 4p^2 = 0, so p = 0.

Q4(ii) Find p if the roots of x^2 + 3x + p - 2 = 0 differ by 2

Step 1: Here S = -3 and P = p - 2.

Step 2: Formula: (alpha - beta)^2 = S^2 - 4P = 9 - 4(p - 2) = 17 - 4p.

Step 3: The roots differ by 2, so (alpha - beta)^2 = 4: 17 - 4p = 4.

Step 4: 4p = 13, so p = 13/4.

Q5(i) Find m if the roots of x^2 - 7x + 3m - 5 = 0 satisfy 3.alpha + 2.beta = 4

Step 1: S = alpha + beta = 7 ... (i). Given 3.alpha + 2.beta = 4 ... (ii).

Step 2: Multiply (i) by 2: 2.alpha + 2.beta = 14. Subtract from (ii): alpha = 4 - 14 = -10.

Step 3: From (i): beta = 7 - (-10) = 17.

Step 4: P = alpha.beta = (-10)(17) = -170. Also P = 3m - 5.

Step 5: 3m - 5 = -170, so 3m = -165, so m = -55.

Q5(ii) Find m if the roots of x^2 + 7x + 3m - 5 = 0 satisfy 3.alpha - 2.beta = 4

Step 1: S = alpha + beta = -7 ... (i). Given 3.alpha - 2.beta = 4 ... (ii).

Step 2: Multiply (i) by 2: 2.alpha + 2.beta = -14. Add to (ii): 5.alpha = -10, so alpha = -2.

Step 3: From (i): beta = -7 + 2 = -5.

Step 4: P = alpha.beta = (-2)(-5) = 10. Also P = 3m - 5.

Step 5: 3m - 5 = 10, so 3m = 15, so m = 5.

Q5(iii) Find m if the roots of 3x^2 - 2x + 7m + 2 = 0 satisfy 7.alpha - 3.beta = 18

Step 1: S = alpha + beta = 2/3 ... (i). Given 7.alpha - 3.beta = 18 ... (ii).

Step 2: Multiply (i) by 3: 3.alpha + 3.beta = 2. Add to (ii): 10.alpha = 20, so alpha = 2.

Step 3: From (i): beta = 2/3 - 2 = -4/3.

Step 4: P = alpha.beta = 2 x (-4/3) = -8/3. Also P = (7m + 2)/3.

Step 5: 7m + 2 = -8, so 7m = -10, so m = -10/7.

Q6(i) Find m if sum and product of the roots of (2m + 3)x^2 + (7m - 5)x + (3m - 10) = 0 are equal to a given number lambda

Step 1: S = -(7m - 5)/(2m + 3) and P = (3m - 10)/(2m + 3).

Step 2: Given S = P = lambda, so S = P: -(7m - 5) = 3m - 10.

Step 3: -7m + 5 = 3m - 10, so 15 = 10m.

Step 4: m = 3/2.

Q6(ii) Find m if sum and product of the roots of 4x^2 - (3 + 5m)x - (9m - 17) = 0 are equal to a given number lambda

Step 1: S = (3 + 5m)/4 and P = -(9m - 17)/4 = (17 - 9m)/4.

Step 2: Given S = P: 3 + 5m = 17 - 9m.

Step 3: 14m = 14, so m = 1.

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 1, b = -5, c = 3. Step 2: Formulas: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a, and product of roots P = alpha.beta = c/a. Step 3: S = -(-5)/1 = 5 and P = 3/1 = 3. So S = 5 and P = 3.

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 3x^2 + 7x - 11 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 3, b = 7, c = -11. Step 2: Formulas: S = alpha + beta = -b/a and P = alpha.beta = c/a. Step 3: S = -7/3 and P = -11/3. So S = -7/3 and P = -11/3.

mcqs.q: Without solving, find the sum of the roots of px^2 - qx + r = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Here a = p, b = -q, c = r. Step 2: Formula: sum of roots S = alpha + beta = -b/a. Step 3: S = -(-q)/p = q/p. (The product is P = c/a = r/p.) So the sum of the roots is q/p.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the roots of 2kx^2 - 3x + 4k = 0 is twice the product of the roots.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formulas: S = -b/a and P = c/a. Here a = 2k, b = -3, c = 4k, so S = 3/(2k) and P = 4k/(2k) = 2. Step 2: Given condition S = 2P: 3/(2k) = 2 x 2 = 4. Step 3: 3 = 8k, so k = 3/8.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the roots of x^2 + (3k - 7)x + 5k = 0 is 3/2 times the product of the roots.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formulas: S = -b/a and P = c/a. Here S = 7 - 3k and P = 5k. Step 2: Condition S = (3/2)P: 7 - 3k = (3/2)(5k) = 15k/2. Step 3: Multiply by 2: 14 - 6k = 15k, so 14 = 21k. Step 4: k = 14/21 = 2/3.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the squares of the roots of 4kx^2 + 3kx - 8 = 0 is 2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Here S = -3k/(4k) = -3/4 and P = -8/(4k) = -2/k. Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = S^2 - 2P. Step 3: Substitute: 9/16 + 4/k = 2. Step 4: 4/k = 2 - 9/16 = 23/16, so k = 64/23.

mcqs.q: Find k if the sum of the squares of the roots of x^2 - 2kx + (2k + 1) = 0 is 6.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Here S = 2k and P = 2k + 1. Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = 4k^2 - 2(2k + 1) = 4k^2 - 4k - 2. Step 3: Set equal to 6: 4k^2 - 4k - 8 = 0; divide by 4: k^2 - k - 2 = 0. Step 4: Factorize: (k - 2)(k + 1) = 0, so k = 2 or k = -1.

mcqs.q: Find p if the roots of x^2 - x + p^2 = 0 differ by unity (1).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Here S = alpha + beta = 1 and P = alpha.beta = p^2. Step 2: Formula: (alpha - beta)^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 4.alpha.beta = S^2 - 4P = 1 - 4p^2. Step 3: The roots differ by 1, so (alpha - beta)^2 = 1: 1 - 4p^2 = 1. Step 4: 4p^2 = 0, so p = 0.

mcqs.q: Find p if the roots of x^2 + 3x + p - 2 = 0 differ by 2.
