mcqs.why: Step 1: Here S = -3 and P = p - 2. Step 2: Formula: (alpha - beta)^2 = S^2 - 4P = 9 - 4(p - 2) = 17 - 4p. Step 3: The roots differ by 2, so (alpha - beta)^2 = 4: 17 - 4p = 4. Step 4: 4p = 13, so p = 13/4.

mcqs.q: Find m if the roots alpha, beta of x^2 - 7x + 3m - 5 = 0 satisfy 3.alpha + 2.beta = 4.
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = alpha + beta = 7 ... (i), and 3.alpha + 2.beta = 4 ... (ii). Step 2: Multiply (i) by 2: 2.alpha + 2.beta = 14; subtract from (ii): alpha = 4 - 14 = -10. Step 3: From (i): beta = 7 - (-10) = 17. Step 4: P = alpha.beta = -170, and also P = 3m - 5. Step 5: 3m - 5 = -170, so 3m = -165 and m = -55.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, evaluate alpha^2 + beta^2

Step 1: Here S = alpha + beta = -p and P = alpha.beta = q.

Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = S^2 - 2P.

Step 3: = (-p)^2 - 2q = p^2 - 2q.

Answer: p^2 - 2q.

Q1(ii) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, evaluate alpha^3.beta + alpha.beta^3

Step 1: S = -p and P = q.

Step 2: Factor: alpha^3.beta + alpha.beta^3 = alpha.beta(alpha^2 + beta^2) = P(S^2 - 2P).

Step 3: = q(p^2 - 2q).

Answer: q(p^2 - 2q).

Q1(iii) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, evaluate alpha/beta + beta/alpha

Step 1: S = -p and P = q.

Step 2: alpha/beta + beta/alpha = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = (S^2 - 2P)/P.

Step 3: = (p^2 - 2q)/q.

Answer: (p^2 - 2q)/q.

Q2(i) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find 1/alpha + 1/beta

Step 1: S = 5/4 and P = 6/4 = 3/2.

Step 2: 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta) = S/P.

Step 3: = (5/4)/(3/2) = (5/4)(2/3) = 5/6.

Answer: 5/6.

Q2(ii) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find alpha^2.beta^2

Step 1: P = alpha.beta = 3/2.

Step 2: alpha^2.beta^2 = (alpha.beta)^2 = P^2 = (3/2)^2 = 9/4.

Answer: 9/4.

Q2(iii) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find 1/(alpha^2.beta) + 1/(alpha.beta^2)

Step 1: S = 5/4 and P = 3/2.

Step 2: Take LCM alpha^2.beta^2: the sum = (beta + alpha)/(alpha.beta)^2 = S/P^2.

Step 3: = (5/4)/(9/4) = 5/9.

Answer: 5/9.

Q2(iv) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find alpha^2/beta + beta^2/alpha

Step 1: S = 5/4 and P = 3/2.

Step 2: alpha^2/beta + beta^2/alpha = (alpha^3 + beta^3)/(alpha.beta). Formula: alpha^3 + beta^3 = (alpha + beta)^3 - 3.alpha.beta(alpha + beta) = S^3 - 3PS.

Step 3: S^3 - 3PS = (5/4)^3 - 3(3/2)(5/4) = 125/64 - 45/8 = 125/64 - 360/64 = -235/64.

Step 4: Divide by P: (-235/64)/(3/2) = (-235/64)(2/3) = -235/96.

Answer: -235/96.

Q3(i) If alpha, beta are the roots of lx^2 + mx + n = 0 (l not 0), find alpha^3.beta^2 + alpha^2.beta^3

Step 1: S = -m/l and P = n/l.

Step 2: Factor: alpha^3.beta^2 + alpha^2.beta^3 = alpha^2.beta^2(alpha + beta) = P^2 . S.

Step 3: = (n/l)^2 x (-m/l) = -m.n^2/l^3.

Answer: -mn^2/l^3.

Q3(ii) If alpha, beta are the roots of lx^2 + mx + n = 0 (l not 0), find 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2

Step 1: S = -m/l and P = n/l.

Step 2: 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2 = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta)^2 = (S^2 - 2P)/P^2.

Step 3: Numerator: (m^2/l^2) - 2n/l = (m^2 - 2nl)/l^2. Denominator: n^2/l^2.

Step 4: Value = (m^2 - 2nl)/n^2.

Answer: (m^2 - 2nl)/n^2.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, then alpha^2 + beta^2 equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Here S = alpha + beta = -p and P = alpha.beta = q. Step 2: Formula: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = S^2 - 2P. Step 3: Substitute: (-p)^2 - 2q = p^2 - 2q. So alpha^2 + beta^2 = p^2 - 2q.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, then alpha^3.beta + alpha.beta^3 equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = -p and P = q. Step 2: Factor: alpha^3.beta + alpha.beta^3 = alpha.beta(alpha^2 + beta^2) = P(S^2 - 2P), using the formula alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P. Step 3: Substitute: q(p^2 - 2q). So the value is q(p^2 - 2q).

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, then alpha/beta + beta/alpha equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = -p and P = q. Step 2: alpha/beta + beta/alpha = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = (S^2 - 2P)/P, using the formula alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P. Step 3: Substitute: (p^2 - 2q)/q. So the value is (p^2 - 2q)/q.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find 1/alpha + 1/beta.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formulas: S = -b/a = 5/4 and P = c/a = 6/4 = 3/2. Step 2: 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta) = S/P. Step 3: Substitute: (5/4)/(3/2) = (5/4) x (2/3) = 10/12 = 5/6. So the value is 5/6.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find alpha^2.beta^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: P = alpha.beta = c/a = 6/4 = 3/2. Step 2: alpha^2.beta^2 = (alpha.beta)^2 = P^2. Step 3: Substitute: (3/2)^2 = 9/4. So alpha^2.beta^2 = 9/4.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find 1/(alpha^2.beta) + 1/(alpha.beta^2).
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = 5/4 and P = 3/2. Step 2: Taking LCM alpha^2.beta^2, the sum equals (beta + alpha)/(alpha.beta)^2 = S/P^2. Step 3: Substitute: (5/4)/(3/2)^2 = (5/4)/(9/4) = 5/9. So the value is 5/9.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find alpha^2/beta + beta^2/alpha.
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = 5/4 and P = 3/2. Step 2: alpha^2/beta + beta^2/alpha = (alpha^3 + beta^3)/(alpha.beta), and the formula alpha^3 + beta^3 = S^3 - 3PS. Step 3: S^3 - 3PS = 125/64 - 3(3/2)(5/4) = 125/64 - 360/64 = -235/64. Step 4: Divide by P: (-235/64)/(3/2) = -235/96.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of lx^2 + mx + n = 0 (l not 0), then alpha^3.beta^2 + alpha^2.beta^3 equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formulas: S = -b/a = -m/l and P = c/a = n/l. Step 2: Factor: alpha^3.beta^2 + alpha^2.beta^3 = alpha^2.beta^2(alpha + beta) = P^2 x S. Step 3: Substitute: (n/l)^2 x (-m/l) = -mn^2/l^3. So the value is -mn^2/l^3.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of lx^2 + mx + n = 0 (l not 0), then 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2 equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = -m/l and P = n/l. Step 2: 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2 = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta)^2 = (S^2 - 2P)/P^2. Step 3: Numerator: m^2/l^2 - 2n/l = (m^2 - 2nl)/l^2; denominator: n^2/l^2. Step 4: Value = (m^2 - 2nl)/n^2.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of lx^2 + mx + n = 0 (l not 0), then alpha + beta equals:
mcqs.why: Step 1: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 the formula for the sum of roots is S = alpha + beta = -b/a. Step 2: Here a = l, b = m, c = n. Step 3: Substitute: S = -m/l. (The product is P = c/a = n/l.) So alpha + beta = -m/l.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.5
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(a) Write the quadratic equation having roots 1, 5

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = 1 + 5 = 6.

Step 3: P = (1)(5) = 5.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0.

Q1(b) Write the quadratic equation having roots 4, 9

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = 4 + 9 = 13.

Step 3: P = (4)(9) = 36.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0.

Q1(c) Write the quadratic equation having roots -2, 3

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = -2 + 3 = 1.

Step 3: P = (-2)(3) = -6.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - x - 6 = 0.

Q1(d) Write the quadratic equation having roots 0, -3

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = 0 + (-3) = -3.

Step 3: P = (0)(-3) = 0.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 + 3x = 0.

Q1(e) Write the quadratic equation having roots 2, -6

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = 2 + (-6) = -4.

Step 3: P = (2)(-6) = -12.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 + 4x - 12 = 0.

Q1(f) Write the quadratic equation having roots -1, -7

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = -1 + (-7) = -8.

Step 3: P = (-1)(-7) = 7.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 + 8x + 7 = 0.

Q1(g) Write the quadratic equation having roots 1 + i, 1 - i

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = (1 + i) + (1 - i) = 2.

Step 3: P = (1 + i)(1 - i) = 1 - i^2 = 1 + 1 = 2.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 2x + 2 = 0.

Q1(h) Write the quadratic equation having roots 3 + sqrt(2), 3 - sqrt(2)

Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 2: S = (3 + sqrt(2)) + (3 - sqrt(2)) = 6.

Step 3: P = (3 + sqrt(2))(3 - sqrt(2)) = 9 - 2 = 7.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 6x + 7 = 0.

Q2(a) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, form the equation whose roots are 2.alpha + 1, 2.beta + 1

Step 1: For the given equation S = alpha + beta = 3 and P = alpha.beta = 6.

Step 2: New sum S' = (2.alpha + 1) + (2.beta + 1) = 2(alpha + beta) + 2 = 2(3) + 2 = 8.

Step 3: New product P' = (2.alpha + 1)(2.beta + 1) = 4.alpha.beta + 2(alpha + beta) + 1 = 4(6) + 2(3) + 1 = 31.

Step 4: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2.

Step 5: Required equation: x^2 - 8x + 31 = 0.

Q2(b) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, form the equation whose roots are alpha^2, beta^2

Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6.

Step 2: New sum S' = alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = 9 - 12 = -3.

Step 3: New product P' = alpha^2.beta^2 = (alpha.beta)^2 = 36.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 + 3x + 36 = 0.

Q2(c) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, form the equation whose roots are 1/alpha, 1/beta

Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6.

Step 2: New sum S' = 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta) = 3/6 = 1/2.

Step 3: New product P' = 1/(alpha.beta) = 1/6.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - (1/2)x + 1/6 = 0, i.e. 6x^2 - 3x + 1 = 0.

Q2(d) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, form the equation whose roots are alpha/beta, beta/alpha

Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6.

Step 2: New sum S' = alpha/beta + beta/alpha = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = [(alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta]/(alpha.beta) = (9 - 12)/6 = -1/2.

Step 3: New product P' = (alpha/beta)(beta/alpha) = 1.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 + (1/2)x + 1 = 0, i.e. 2x^2 + x + 2 = 0.

Q2(e) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, form the equation whose roots are alpha + beta and 1/alpha + 1/beta

Step 1: The new roots are the numbers alpha + beta = 3 and 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta) = 3/6 = 1/2.

Step 2: New sum S' = 3 + 1/2 = 7/2.

Step 3: New product P' = 3 x 1/2 = 3/2.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - (7/2)x + 3/2 = 0, i.e. 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0.

Q3(a) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, form the equation whose roots are alpha^2, beta^2

Step 1: S = -p and P = q.

Step 2: New sum S' = alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = p^2 - 2q.

Step 3: New product P' = (alpha.beta)^2 = q^2.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - (p^2 - 2q)x + q^2 = 0.

Q3(b) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, form the equation whose roots are alpha/beta, beta/alpha

Step 1: S = -p and P = q.

Step 2: New sum S' = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = (S^2 - 2P)/P = (p^2 - 2q)/q.

Step 3: New product P' = 1.

Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - [(p^2 - 2q)/q]x + 1 = 0, i.e. qx^2 - (p^2 - 2q)x + q = 0.

mcqs.q: The quadratic equation having roots 1 and 5 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2. Step 2: S = 1 + 5 = 6. Step 3: P = 1 x 5 = 5. Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0.

mcqs.q: The quadratic equation having roots -2 and 3 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2. Step 2: S = -2 + 3 = 1. Step 3: P = (-2)(3) = -6. Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - x - 6 = 0.

mcqs.q: The quadratic equation having roots 0 and -3 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0, where S = r1 + r2 and P = r1.r2. Step 2: S = 0 + (-3) = -3. Step 3: P = 0 x (-3) = 0. Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - (-3)x + 0 = x^2 + 3x = 0.

mcqs.q: The quadratic equation having roots 1 + i and 1 - i is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0. Step 2: S = (1 + i) + (1 - i) = 2. Step 3: P = (1 + i)(1 - i) = 1 - i^2 = 1 + 1 = 2. Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 2x + 2 = 0.

mcqs.q: The quadratic equation having roots 3 + sqrt(2) and 3 - sqrt(2) is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the equation with roots r1, r2 is x^2 - Sx + P = 0. Step 2: S = (3 + sqrt(2)) + (3 - sqrt(2)) = 6. Step 3: P = (3 + sqrt(2))(3 - sqrt(2)) = 9 - 2 = 7. Step 4: Required equation: x^2 - 6x + 7 = 0.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, the equation whose roots are 2.alpha + 1 and 2.beta + 1 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: For the given equation S = alpha + beta = 3 and P = alpha.beta = 6. Step 2: New sum S' = 2(alpha + beta) + 2 = 2(3) + 2 = 8. Step 3: New product P' = (2.alpha + 1)(2.beta + 1) = 4.alpha.beta + 2(alpha + beta) + 1 = 24 + 6 + 1 = 31. Step 4: Formula x^2 - S'x + P' = 0 gives x^2 - 8x + 31 = 0.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, the equation whose roots are alpha^2 and beta^2 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6. Step 2: New sum S' = alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta = 9 - 12 = -3. Step 3: New product P' = (alpha.beta)^2 = 36. Step 4: Formula x^2 - S'x + P' = 0 gives x^2 + 3x + 36 = 0.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, the equation whose roots are 1/alpha and 1/beta is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6. Step 2: New sum S' = 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta) = 3/6 = 1/2. Step 3: New product P' = 1/(alpha.beta) = 1/6. Step 4: x^2 - (1/2)x + 1/6 = 0; multiply by 6: 6x^2 - 3x + 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, the equation whose roots are alpha/beta and beta/alpha is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = 3 and P = 6. Step 2: New sum S' = alpha/beta + beta/alpha = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = [(alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta]/(alpha.beta) = (9 - 12)/6 = -1/2. Step 3: New product P' = (alpha/beta)(beta/alpha) = 1. Step 4: x^2 + (1/2)x + 1 = 0; multiply by 2: 2x^2 + x + 2 = 0.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 + px + q = 0, the equation whose roots are alpha^2 and beta^2 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: S = -p and P = q. Step 2: New sum S' = alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = p^2 - 2q. Step 3: New product P' = (alpha.beta)^2 = q^2. Step 4: Formula x^2 - S'x + P' = 0 gives x^2 - (p^2 - 2q)x + q^2 = 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.6
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Use synthetic division to find quotient and remainder when (x^2 + 7x - 1) is divided by (x + 1)

Step 1: Divisor x + 1 = x - (-1), so use a = -1. Coefficients of dividend: 1, 7, -1.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Multiply 1 x (-1) = -1; add to 7: 6. Multiply 6 x (-1) = -6; add to -1: -7.

Step 3: The last number is the remainder; the others are the quotient coefficients.

Quotient = x + 6; Remainder = -7.

Q1(ii) Use synthetic division to find quotient and remainder when (4x^3 - 5x + 15) is divided by (x + 3)

Step 1: Use a = -3. Coefficients (fill the missing x^2 term with 0): 4, 0, -5, 15.

Step 2: Bring down 4. Multiply 4 x (-3) = -12; add to 0: -12. Multiply (-12)(-3) = 36; add to -5: 31. Multiply 31 x (-3) = -93; add to 15: -78.

Quotient = 4x^2 - 12x + 31; Remainder = -78.

Q1(iii) Use synthetic division to find quotient and remainder when (x^3 + x^2 - 3x + 2) is divided by (x - 2)

Step 1: Use a = 2. Coefficients: 1, 1, -3, 2.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Multiply 1 x 2 = 2; add to 1: 3. Multiply 3 x 2 = 6; add to -3: 3. Multiply 3 x 2 = 6; add to 2: 8.

Quotient = x^2 + 3x + 3; Remainder = 8.

Q2(i) Find h by synthetic division if 3 is the zero of the polynomial 2x^3 - 3hx^2 + 9

Step 1: 3 is a zero, so dividing by (x - 3) leaves remainder 0. Coefficients: 2, -3h, 0, 9; use a = 3.

Step 2: Bring down 2. Multiply 2 x 3 = 6; add: -3h + 6. Multiply 3(-3h + 6) = -9h + 18; add to 0: -9h + 18. Multiply 3(-9h + 18) = -27h + 54; add to 9: remainder = -27h + 63.

Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -27h + 63 = 0, so h = 63/27 = 7/3.

Answer: h = 7/3.

Q2(ii) Find h by synthetic division if 1 is the zero of the polynomial x^3 - 2hx^2 + 11

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, -2h, 0, 11; use a = 1.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Add 1: -2h + 1. Add again: -2h + 1. Remainder = (-2h + 1) + 11 = -2h + 12.

Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -2h + 12 = 0, so h = 6.

Answer: h = 6.

Q2(iii) Find h by synthetic division if -1 is the zero of the polynomial 2x^3 + 5hx - 23

Step 1: Coefficients: 2, 0, 5h, -23; use a = -1.

Step 2: Bring down 2. Multiply 2 x (-1) = -2; add to 0: -2. Multiply (-2)(-1) = 2; add to 5h: 5h + 2. Multiply (-1)(5h + 2) = -5h - 2; add to -23: remainder = -5h - 25.

Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -5h - 25 = 0, so h = -5.

Answer: h = -5.

Q3(i) Use synthetic division to find l and m if (x + 3) and (x - 2) are factors of x^3 + 4x^2 + 2lx + m

Step 1: Factors (x + 3) and (x - 2) mean -3 and 2 are zeros, so P(-3) = 0 and P(2) = 0.

Step 2: P(-3) = -27 + 36 - 6l + m = 0, so m - 6l + 9 = 0 ... (i).

Step 3: P(2) = 8 + 16 + 4l + m = 0, so m + 4l + 24 = 0 ... (ii).

Step 4: Subtract (i) from (ii): 10l + 15 = 0, so l = -3/2.

Step 5: From (i): m = 6l - 9 = 6(-3/2) - 9 = -18.

Answer: l = -3/2, m = -18.

Q3(ii) Use synthetic division to find l and m if (x - 1) and (x + 1) are factors of x^3 - 3lx^2 + 2mx + 6

Step 1: 1 and -1 are zeros, so P(1) = 0 and P(-1) = 0.

Step 2: P(1) = 1 - 3l + 2m + 6 = 0, so -3l + 2m + 7 = 0 ... (i).

Step 3: P(-1) = -1 - 3l - 2m + 6 = 0, so -3l - 2m + 5 = 0 ... (ii).

Step 4: Add (i) and (ii): -6l + 12 = 0, so l = 2.

Step 5: From (i): 2m = 3l - 7 = 6 - 7 = -1, so m = -1/2.

Answer: l = 2, m = -1/2.

Q4(i) Solve by synthetic division: 2 is the root of x^3 - 28x + 48 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 0, -28, 48; divide by (x - 2) using a = 2.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Multiply 2; add to 0: 2. Multiply 4; add to -28: -24. Multiply -48; add to 48: 0 (checks: 2 is a root).

Step 3: Depressed equation: x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (x + 6)(x - 4) = 0, so x = -6 or x = 4.

Solution set = {-6, 2, 4}.

Q4(ii) Solve by synthetic division: 3 is the root of 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients: 2, -3, -11, 6; use a = 3.

Step 2: Bring down 2. Multiply 6; add to -3: 3. Multiply 9; add to -11: -2. Multiply -6; add to 6: 0.

Step 3: Depressed equation: 2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: 2x^2 + 4x - x - 2 = 0, so 2x(x + 2) - 1(x + 2) = 0, so (x + 2)(2x - 1) = 0, giving x = -2 or x = 1/2.

Solution set = {-2, 1/2, 3}.

Q4(iii) Solve by synthetic division: -1 is the root of 4x^3 - x^2 - 11x - 6 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients: 4, -1, -11, -6; use a = -1.

Step 2: Bring down 4. Multiply -4; add to -1: -5. Multiply 5; add to -11: -6. Multiply 6; add to -6: 0.

Step 3: Depressed equation: 4x^2 - 5x - 6 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize (ac = -24; numbers -8, 3): 4x^2 - 8x + 3x - 6 = 0, so 4x(x - 2) + 3(x - 2) = 0, so (x - 2)(4x + 3) = 0, giving x = 2 or x = -3/4.

Solution set = {-1, -3/4, 2}.

Q5(i) Solve by synthetic division: 1 and 3 are the roots of x^4 - 10x^2 + 9 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 0, -10, 0, 9. Divide by (x - 1): row becomes 1, 1, -9, -9, remainder 0.

Step 2: Divide the result 1, 1, -9, -9 by (x - 3): row becomes 1, 4, 3, remainder 0.

Step 3: Depressed equation: x^2 + 4x + 3 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (x + 1)(x + 3) = 0, so x = -1 or x = -3.

Solution set = {-3, -1, 1, 3}.

Q5(ii) Solve by synthetic division: 3 and -4 are the roots of x^4 + 2x^3 - 13x^2 - 14x + 24 = 0

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 2, -13, -14, 24. Divide by (x - 3): row becomes 1, 5, 2, -8, remainder 0.

Step 2: Divide 1, 5, 2, -8 by (x + 4) using a = -4: row becomes 1, 1, -2, remainder 0.

Step 3: Depressed equation: x^2 + x - 2 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (x + 2)(x - 1) = 0, so x = -2 or x = 1.

Solution set = {-4, -2, 1, 3}.

mcqs.q: Use synthetic division: when (x^2 + 7x - 1) is divided by (x + 1), the quotient is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Divisor x + 1 = x - (-1), so use a = -1. Coefficients of the dividend: 1, 7, -1. Step 2: Bring down 1; multiply 1 x (-1) = -1, add to 7: 6; multiply 6 x (-1) = -6, add to -1: -7. Step 3: The last number -7 is the remainder and the others are the quotient coefficients, so the quotient is x + 6 (remainder -7).

mcqs.q: Use synthetic division: when (4x^3 - 5x + 15) is divided by (x + 3), the quotient is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use a = -3. Coefficients, filling the missing x^2 term with 0: 4, 0, -5, 15. Step 2: Bring down 4; multiply by -3: -12, add to 0: -12; multiply: 36, add to -5: 31; multiply: -93, add to 15: -78. Step 3: Quotient coefficients 4, -12, 31 give quotient 4x^2 - 12x + 31 (remainder -78).

mcqs.q: Use synthetic division: when (x^3 + x^2 - 3x + 2) is divided by (x - 2), the remainder is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Use a = 2. Coefficients: 1, 1, -3, 2. Step 2: Bring down 1; multiply 1 x 2 = 2, add to 1: 3; multiply 3 x 2 = 6, add to -3: 3; multiply 3 x 2 = 6, add to 2: 8. Step 3: The last number is the remainder, so the remainder is 8 (quotient x^2 + 3x + 3).

mcqs.q: Find h by synthetic division if 3 is the zero of the polynomial 2x^3 - 3hx^2 + 9.
mcqs.why: Step 1: 3 is a zero, so dividing by (x - 3) leaves remainder 0. Coefficients: 2, -3h, 0, 9; use a = 3. Step 2: Synthetic division gives remainder = -27h + 63. Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -27h + 63 = 0, so 27h = 63 and h = 63/27 = 7/3.

mcqs.q: Find h by synthetic division if 1 is the zero of the polynomial x^3 - 2hx^2 + 11.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Coefficients: 1, -2h, 0, 11; use a = 1. Step 2: Bring down 1; add 1: -2h + 1; add again: -2h + 1; remainder = (-2h + 1) + 11 = -2h + 12. Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -2h + 12 = 0, so h = 6.

mcqs.q: Find h by synthetic division if -1 is the zero of the polynomial 2x^3 + 5hx - 23.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Coefficients: 2, 0, 5h, -23; use a = -1. Step 2: Bring down 2; multiply by -1: -2, add to 0: -2; multiply: 2, add to 5h: 5h + 2; multiply by -1: -5h - 2, add to -23: remainder = -5h - 25. Step 3: Set the remainder to 0: -5h - 25 = 0, so h = -5.

mcqs.q: Use synthetic division to find m if (x + 3) and (x - 2) are factors of x^3 + 4x^2 + 2lx + m (given l = -3/2).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Factors (x + 3) and (x - 2) mean -3 and 2 are zeros, so P(-3) = 0 and P(2) = 0. Step 2: P(-3) = -27 + 36 - 6l + m = 0 gives m - 6l + 9 = 0; P(2) = 8 + 16 + 4l + m = 0 gives m + 4l + 24 = 0. Step 3: Subtracting gives 10l + 15 = 0, so l = -3/2. Step 4: m = 6l - 9 = 6(-3/2) - 9 = -18.

mcqs.q: Use synthetic division to find l if (x - 1) and (x + 1) are factors of x^3 - 3lx^2 + 2mx + 6.
mcqs.why: Step 1: 1 and -1 are zeros, so P(1) = 0 and P(-1) = 0. Step 2: P(1) = 1 - 3l + 2m + 6 = 0 gives -3l + 2m + 7 = 0; P(-1) = -1 - 3l - 2m + 6 = 0 gives -3l - 2m + 5 = 0. Step 3: Add the two equations: -6l + 12 = 0, so l = 2 (and then m = -1/2).

mcqs.q: Solve by synthetic division, given that 2 is a root of x^3 - 28x + 48 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 0, -28, 48; divide by (x - 2) using a = 2. Step 2: Synthetic division gives the depressed equation x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0 with remainder 0. Step 3: Factorize: (x + 6)(x - 4) = 0, so x = -6 or x = 4. Step 4: Together with the given root 2, the solution set is {-6, 2, 4}.

mcqs.q: Solve by synthetic division, given that 3 is a root of 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6 = 0. The solution set is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Coefficients: 2, -3, -11, 6; use a = 3. Step 2: Synthetic division gives the depressed equation 2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0 with remainder 0. Step 3: Factorize: 2x^2 + 4x - x - 2 = (x + 2)(2x - 1) = 0, giving x = -2 or x = 1/2. Step 4: Together with the given root 3, the solution set is {-2, 1/2, 3}.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.7
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 Solve: x + y = 5 ; x^2 - 2y - 14 = 0

Step 1: From the linear equation, y = 5 - x.

Step 2: Substitute in the quadratic: x^2 - 2(5 - x) - 14 = 0, so x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0.

Step 3: Factorize: (x + 6)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 4 or x = -6.

Step 4: Corresponding y: x = 4 gives y = 1; x = -6 gives y = 11.

Solution set = {(-6, 11), (4, 1)}.

Q2 Solve: 3x - 2y = 1 ; x^2 + xy - y^2 = 1

Step 1: From the linear equation, y = (3x - 1)/2.

Step 2: Substitute and multiply by 4: 4x^2 + 2x(3x - 1) - (3x - 1)^2 = 4.

Step 3: Expand: 4x^2 + 6x^2 - 2x - 9x^2 + 6x - 1 - 4 = 0, so x^2 + 4x - 5 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (x + 5)(x - 1) = 0, so x = 1 or x = -5.

Step 5: Corresponding y: x = 1 gives y = 1; x = -5 gives y = -8.

Solution set = {(-5, -8), (1, 1)}.

Q3 Solve: x - y = 7 ; 2/x - 5/y = 2

Step 1: From the linear equation, x = y + 7.

Step 2: Clear fractions in the second equation (multiply by xy): 2y - 5x = 2xy.

Step 3: Substitute x = y + 7: 2y - 5(y + 7) = 2y(y + 7), so -3y - 35 = 2y^2 + 14y.

Step 4: Standard form: 2y^2 + 17y + 35 = 0. Discriminant = 289 - 280 = 9. Formula: y = (-17 +- 3)/4, so y = -5 or y = -7/2.

Step 5: Corresponding x: y = -5 gives x = 2; y = -7/2 gives x = 7/2.

Solution set = {(2, -5), (7/2, -7/2)}.

Q4 Solve: x + y = a - b ; a/x - b/y = 2

Step 1: Put s = a - b, so y = s - x.

Step 2: Clear fractions: a(s - x) - bx = 2x(s - x), so as - ax - bx = 2sx - 2x^2.

Step 3: Standard form with s = a - b: 2x^2 - (3a - b)x + a(a - b) = 0.

Step 4: Discriminant: (3a - b)^2 - 8a(a - b) = 9a^2 - 6ab + b^2 - 8a^2 + 8ab = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2.

Step 5: Formula: x = [(3a - b) +- (a + b)]/4, so x = a or x = (a - b)/2.

Step 6: Corresponding y = s - x: x = a gives y = -b; x = (a - b)/2 gives y = (a - b)/2.

Solution set = {(a, -b), ((a - b)/2, (a - b)/2)}.

Q5 Solve: x^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 10 ; x^2 + y^2 + 4x = 1

Step 1: Expand the first equation: x^2 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = 10, so x^2 + y^2 = 9 + 2y ... (i).

Step 2: Substitute (i) in the second equation: 9 + 2y + 4x = 1, so 2x + y = -4, so y = -4 - 2x ... (ii).

Step 3: Put (ii) in (i): x^2 + (-4 - 2x)^2 = 9 + 2(-4 - 2x), so x^2 + 4x^2 + 16x + 16 = 1 - 4x... collecting: 5x^2 + 20x + 15 = 0. Divide by 5: x^2 + 4x + 3 = 0.

Step 4: Factorize: (x + 1)(x + 3) = 0, so x = -1 or x = -3.

Step 5: From (ii): x = -1 gives y = -2; x = -3 gives y = 2.

Solution set = {(-3, 2), (-1, -2)}.

Q6 Solve: (x + 1)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 5 ; (x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 5

Step 1: Expand: eq1 gives x^2 + y^2 + 2x + 2y = 3 ... (i); eq2 gives x^2 + y^2 + 4x = 1, so x^2 + y^2 = 1 - 4x ... (ii).

Step 2: Substitute (ii) in (i): 1 - 4x + 2x + 2y = 3, so -2x + 2y = 2, so y = x + 1 ... (iii).

Step 3: Put (iii) in (ii): x^2 + (x + 1)^2 = 1 - 4x, so 2x^2 + 2x + 1 = 1 - 4x, so 2x^2 + 6x = 0, so 2x(x + 3) = 0.

Step 4: x = 0 or x = -3.

Step 5: From (iii): x = 0 gives y = 1; x = -3 gives y = -2.

Solution set = {(-3, -2), (0, 1)}.

Q7 Solve: x^2 + 2y^2 = 22 ; 5x^2 + y^2 = 29

Step 1: Multiply the second equation by 2: 10x^2 + 2y^2 = 58.

Step 2: Subtract the first equation: 9x^2 = 36, so x^2 = 4, so x = +-2.

Step 3: From the second equation: y^2 = 29 - 5(4) = 9, so y = +-3.

Step 4: Every combination satisfies both equations.

Solution set = {(2, 3), (2, -3), (-2, 3), (-2, -3)}.

Q8 Solve: 4x^2 - 5y^2 = 6 ; 3x^2 + y^2 = 14

Step 1: From the second equation: y^2 = 14 - 3x^2.

Step 2: Substitute in the first: 4x^2 - 5(14 - 3x^2) = 6, so 19x^2 - 70 = 6, so 19x^2 = 76, so x^2 = 4, x = +-2.

Step 3: y^2 = 14 - 12 = 2, so y = +-sqrt(2).

Solution set = {(2, sqrt(2)), (2, -sqrt(2)), (-2, sqrt(2)), (-2, -sqrt(2))}.

Q9 Solve: 7x^2 - 3y^2 = 4 ; 2x^2 + 5y^2 = 7

Step 1: Multiply the first equation by 5: 35x^2 - 15y^2 = 20. Multiply the second by 3: 6x^2 + 15y^2 = 21.

Step 2: Add: 41x^2 = 41, so x^2 = 1, x = +-1.

Step 3: From the second equation: 5y^2 = 7 - 2 = 5, so y^2 = 1, y = +-1.

Solution set = {(1, 1), (1, -1), (-1, 1), (-1, -1)}.

Q10 Solve: x^2 + 2y^2 = 3 ; x^2 + 4xy - 5y^2 = 0

Step 1: Factorize the homogeneous equation: x^2 + 4xy - 5y^2 = (x + 5y)(x - y) = 0, so x = y or x = -5y.

Step 2: Case x = y: x^2 + 2x^2 = 3, so x^2 = 1, giving (1, 1) and (-1, -1).

Step 3: Case x = -5y: 25y^2 + 2y^2 = 3, so 27y^2 = 3, y^2 = 1/9, y = +-1/3, with x = -5y giving (-5/3, 1/3) and (5/3, -1/3).

Solution set = {(1, 1), (-1, -1), (-5/3, 1/3), (5/3, -1/3)}.

Q11 Solve: 3x^2 - y^2 = 26 ; 3x^2 - 5xy - 12y^2 = 0

Step 1: Factorize the homogeneous equation: 3x^2 - 5xy - 12y^2 = (x - 3y)(3x + 4y) = 0, so x = 3y or 3x = -4y.

Step 2: Case x = 3y: 3(9y^2) - y^2 = 26y^2 = 26, so y = +-1, giving (3, 1) and (-3, -1).

Step 3: Case x = -4y/3: 3(16y^2/9) - y^2 = 13y^2/3 = 26, so y^2 = 6, y = +-sqrt(6), with x = -4y/3 giving (-4.sqrt(6)/3, sqrt(6)) and (4.sqrt(6)/3, -sqrt(6)).

Solution set = {(3, 1), (-3, -1), (-4.sqrt(6)/3, sqrt(6)), (4.sqrt(6)/3, -sqrt(6))}.

Q12 Solve: x^2 + xy = 5 ; y^2 + xy = 3

Step 1: Add the equations: x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = 8, so (x + y)^2 = 8, so x + y = +-2.sqrt(2) ... (i).

Step 2: Subtract: x^2 - y^2 = 2, so (x - y)(x + y) = 2, so x - y = 2/(x + y) = +-sqrt(2)/2 with the same sign as (i) ... (ii).

Step 3: Case +: adding (i),(ii): 2x = 2.sqrt(2) + sqrt(2)/2 = 5.sqrt(2)/2, so x = 5.sqrt(2)/4 and y = 3.sqrt(2)/4.

Step 4: Case -: x = -5.sqrt(2)/4 and y = -3.sqrt(2)/4.

Solution set = {(5.sqrt(2)/4, 3.sqrt(2)/4), (-5.sqrt(2)/4, -3.sqrt(2)/4)}.

Q13 Solve: x^2 - 2xy = 7 ; xy + 3y^2 = 2

Step 1: From the second equation: xy = 2 - 3y^2 ... (i).

Step 2: Substitute in the first: x^2 = 7 + 2xy = 7 + 2(2 - 3y^2) = 11 - 6y^2 ... (ii).

Step 3: Square (i) and use (ii): x^2y^2 = (11 - 6y^2)y^2 = (2 - 3y^2)^2. Expand: 11y^2 - 6y^4 = 4 - 12y^2 + 9y^4, so 15y^4 - 23y^2 + 4 = 0.

Step 4: Treat as quadratic in y^2: discriminant = 529 - 240 = 289 = 17^2. y^2 = (23 +- 17)/30, so y^2 = 4/3 or y^2 = 1/5.

Step 5: y^2 = 4/3: from (i) xy = 2 - 4 = -2, so x = -2/y, giving (-sqrt(3), 2.sqrt(3)/3) and (sqrt(3), -2.sqrt(3)/3).

Step 6: y^2 = 1/5: from (i) xy = 2 - 3/5 = 7/5, so x = (7/5)/y, giving (7.sqrt(5)/5, sqrt(5)/5) and (-7.sqrt(5)/5, -sqrt(5)/5).

Solution set = {(-sqrt(3), 2.sqrt(3)/3), (sqrt(3), -2.sqrt(3)/3), (7.sqrt(5)/5, sqrt(5)/5), (-7.sqrt(5)/5, -sqrt(5)/5)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x + y = 5 and x^2 - 2y - 14 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: From the linear equation, y = 5 - x. Step 2: Substitute: x^2 - 2(5 - x) - 14 = 0, so x^2 + 2x - 24 = 0. Step 3: Factorize: (x + 6)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 4 or x = -6. Step 4: x = 4 gives y = 1; x = -6 gives y = 11. Solution set = {(-6, 11), (4, 1)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: 3x - 2y = 1 and x^2 + xy - y^2 = 1.
mcqs.why: Step 1: From the linear equation, y = (3x - 1)/2. Step 2: Substitute and multiply by 4: 4x^2 + 2x(3x - 1) - (3x - 1)^2 = 4. Step 3: Expand: x^2 + 4x - 5 = 0. Step 4: Factorize: (x + 5)(x - 1) = 0, so x = 1 or x = -5. Step 5: x = 1 gives y = 1; x = -5 gives y = -8. Solution set = {(-5, -8), (1, 1)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x - y = 7 and 2/x - 5/y = 2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: From the linear equation, x = y + 7. Step 2: Clear fractions (multiply by xy): 2y - 5x = 2xy. Step 3: Substitute: -3y - 35 = 2y^2 + 14y, so 2y^2 + 17y + 35 = 0. Step 4: Discriminant = 289 - 280 = 9; formula: y = (-17 +- 3)/4, so y = -5 or y = -7/2. Step 5: y = -5 gives x = 2; y = -7/2 gives x = 7/2.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x^2 + 2y^2 = 22 and 5x^2 + y^2 = 29.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply the second equation by 2: 10x^2 + 2y^2 = 58. Step 2: Subtract the first equation: 9x^2 = 36, so x^2 = 4 and x = +-2. Step 3: From the second equation: y^2 = 29 - 5(4) = 9, so y = +-3. Step 4: Every combination satisfies both equations: {(2, 3), (2, -3), (-2, 3), (-2, -3)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: 4x^2 - 5y^2 = 6 and 3x^2 + y^2 = 14.
mcqs.why: Step 1: From the second equation: y^2 = 14 - 3x^2. Step 2: Substitute in the first: 4x^2 - 5(14 - 3x^2) = 6, so 19x^2 = 76 and x^2 = 4, giving x = +-2. Step 3: y^2 = 14 - 12 = 2, so y = +-sqrt(2). Step 4: Solution set = {(2, sqrt(2)), (2, -sqrt(2)), (-2, sqrt(2)), (-2, -sqrt(2))}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: 7x^2 - 3y^2 = 4 and 2x^2 + 5y^2 = 7.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply the first equation by 5: 35x^2 - 15y^2 = 20; multiply the second by 3: 6x^2 + 15y^2 = 21. Step 2: Add: 41x^2 = 41, so x^2 = 1 and x = +-1. Step 3: From the second equation: 5y^2 = 7 - 2 = 5, so y^2 = 1 and y = +-1. Step 4: Solution set = {(1, 1), (1, -1), (-1, 1), (-1, -1)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 10 and x^2 + y^2 + 4x = 1.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand the first equation: x^2 + y^2 = 9 + 2y ... (i). Step 2: Substitute (i) in the second: 9 + 2y + 4x = 1, so y = -4 - 2x ... (ii). Step 3: Put (ii) in (i): 5x^2 + 20x + 15 = 0; divide by 5: x^2 + 4x + 3 = 0. Step 4: Factorize: (x + 1)(x + 3) = 0, so x = -1 or x = -3. Step 5: x = -1 gives y = -2; x = -3 gives y = 2.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: (x + 1)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 5 and (x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand: eq1 gives x^2 + y^2 + 2x + 2y = 3 and eq2 gives x^2 + y^2 = 1 - 4x. Step 2: Substitute: 1 - 4x + 2x + 2y = 3, so y = x + 1. Step 3: Substitute back: x^2 + (x + 1)^2 = 1 - 4x, so 2x^2 + 6x = 0, i.e. 2x(x + 3) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = -3. Step 4: x = 0 gives y = 1; x = -3 gives y = -2.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x^2 + xy = 5 and y^2 + xy = 3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Add the equations: (x + y)^2 = 8, so x + y = +-2.sqrt(2). Step 2: Subtract: (x - y)(x + y) = 2, so x - y = +-sqrt(2)/2 with the same sign. Step 3: Positive case: adding gives 2x = 5.sqrt(2)/2, so x = 5.sqrt(2)/4 and y = 3.sqrt(2)/4. Step 4: Negative case gives the negatives of both. Solution set = {(5.sqrt(2)/4, 3.sqrt(2)/4), (-5.sqrt(2)/4, -3.sqrt(2)/4)}.

mcqs.q: Solve the simultaneous equations: x^2 + 2y^2 = 3 and x^2 + 4xy - 5y^2 = 0.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Factorize the homogeneous equation: (x + 5y)(x - y) = 0, so x = y or x = -5y. Step 2: Case x = y: 3x^2 = 3, so x^2 = 1, giving (1, 1) and (-1, -1). Step 3: Case x = -5y: 27y^2 = 3, so y^2 = 1/9 and y = +-1/3, giving (-5/3, 1/3) and (5/3, -1/3). Solution set = {(1, 1), (-1, -1), (-5/3, 1/3), (5/3, -1/3)}.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.8
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 The product of two positive consecutive numbers is 182. Find the numbers.

Step 1: Let the numbers be n and n + 1. Then n(n + 1) = 182.

Step 2: n^2 + n - 182 = 0.

Step 3: Factorize (ac = -182; numbers 14, -13): (n + 14)(n - 13) = 0, so n = 13 or n = -14.

Step 4: Positive numbers: n = 13, so the numbers are 13 and 14.

Check: 13 x 14 = 182. Correct.

Q2 The sum of the squares of three positive consecutive numbers is 77. Find them.

Step 1: Let the numbers be n - 1, n, n + 1. Then (n - 1)^2 + n^2 + (n + 1)^2 = 77.

Step 2: Expand: 3n^2 + 2 = 77, so 3n^2 = 75, so n^2 = 25, n = 5 (positive).

Step 3: The numbers are 4, 5, 6.

Check: 16 + 25 + 36 = 77. Correct.

Q3 The sum of five times a number and the square of the number is 204. Find the number.

Step 1: Let the number be n. Then n^2 + 5n = 204.

Step 2: n^2 + 5n - 204 = 0. Discriminant = 25 + 816 = 841 = 29^2.

Step 3: Formula: n = (-5 +- 29)/2, so n = 12 or n = -17.

Answer: 12 (the negative root -17 also satisfies the equation).

Q4 The product of five less than three times a certain number and one less than four times the number is 7. Find the number.

Step 1: Let the number be n. Then (3n - 5)(4n - 1) = 7.

Step 2: Expand: 12n^2 - 23n + 5 = 7, so 12n^2 - 23n - 2 = 0.

Step 3: Discriminant = 529 + 96 = 625 = 25^2. Formula: n = (23 +- 25)/24, so n = 2 or n = -1/12.

Answer: 2 (the other algebraic root is -1/12).

Q5 The difference of a number and its reciprocal is 15/4. Find the number.

Step 1: Let the number be n. Then n - 1/n = 15/4.

Step 2: Multiply by 4n: 4n^2 - 4 = 15n, so 4n^2 - 15n - 4 = 0.

Step 3: Discriminant = 225 + 64 = 289 = 17^2. Formula: n = (15 +- 17)/8, so n = 4 or n = -1/4.

Answer: 4 (the other algebraic root is -1/4).

Q6 The sum of the squares of two digits of a positive integral number is 65 and the number is 9 times the sum of its digits. Find the number.

Step 1: Let the tens digit be a and the units digit be b. Then a^2 + b^2 = 65 ... (i), and the number 10a + b = 9(a + b) ... (ii).

Step 2: From (ii): 10a + b = 9a + 9b, so a = 8b.

Step 3: Substitute in (i): 64b^2 + b^2 = 65, so 65b^2 = 65, so b^2 = 1, b = 1 (digit).

Step 4: a = 8. The number is 81.

Check: 8^2 + 1^2 = 65 and 81 = 9 x (8 + 1). Correct.

Q7 The sum of the co-ordinates of a point is 9 and the sum of their squares is 45. Find the co-ordinates of the point.

Step 1: Let the co-ordinates be x, y. Then x + y = 9 ... (i) and x^2 + y^2 = 45 ... (ii).

Step 2: Square (i): x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = 81. Using (ii): 45 + 2xy = 81, so xy = 18.

Step 3: x, y are roots of t^2 - 9t + 18 = 0, i.e. (t - 3)(t - 6) = 0, so t = 3 or 6.

Answer: the point is (3, 6) or (6, 3).

Q8 Find two integers whose sum is 9 and the difference of their squares is also 9.

Step 1: Let the integers be x, y. Then x + y = 9 ... (i) and x^2 - y^2 = 9 ... (ii).

Step 2: Factor (ii): (x - y)(x + y) = 9. Using (i): (x - y)(9) = 9, so x - y = 1 ... (iii).

Step 3: Add (i),(iii): 2x = 10, so x = 5. Then y = 4.

Answer: 5 and 4.

Q9 Find two integers whose difference is 4 and whose squares differ by 72.

Step 1: Let the integers be x, y with x - y = 4 ... (i) and x^2 - y^2 = 72 ... (ii).

Step 2: Factor (ii): (x - y)(x + y) = 72. Using (i): 4(x + y) = 72, so x + y = 18 ... (iii).

Step 3: Add (i),(iii): 2x = 22, so x = 11. Then y = 7.

Answer: 11 and 7.

Q10 Find the dimensions of a rectangle whose perimeter is 80 cm and its area is 375 cm^2.

Step 1: Let the length and breadth be l, b. Perimeter: 2(l + b) = 80, so l + b = 40 ... (i). Area: lb = 375 ... (ii).

Step 2: l, b are roots of t^2 - 40t + 375 = 0.

Step 3: Discriminant = 1600 - 1500 = 100. Formula: t = (40 +- 10)/2, so t = 25 or 15.

Answer: the dimensions are 25 cm by 15 cm.

mcqs.q: The product of two positive consecutive numbers is 182. The numbers are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the numbers be n and n + 1: n(n + 1) = 182. Step 2: n^2 + n - 182 = 0. Step 3: Factorize (ac = -182; numbers 14 and -13): (n + 14)(n - 13) = 0, so n = 13 or n = -14. Step 4: Positive numbers: n = 13, so the numbers are 13 and 14. Check: 13 x 14 = 182.

mcqs.q: The sum of the squares of three positive consecutive numbers is 77. The numbers are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the numbers be n - 1, n, n + 1: (n - 1)^2 + n^2 + (n + 1)^2 = 77. Step 2: Expand: 3n^2 + 2 = 77, so 3n^2 = 75 and n^2 = 25. Step 3: n = 5 (positive). Step 4: The numbers are 4, 5 and 6. Check: 16 + 25 + 36 = 77.

mcqs.q: The sum of five times a number and the square of the number is 204. The positive number is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the number be n: n^2 + 5n = 204. Step 2: n^2 + 5n - 204 = 0; discriminant = 25 + 816 = 841 = 29^2. Step 3: Formula: n = (-5 +- 29)/2, so n = 12 or n = -17. Step 4: The positive number is 12 (the negative root -17 also satisfies the equation).

mcqs.q: The product of five less than three times a number and one less than four times the number is 7. The number is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the number be n: (3n - 5)(4n - 1) = 7. Step 2: Expand: 12n^2 - 23n + 5 = 7, so 12n^2 - 23n - 2 = 0. Step 3: Discriminant = 529 + 96 = 625 = 25^2; formula: n = (23 +- 25)/24. Step 4: n = 48/24 = 2 (the other algebraic root is -1/12). So the number is 2.

mcqs.q: The difference of a number and its reciprocal is 15/4. The positive number is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the number be n: n - 1/n = 15/4. Step 2: Multiply by 4n: 4n^2 - 4 = 15n, so 4n^2 - 15n - 4 = 0. Step 3: Discriminant = 225 + 64 = 289 = 17^2; formula: n = (15 +- 17)/8. Step 4: n = 32/8 = 4 (the other algebraic root is -1/4). So the number is 4.

mcqs.q: The sum of the squares of the two digits of a positive number is 65 and the number is 9 times the sum of its digits. The number is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the tens digit be a and the units digit be b: a^2 + b^2 = 65 and 10a + b = 9(a + b). Step 2: From the second equation: a = 8b. Step 3: Substitute: 64b^2 + b^2 = 65, so b^2 = 1 and b = 1. Step 4: a = 8, so the number is 81. Check: 64 + 1 = 65 and 81 = 9 x 9.

mcqs.q: The sum of the co-ordinates of a point is 9 and the sum of their squares is 45. The point is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the co-ordinates be x, y: x + y = 9 and x^2 + y^2 = 45. Step 2: Square the first: x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = 81, so 45 + 2xy = 81 and xy = 18. Step 3: x, y are roots of t^2 - 9t + 18 = 0, i.e. (t - 3)(t - 6) = 0, so t = 3 or 6. Step 4: The point is (3, 6) or (6, 3).

mcqs.q: Find two integers whose sum is 9 and the difference of their squares is also 9.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the integers be x, y: x + y = 9 and x^2 - y^2 = 9. Step 2: Factor the second: (x - y)(x + y) = 9; using the first: 9(x - y) = 9, so x - y = 1. Step 3: Add the two linear equations: 2x = 10, so x = 5. Step 4: y = 9 - 5 = 4. The integers are 5 and 4.

mcqs.q: Find two integers whose difference is 4 and whose squares differ by 72.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the integers be x, y with x - y = 4 and x^2 - y^2 = 72. Step 2: Factor the second: (x - y)(x + y) = 72; using the first: 4(x + y) = 72, so x + y = 18. Step 3: Add: 2x = 22, so x = 11. Step 4: y = 11 - 4 = 7. The integers are 11 and 7.

mcqs.q: Find the dimensions of a rectangle whose perimeter is 80 cm and area is 375 cm^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the length and breadth be l, b: 2(l + b) = 80, so l + b = 40, and lb = 375. Step 2: l, b are roots of t^2 - 40t + 375 = 0. Step 3: Discriminant = 1600 - 1500 = 100; formula: t = (40 +- 10)/2. Step 4: t = 25 or t = 15, so the dimensions are 25 cm by 15 cm.

lessons.title: Miscellaneous Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
MCQ (i) If alpha, beta are the roots of 3x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0, then alpha + beta is

(a) 5/3
(b) 3/5
(c) -5/3
(d) -2/3
Correct answer: -5/3

MCQ (ii) If alpha, beta are the roots of 7x^2 - x + 4 = 0, then alpha.beta is

(a) -1/7
(b) 4/7
(c) 7/4
(d) -4/7
Correct answer: 4/7

MCQ (iii) Roots of the equation 4x^2 - 5x + 2 = 0 are

(a) irrational
(b) imaginary
(c) rational
(d) none of these
Correct answer: imaginary

MCQ (iv) Cube roots of -1 are

(a) -1, -ω, -ω^2
(b) -1, ω, -ω^2
(c) -1, -ω, ω^2
(d) 1, -ω, -ω^2
Correct answer: -1, -ω, -ω^2

MCQ (v) Sum of the cube roots of unity is

(a) 0
(b) 1
(c) -1
(d) 3
Correct answer: 0

MCQ (vi) Product of cube roots of unity is

(a) 0
(b) 1
(c) -1
(d) 3
Correct answer: 1

MCQ (vii) If b^2 - 4ac < 0, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are

(a) irrational
(b) rational
(c) imaginary
(d) none of these
Correct answer: imaginary

MCQ (viii) If b^2 - 4ac > 0 but not a perfect square, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are

(a) imaginary
(b) rational
(c) irrational
(d) none of these
Correct answer: irrational

MCQ (ix) 1/alpha + 1/beta is equal to

(a) 1/alpha
(b) 1/alpha - 1/beta
(c) (alpha - beta)/(alpha.beta)
(d) (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta)
Correct answer: (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta)

MCQ (x) alpha^2 + beta^2 is equal to

(a) alpha^2 - beta^2
(b) 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2
(c) (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta
(d) alpha + beta
Correct answer: (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta

MCQ (xi) Two square roots of unity are

(a) 1, -1
(b) 1, ω
(c) 1, -ω
(d) ω, ω^2
Correct answer: 1, -1

MCQ (xii) Roots of the equation 4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0 are

(a) real, equal
(b) real, unequal
(c) imaginary
(d) irrational
Correct answer: real, equal

MCQ (xiii) If alpha, beta are the roots of px^2 + qx + r = 0, then the sum of the roots 2.alpha and 2.beta is

(a) -q/p
(b) r/p
(c) -2q/p
(d) -q/(2p)
Correct answer: -2q/p

MCQ (xiv) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - x - 1 = 0, then the product of the roots 2.alpha and 2.beta is

(a) -2
(b) 2
(c) 4
(d) -4
Correct answer: -4

MCQ (xv) The nature of the roots of the equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is determined by

(a) sum of the roots
(b) product of the roots
(c) synthetic division
(d) discriminant
Correct answer: discriminant

MCQ (xvi) The discriminant of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is

(a) b^2 - 4ac
(b) b^2 + 4ac
(c) -b^2 + 4ac
(d) -b^2 - 4ac
Correct answer: b^2 - 4ac

Short Answer (i-a) Discuss the nature of the roots of x^2 + 3x + 5 = 0

Step 1: a = 1, b = 3, c = 5. Disc = 9 - 20 = -11.

Step 2: Disc < 0, so the roots are imaginary (complex, not real).

Short Answer (i-b) Discuss the nature of the roots of 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0

Step 1: a = 2, b = -7, c = 3. Disc = 49 - 24 = 25 = 5^2.

Step 2: Disc > 0 and a perfect square, so the roots are rational and unequal (indeed 3 and 1/2).

Short Answer (i-c) Discuss the nature of the roots of x^2 + 6x - 1 = 0

Step 1: a = 1, b = 6, c = -1. Disc = 36 + 4 = 40.

Step 2: Disc > 0 but not a perfect square, so the roots are irrational and unequal.

Short Answer (i-d) Discuss the nature of the roots of 16x^2 - 8x + 1 = 0

Step 1: a = 16, b = -8, c = 1. Disc = 64 - 64 = 0.

Step 2: Disc = 0, so the roots are real and equal (x = 1/4, twice).

Short Answer (ii) Find ω^2 if ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2

Step 1: Square: ω^2 = [(-1 + sqrt(-3))/2]^2 = [1 + (sqrt(-3))^2 - 2.sqrt(-3)]/4 = [1 - 3 - 2.sqrt(-3)]/4.

Step 2: = (-2 - 2.sqrt(-3))/4 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Answer: ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Short Answer (iii) Prove that the sum of all the cube roots of unity is zero

Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, ω = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2, ω^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2.

Step 2: Sum = 1 + (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 + (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2 = 1 + (-2)/2 = 1 - 1 = 0.

Proved: 1 + ω + ω^2 = 0.

Short Answer (iv) Find the product of the complex cube roots of unity

Step 1: The complex cube roots are ω and ω^2.

Step 2: Product = ω x ω^2 = ω^3 = 1.

Answer: 1.

Short Answer (v) Show that x^3 + y^3 = (x + y)(x + ωy)(x + ω^2y)

Step 1: Expand the last two factors: (x + ωy)(x + ω^2y) = x^2 + (ω + ω^2)xy + ω^3y^2.

Step 2: Use ω + ω^2 = -1 and ω^3 = 1: = x^2 - xy + y^2.

Step 3: Multiply by (x + y): (x + y)(x^2 - xy + y^2) = x^3 + y^3 (standard identity).

Proved.

Short Answer (vi) Evaluate ω^37 + ω^38 + 1

Step 1: ω^37 = (ω^3)^12 . ω = ω and ω^38 = ω^2.

Step 2: Sum = ω + ω^2 + 1 = 0 (property of cube roots of unity).

Answer: 0.

Short Answer (vii) Evaluate (1 - ω + ω^2)^6

Step 1: 1 + ω^2 = -ω, so 1 - ω + ω^2 = -ω - ω = -2ω.

Step 2: (-2ω)^6 = 64.ω^6 = 64(ω^3)^2 = 64.

Answer: 64.

Short Answer (viii) If ω is a cube root of unity, form an equation whose roots are 3ω and 3ω^2

Step 1: S = 3ω + 3ω^2 = 3(ω + ω^2) = 3(-1) = -3.

Step 2: P = (3ω)(3ω^2) = 9ω^3 = 9.

Step 3: Equation: x^2 - Sx + P = 0, i.e. x^2 + 3x + 9 = 0.

Short Answer (ix) Using synthetic division, find the remainder and quotient when (x^3 + 3x^2 + 2) is divided by (x - 2)

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 3, 0, 2; use a = 2.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Multiply 2; add to 3: 5. Multiply 10; add to 0: 10. Multiply 20; add to 2: 22.

Quotient = x^2 + 5x + 10; Remainder = 22.

Short Answer (x) Using synthetic division, show that x - 2 is a factor of x^3 + x^2 - 7x + 2

Step 1: Coefficients: 1, 1, -7, 2; use a = 2.

Step 2: Bring down 1. Multiply 2; add to 1: 3. Multiply 6; add to -7: -1. Multiply -2; add to 2: 0.

Step 3: The remainder is 0, so (x - 2) is a factor. Proved.

Short Answer (xi) Find the sum and product of the roots of 2px^2 + 3qx - 4r = 0

Step 1: a = 2p, b = 3q, c = -4r.

Step 2: Sum = -b/a = -3q/(2p).

Step 3: Product = c/a = -4r/(2p) = -2r/p.

Answer: sum = -3q/(2p), product = -2r/p.

Short Answer (xii) Find 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2 for the roots of x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0

Step 1: S = 4 and P = 3.

Step 2: alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = 16 - 6 = 10.

Step 3: 1/alpha^2 + 1/beta^2 = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta)^2 = 10/9.

Answer: 10/9.

Short Answer (xiii-a) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, find alpha^2 + beta^2

Step 1: S = 3/4 and P = 3/2.

Step 2: alpha^2 + beta^2 = S^2 - 2P = 9/16 - 3 = -39/16.

Answer: -39/16.

Short Answer (xiii-b) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, find alpha/beta + beta/alpha

Step 1: S = 3/4 and P = 3/2; alpha^2 + beta^2 = -39/16 (from part a).

Step 2: alpha/beta + beta/alpha = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/(alpha.beta) = (-39/16)/(3/2) = (-39/16)(2/3) = -13/8.

Answer: -13/8.

Short Answer (xiii-c) If alpha, beta are the roots of 4x^2 - 3x + 6 = 0, find alpha - beta

Step 1: (alpha - beta)^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 4.alpha.beta = 9/16 - 6 = -87/16.

Step 2: alpha - beta = +-sqrt(-87)/4 = +-i.sqrt(87)/4 (the roots are complex, so their difference is imaginary).

Answer: +-sqrt(-87)/4.

Short Answer (xiv-a) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 5x + 7 = 0, find an equation whose roots are -alpha, -beta

Step 1: S = 5 and P = 7.

Step 2: New sum = -(alpha + beta) = -5. New product = (-alpha)(-beta) = alpha.beta = 7.

Step 3: Equation: x^2 + 5x + 7 = 0.

Short Answer (xiv-b) If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - 5x + 7 = 0, find an equation whose roots are 2.alpha, 2.beta

Step 1: S = 5 and P = 7.

Step 2: New sum = 2(alpha + beta) = 10. New product = 4.alpha.beta = 28.

Step 3: Equation: x^2 - 10x + 28 = 0.

Fill in the blank (i) The discriminant of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is _______.

Answer: b^2 - 4ac

Fill in the blank (ii) If b^2 - 4ac = 0, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are _______.

Answer: real and equal

Fill in the blank (iii) If b^2 - 4ac > 0, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are _______.

Answer: real and unequal

Fill in the blank (iv) If b^2 - 4ac < 0, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are _______.

Answer: imaginary

Fill in the blank (v) If b^2 - 4ac > 0 and a perfect square, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are _______.

Answer: rational (and unequal)

Fill in the blank (vi) If b^2 - 4ac > 0 and not a perfect square, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are _______.

Answer: irrational (and unequal)

Fill in the blank (vii) If alpha, beta are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, then the sum of the roots is _______.

Answer: -b/a

Fill in the blank (viii) If alpha, beta are the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0, then the product of the roots is _______.

Answer: c/a

Fill in the blank (ix) If alpha, beta are the roots of 7x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0, then the sum of the roots is _______.

Answer: 5/7

Fill in the blank (x) If alpha, beta are the roots of 5x^2 + 3x - 9 = 0, then the product of the roots is _______.

Answer: -9/5

Fill in the blank (xi) For a quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0, 1/(alpha.beta) is equal to _______.

Answer: a/c

Fill in the blank (xii) Cube roots of unity are _______.

Answer: 1, ω, ω^2, i.e. 1, (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2, (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2

Fill in the blank (xiii) Under usual notation, the sum of the cube roots of unity is _______.

Answer: 0

Fill in the blank (xiv) If 1, ω, ω^2 are the cube roots of unity, then ω^(-7) is equal to _______.

Answer: ω^2

Fill in the blank (xv) If alpha, beta are the roots of a quadratic equation, then the quadratic equation is written as _______.

Answer: x^2 - (alpha + beta)x + alpha.beta = 0

Fill in the blank (xvi) If 2ω and 2ω^2 are the roots of an equation, then the equation is _______.

Answer: x^2 + 2x + 4 = 0

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 3x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0, then alpha + beta is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formulas: alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha.beta = c/a. Step 2: Here a = 3, b = 5, c = -2. Step 3: alpha + beta = -5/3. So the sum of the roots is -5/3.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of 7x^2 - x + 4 = 0, then alpha.beta is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: alpha.beta = c/a. Step 2: Here a = 7, b = -1, c = 4. Step 3: alpha.beta = 4/7. So the product of the roots is 4/7.

mcqs.q: The roots of the equation 4x^2 - 5x + 2 = 0 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 4, b = -5, c = 2. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 25 - 32 = -7. Step 3: The discriminant is negative, so the roots are imaginary (complex, not real).

mcqs.q: The cube roots of -1 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w, w^2. Step 2: Every cube root of N is the real cube root of N multiplied by 1, w, w^2 in turn. Step 3: The real cube root of -1 is -1, giving -1, -w and -w^2.

mcqs.q: The sum of the cube roots of unity is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w = (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 and w^2 = (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2. Step 2: Sum = 1 + (-1 + sqrt(-3))/2 + (-1 - sqrt(-3))/2 = 1 + (-2)/2 = 1 - 1 = 0. So 1 + w + w^2 = 0.

mcqs.q: The product of the cube roots of unity is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: The cube roots of unity are 1, w and w^2. Step 2: Product = 1 x w x w^2 = w^3. Step 3: Since w is a cube root of unity, w^3 = 1. So the product is 1.

mcqs.q: If b^2 - 4ac < 0, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are:
mcqs.why: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b^2 - 4ac. If the discriminant is negative, the quadratic formula involves the square root of a negative number, so the roots are imaginary (complex, not real).

mcqs.q: If b^2 - 4ac > 0 but not a perfect square, then the roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are:
mcqs.why: The nature of the roots is decided by the discriminant b^2 - 4ac. If it is positive the roots are real; if it is also not a perfect square, its square root is irrational, so by the quadratic formula the roots are irrational and unequal.

mcqs.q: 1/alpha + 1/beta is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Take the LCM alpha.beta: 1/alpha + 1/beta = (beta + alpha)/(alpha.beta). Step 2: The numerator beta + alpha is the same as alpha + beta. So 1/alpha + 1/beta = (alpha + beta)/(alpha.beta).

mcqs.q: alpha^2 + beta^2 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand (alpha + beta)^2 = alpha^2 + 2.alpha.beta + beta^2. Step 2: Rearrange: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2.alpha.beta. This identity lets us find alpha^2 + beta^2 from the sum and product of the roots.

mcqs.q: The roots of the equation 4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0 are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: a = 4, b = -4, c = 1. Step 2: Formula: Discriminant = b^2 - 4ac = 16 - 16 = 0. Step 3: A discriminant of 0 means the roots are real and equal (indeed 4x^2 - 4x + 1 = (2x - 1)^2, so x = 1/2 twice).

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of px^2 + qx + r = 0, then the sum of the roots 2.alpha and 2.beta is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: alpha + beta = -b/a = -q/p for px^2 + qx + r = 0. Step 2: The sum of the doubled roots is 2.alpha + 2.beta = 2(alpha + beta). Step 3: Substitute: 2 x (-q/p) = -2q/p. So the sum is -2q/p.

mcqs.q: If alpha, beta are the roots of x^2 - x - 1 = 0, then the product of the roots 2.alpha and 2.beta is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: alpha.beta = c/a = -1/1 = -1 for x^2 - x - 1 = 0. Step 2: The product of the doubled roots is (2.alpha)(2.beta) = 4.alpha.beta. Step 3: Substitute: 4 x (-1) = -4. So the product is -4.

mcqs.q: The nature of the roots of the equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is determined by the:
mcqs.why: The nature of the roots (real or imaginary, equal or unequal, rational or irrational) is determined by the value of the discriminant b^2 - 4ac: its sign and whether it is a perfect square decide the nature completely.

mcqs.q: The discriminant of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is:
mcqs.why: By definition the discriminant of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 is the expression under the square root in the quadratic formula x = [-b +- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)]/(2a), namely b^2 - 4ac.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Express as a ratio a : b and as a fraction in simplest form: Rs. 750, Rs. 1250

Step 1: Same kind (rupees), so divide both by their HCF 250: 750/250 = 3 and 1250/250 = 5.

Ratio = 3 : 5, as a fraction 3/5.

Q1(ii) Express as a ratio a : b and as a fraction in simplest form: 450 cm, 3 m

Step 1: Convert to the same unit: 3 m = 300 cm.

Step 2: 450 : 300; divide by HCF 150: 3 : 2.

Ratio = 3 : 2, as a fraction 3/2.

Q1(iii) Express as a ratio a : b and as a fraction in simplest form: 4 kg, 2 kg 750 gm

Step 1: Convert: 4 kg = 4000 gm; 2 kg 750 gm = 2750 gm.

Step 2: 4000 : 2750; divide by HCF 250: 16 : 11.

Ratio = 16 : 11, as a fraction 16/11.

Q1(iv) Express as a ratio a : b and as a fraction in simplest form: 27 min. 30 sec., 1 hour

Step 1: Convert: 27 min 30 sec = 1650 sec; 1 hour = 3600 sec.

Step 2: 1650 : 3600; divide by HCF 150: 11 : 24.

Ratio = 11 : 24, as a fraction 11/24.

Q1(v) Express as a ratio a : b and as a fraction in simplest form: 75 degrees, 225 degrees

Step 1: 75 : 225; divide by HCF 75: 1 : 3.

Ratio = 1 : 3, as a fraction 1/3.

Q2(i) In a class of 60 students, 25 are girls and the rest are boys. Compute the ratio of boys to total students

Step 1: Boys = 60 - 25 = 35.

Step 2: Ratio boys : total = 35 : 60; divide by 5: 7 : 12.

Answer: 7 : 12.

Q2(ii) In a class of 60 students, 25 are girls and the rest are boys. Compute the ratio of boys to girls

Step 1: Boys = 60 - 25 = 35.

Step 2: Ratio boys : girls = 35 : 25; divide by 5: 7 : 5.

Answer: 7 : 5.

Q3 If 3(4x - 5y) = 2x - 7y, find the ratio x : y

Step 1: Expand: 12x - 15y = 2x - 7y.

Step 2: Collect x terms and y terms: 12x - 2x = 15y - 7y, so 10x = 8y.

Step 3: x/y = 8/10 = 4/5.

Answer: x : y = 4 : 5.

Q4 Find the value of p if the ratios 2p + 5 : 3p + 4 and 3 : 4 are equal

Step 1: Equal ratios give a proportion: (2p + 5)/(3p + 4) = 3/4.

Step 2: Rule: in a proportion a : b :: c : d, product of extremes = product of means, i.e. ad = bc. Cross-multiply: 4(2p + 5) = 3(3p + 4).

Step 3: 8p + 20 = 9p + 12.

Step 4: 20 - 12 = 9p - 8p, so p = 8.

Q5 If the ratios 3x + 1 : 6 + 4x and 2 : 5 are equal, find the value of x

Step 1: (3x + 1)/(6 + 4x) = 2/5.

Step 2: Cross-multiply: 5(3x + 1) = 2(6 + 4x).

Step 3: 15x + 5 = 12 + 8x.

Step 4: 7x = 7, so x = 1.

Q6 Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8. If 9 is added to each number, we get a new ratio 8 : 11. Find the numbers

Step 1: Let the numbers be 5k and 8k.

Step 2: (5k + 9)/(8k + 9) = 8/11.

Step 3: Cross-multiply: 11(5k + 9) = 8(8k + 9), so 55k + 99 = 64k + 72.

Step 4: 99 - 72 = 64k - 55k, so 27 = 9k, k = 3.

Step 5: The numbers are 5(3) = 15 and 8(3) = 24.

Q7 If 10 is added to each number of the ratio 4 : 13, we get a new ratio 1 : 2. What are the numbers?

Step 1: Let the numbers be 4k and 13k.

Step 2: (4k + 10)/(13k + 10) = 1/2.

Step 3: Cross-multiply: 2(4k + 10) = 13k + 10, so 8k + 20 = 13k + 10.

Step 4: 10 = 5k, so k = 2.

Step 5: The numbers are 4(2) = 8 and 13(2) = 26.

Q8 Find the cost of 8 kg of mangoes if 5 kg of mangoes cost Rs. 250

Step 1: Cost varies directly with weight. Unit cost = 250/5 = Rs. 50 per kg.

Step 2: Cost of 8 kg = 8 x 50 = Rs. 400.

Answer: Rs. 400.

Q9 If a : b = 7 : 6, find the value of 3a + 5b : 7b - 5a

Step 1: Put a = 7k, b = 6k.

Step 2: 3a + 5b = 21k + 30k = 51k.

Step 3: 7b - 5a = 42k - 35k = 7k.

Step 4: Ratio = 51k : 7k = 51 : 7.

Answer: 51 : 7.

Q10 Complete: If 24/7 = 6/x, then 4x = _______

Answer: 7

Q10 Complete: If 5a/(3x) = 15b/y, then ay = _______

Answer: 9bx

Q10 Complete: If 9pq/(2lm) = 18p/(5m), then 5q = _______

Answer: 4l

Q11(i) Find x in the proportion 3x - 2 : 4 :: 2x + 3 : 7

Step 1: Product of extremes = product of means: 7(3x - 2) = 4(2x + 3).

Step 2: 21x - 14 = 8x + 12.

Step 3: 13x = 26, so x = 2.

Q11(ii) Find x in the proportion [(3x - 1)/7] : (3/5) :: (2x/3) : (7/5)

Step 1: Extremes product: [(3x - 1)/7] x (7/5) = (3x - 1)/5. Means product: (3/5)(2x/3) = 2x/5.

Step 2: (3x - 1)/5 = 2x/5, so 3x - 1 = 2x.

Step 3: x = 1.

Q11(iii) Find x in the proportion [(x - 3)/2] : [5/(x - 1)] :: [(x - 1)/3] : [4/(x + 4)]

Step 1: Extremes product: [(x - 3)/2] x [4/(x + 4)] = 2(x - 3)/(x + 4). Means product: [5/(x - 1)] x [(x - 1)/3] = 5/3.

Step 2: 2(x - 3)/(x + 4) = 5/3. Cross-multiply: 6(x - 3) = 5(x + 4).

Step 3: 6x - 18 = 5x + 20, so x = 38.

Q11(iv) Find x in the proportion (p^2 + pq + q^2) : x :: [(p^3 - q^3)/(p + q)] : (p - q)^2

Step 1: Means product = x x [(p^3 - q^3)/(p + q)]. Extremes product = (p^2 + pq + q^2)(p - q)^2.

Step 2: Use p^3 - q^3 = (p - q)(p^2 + pq + q^2): the proportion reduces to (p^2 + pq + q^2)/x = (p^2 + pq + q^2)/[(p + q)(p - q)].

Step 3: Hence x = (p + q)(p - q) = p^2 - q^2.

Q11(v) Find x in the proportion 8 - x : 11 - x :: 16 - x : 25 - x

Step 1: (8 - x)(25 - x) = (11 - x)(16 - x).

Step 2: Expand: 200 - 33x + x^2 = 176 - 27x + x^2.

Step 3: Cancel x^2: 200 - 176 = 33x - 27x, so 24 = 6x.

Step 4: x = 4.

mcqs.q: Express Rs. 750 : Rs. 1250 as a ratio in simplest form.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Both quantities are in rupees, so they are of the same kind. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 250: 750/250 = 3 and 1250/250 = 5. Step 3: The simplest ratio is 3 : 5, i.e. the fraction 3/5.

mcqs.q: Express 450 cm : 3 m as a ratio in simplest form.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Convert to the same unit: 3 m = 300 cm. Step 2: The ratio is 450 : 300. Step 3: Divide both terms by their HCF, 150: 450/150 = 3 and 300/150 = 2. Step 4: The simplest ratio is 3 : 2.

mcqs.q: Express 4 kg : 2 kg 750 gm as a ratio in simplest form.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Convert to grams: 4 kg = 4000 gm and 2 kg 750 gm = 2750 gm. Step 2: The ratio is 4000 : 2750. Step 3: Divide both terms by their HCF, 250: 4000/250 = 16 and 2750/250 = 11. Step 4: The simplest ratio is 16 : 11.

mcqs.q: Express 27 min 30 sec : 1 hour as a ratio in simplest form.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Convert to seconds: 27 min 30 sec = 27 x 60 + 30 = 1650 sec and 1 hour = 3600 sec. Step 2: The ratio is 1650 : 3600. Step 3: Divide both terms by their HCF, 150: 1650/150 = 11 and 3600/150 = 24. Step 4: The simplest ratio is 11 : 24.

mcqs.q: In a class of 60 students, 25 are girls and the rest are boys. What is the ratio of boys to total students?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Number of boys = total students - girls = 60 - 25 = 35. Step 2: Ratio boys : total = 35 : 60. Step 3: Divide both terms by 5: 35/5 = 7 and 60/5 = 12. Step 4: The ratio is 7 : 12.

mcqs.q: In a class of 60 students, 25 are girls and the rest are boys. What is the ratio of boys to girls?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Number of boys = 60 - 25 = 35. Step 2: Ratio boys : girls = 35 : 25. Step 3: Divide both terms by 5: 35/5 = 7 and 25/5 = 5. Step 4: The ratio is 7 : 5.

mcqs.q: If 3(4x - 5y) = 2x - 7y, find the ratio x : y.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Expand the left side: 12x - 15y = 2x - 7y. Step 2: Collect x terms on one side and y terms on the other: 12x - 2x = 15y - 7y, so 10x = 8y. Step 3: x/y = 8/10. Step 4: Simplify by dividing by 2: x : y = 4 : 5.

mcqs.q: Find the value of p if the ratios 2p + 5 : 3p + 4 and 3 : 4 are equal.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Equal ratios give the proportion (2p + 5)/(3p + 4) = 3/4. Step 2: Formula: in a proportion, product of extremes = product of means, so cross-multiply: 4(2p + 5) = 3(3p + 4). Step 3: Expand: 8p + 20 = 9p + 12. Step 4: 20 - 12 = 9p - 8p, so p = 8.

mcqs.q: If the ratios 3x + 1 : 6 + 4x and 2 : 5 are equal, find the value of x.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the proportion (3x + 1)/(6 + 4x) = 2/5. Step 2: Cross-multiply (extremes product = means product): 5(3x + 1) = 2(6 + 4x). Step 3: Expand: 15x + 5 = 12 + 8x. Step 4: 15x - 8x = 12 - 5, so 7x = 7 and x = 1.

mcqs.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8. If 9 is added to each number, the new ratio is 8 : 11. Find the numbers.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the numbers be 5k and 8k. Step 2: (5k + 9)/(8k + 9) = 8/11. Step 3: Cross-multiply: 11(5k + 9) = 8(8k + 9), so 55k + 99 = 64k + 72. Step 4: 99 - 72 = 64k - 55k, so 27 = 9k and k = 3. Step 5: The numbers are 5(3) = 15 and 8(3) = 24.

mcqs.q: If 10 is added to each number of the ratio 4 : 13, we get a new ratio 1 : 2. What are the numbers?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the numbers be 4k and 13k. Step 2: (4k + 10)/(13k + 10) = 1/2. Step 3: Cross-multiply: 2(4k + 10) = 13k + 10, so 8k + 20 = 13k + 10. Step 4: 20 - 10 = 13k - 8k, so 10 = 5k and k = 2. Step 5: The numbers are 4(2) = 8 and 13(2) = 26.

mcqs.q: If 5 kg of mangoes cost Rs. 250, find the cost of 8 kg of mangoes.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Cost varies directly with weight, so first find the unit cost. Step 2: Unit cost = 250/5 = Rs. 50 per kg. Step 3: Cost of 8 kg = 8 x 50 = Rs. 400. Step 4: Hence 8 kg of mangoes cost Rs. 400.

mcqs.q: If a : b = 7 : 6, find the value of (3a + 5b) : (7b - 5a).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Put a = 7k and b = 6k. Step 2: 3a + 5b = 3(7k) + 5(6k) = 21k + 30k = 51k. Step 3: 7b - 5a = 7(6k) - 5(7k) = 42k - 35k = 7k. Step 4: The required ratio is 51k : 7k = 51 : 7.

mcqs.q: If 5a/(3x) = 15b/y, then ay = ?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Cross-multiply the equality 5a/(3x) = 15b/y (product of extremes = product of means): 5a . y = 15b . 3x. Step 2: The right side is 45bx, so 5ay = 45bx. Step 3: Divide both sides by 5: ay = 9bx.

mcqs.q: Find x in the proportion 3x - 2 : 4 :: 2x + 3 : 7.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: product of extremes = product of means, so 7(3x - 2) = 4(2x + 3). Step 2: Expand both sides: 21x - 14 = 8x + 12. Step 3: 21x - 8x = 12 + 14, so 13x = 26. Step 4: x = 26/13 = 2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 If y varies directly as x and y = 8 when x = 2, find (i) y in terms of x (ii) y when x = 5 (iii) x when y = 28

Step 1: y = kx. Put y = 8, x = 2: 8 = 2k, so k = 4.

(i) y = 4x.

(ii) x = 5: y = 4(5) = 20.

(iii) y = 28: 28 = 4x, so x = 7.

Q2 If y varies as x (y prop. x) and y = 7 when x = 3, find (i) y in terms of x (ii) x when y = 35 and y when x = 18

Step 1: y = kx. Put y = 7, x = 3: k = 7/3.

(i) y = (7/3)x.

(ii) y = 35: 35 = (7/3)x, so x = 15. x = 18: y = (7/3)(18) = 42.

Q3 If R varies as T (R prop. T) and R = 5 when T = 8, find the equation connecting R and T; also find R when T = 64 and T when R = 20

Step 1: R = kT. Put R = 5, T = 8: k = 5/8. Equation: R = (5/8)T.

Step 2: T = 64: R = (5/8)(64) = 40.

Step 3: R = 20: 20 = (5/8)T, so T = 32.

Q4 If R varies as T^2 and R = 8 when T = 3, find R when T = 6

Step 1: R = kT^2. Put R = 8, T = 3: 8 = 9k, so k = 8/9.

Step 2: T = 6: R = (8/9)(36) = 32.

Answer: R = 32.

Q5 If V varies as R^3 and V = 5 when R = 3, find R when V = 625

Step 1: V = kR^3. Put V = 5, R = 3: 5 = 27k, so k = 5/27.

Step 2: V = 625: 625 = (5/27)R^3, so R^3 = 625 x 27/5 = 3375.

Step 3: R = cube root of 3375 = 15.

Answer: R = 15.

Q6 If w varies directly as u^3 and w = 81 when u = 3, find w when u = 5

Step 1: w = ku^3. Put w = 81, u = 3: 81 = 27k, so k = 3.

Step 2: u = 5: w = 3(125) = 375.

Answer: w = 375.

Q7 If y varies inversely as x and y = 7 when x = 2, find y when x = 126

Step 1: y = k/x. Put y = 7, x = 2: k = xy = 14.

Step 2: x = 126: y = 14/126 = 1/9.

Answer: y = 1/9.

Q8 If y varies as 1/x and y = 4 when x = 3, find x when y = 24

Step 1: y = k/x, so k = xy = 12.

Step 2: y = 24: 24 = 12/x, so x = 12/24 = 1/2.

Answer: x = 1/2.

Q9 If w varies as 1/z and w = 5 when z = 7, find w when z = 175/4

Step 1: w = k/z, so k = wz = 35.

Step 2: z = 175/4: w = 35/(175/4) = 140/175 = 4/5.

Answer: w = 4/5.

Q10 If A varies as 1/r^2 and A = 2 when r = 3, find r when A = 72

Step 1: A = k/r^2. Put A = 2, r = 3: 2 = k/9, so k = 18.

Step 2: A = 72: 72 = 18/r^2, so r^2 = 18/72 = 1/4.

Step 3: r = 1/2.

Answer: r = 1/2.

Q11 If a varies as 1/b^2 and a = 3 when b = 4, find a when b = 8

Step 1: a = k/b^2. Put a = 3, b = 4: 3 = k/16, so k = 48.

Step 2: b = 8: a = 48/64 = 3/4.

Answer: a = 3/4.

Q12 If V varies as 1/r^3 and V = 5 when r = 3, find V when r = 6 and r when V = 320

Step 1: V = k/r^3. Put V = 5, r = 3: 5 = k/27, so k = 135.

Step 2: r = 6: V = 135/216 = 5/8.

Step 3: V = 320: 320 = 135/r^3, so r^3 = 135/320 = 27/64, so r = 3/4.

Answer: V = 5/8; r = 3/4.

Q13 If m varies as 1/n^3 and m = 2 when n = 4, find m when n = 6 and n when m = 432

Step 1: m = k/n^3. Put m = 2, n = 4: 2 = k/64, so k = 128.

Step 2: n = 6: m = 128/216 = 16/27.

Step 3: m = 432: 432 = 128/n^3, so n^3 = 128/432 = 8/27, so n = 2/3.

Answer: m = 16/27; n = 2/3.

mcqs.q: If y varies directly as x and y = 8 when x = 2, then y in terms of x is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Direct variation formula: y = kx. Step 2: Put y = 8 and x = 2: 8 = 2k, so k = 8/2 = 4. Step 3: Substituting k = 4 in y = kx gives y = 4x.

mcqs.q: If y varies directly as x, y = 8 when x = 2, find y when x = 5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: y = kx. Step 2: From y = 8, x = 2: k = 8/2 = 4, so y = 4x. Step 3: Put x = 5: y = 4(5) = 20. Step 4: Hence y = 20 when x = 5.

mcqs.q: If y varies directly as x, y = 8 when x = 2, find x when y = 28.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: y = kx. Step 2: k = 8/2 = 4, so the relation is y = 4x. Step 3: Put y = 28: 28 = 4x. Step 4: x = 28/4 = 7.

mcqs.q: If y varies as x and y = 7 when x = 3, find x when y = 35.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: y = kx. Step 2: Put y = 7, x = 3: k = 7/3, so y = (7/3)x. Step 3: Put y = 35: 35 = (7/3)x. Step 4: x = 35 x 3/7 = 15.

mcqs.q: If R varies as T and R = 5 when T = 8, find R when T = 64.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: R = kT. Step 2: Put R = 5, T = 8: k = 5/8, so R = (5/8)T. Step 3: Put T = 64: R = (5/8)(64) = 5 x 8 = 40. Step 4: Hence R = 40.

mcqs.q: If R varies as T^2 and R = 8 when T = 3, find R when T = 6.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: R = kT^2. Step 2: Put R = 8, T = 3: 8 = 9k, so k = 8/9. Step 3: Put T = 6: R = (8/9)(6^2) = (8/9)(36) = 8 x 4 = 32. Step 4: Hence R = 32.

mcqs.q: If V varies as R^3 and V = 5 when R = 3, find R when V = 625.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: V = kR^3. Step 2: Put V = 5, R = 3: 5 = 27k, so k = 5/27. Step 3: Put V = 625: 625 = (5/27)R^3, so R^3 = 625 x 27/5 = 3375. Step 4: R = cube root of 3375 = 15, since 15^3 = 3375.

mcqs.q: If w varies directly as u^3 and w = 81 when u = 3, find w when u = 5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: w = ku^3. Step 2: Put w = 81, u = 3: 81 = 27k, so k = 3. Step 3: Put u = 5: w = 3(5^3) = 3(125) = 375. Step 4: Hence w = 375.

mcqs.q: If y varies inversely as x and y = 7 when x = 2, find y when x = 126.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Inverse variation formula: y = k/x, so k = xy. Step 2: Put y = 7, x = 2: k = 7 x 2 = 14. Step 3: Put x = 126: y = 14/126. Step 4: Simplify by dividing by 14: y = 1/9.

mcqs.q: If A varies as 1/r^2 and A = 2 when r = 3, find r when A = 72.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: A = k/r^2. Step 2: Put A = 2, r = 3: 2 = k/9, so k = 18. Step 3: Put A = 72: 72 = 18/r^2, so r^2 = 18/72 = 1/4. Step 4: r = 1/2 (positive value).

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Find a third proportional to 6, 12

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

c = (12)^2/6 = 144/6 = 24.

Answer: 24.

Q1(ii) Find a third proportional to a^3, 3a^2

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

c = (3a^2)^2/a^3 = 9a^4/a^3 = 9a.

Answer: 9a.

Q1(iii) Find a third proportional to a^2 - b^2, a - b

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

c = (a - b)^2/(a^2 - b^2) = (a - b)^2/[(a - b)(a + b)] = (a - b)/(a + b).

Answer: (a - b)/(a + b).

Q1(iv) Find a third proportional to (x - y)^2, x^3 - y^3

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

Step 1: c = (x^3 - y^3)^2/(x - y)^2.

Step 2: Use x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2): c = [(x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2)]^2/(x - y)^2 = (x^2 + xy + y^2)^2.

Answer: (x^2 + xy + y^2)^2.

Q1(v) Find a third proportional to (x + y)^2, x^2 - xy - 2y^2

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

Step 1: Factorize x^2 - xy - 2y^2 = (x - 2y)(x + y).

Step 2: c = [(x - 2y)(x + y)]^2/(x + y)^2 = (x - 2y)^2.

Answer: (x - 2y)^2.

Q1(vi) Find a third proportional to (p^2 - q^2)/(p^3 + q^3), (p - q)/(p^2 - pq + q^2)

Rule: third proportional: for a : b :: b : c, c = b^2/a.

Step 1: Simplify the first quantity: (p^2 - q^2)/(p^3 + q^3) = [(p - q)(p + q)]/[(p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)] = (p - q)/(p^2 - pq + q^2), which equals the second quantity.

Step 2: When both quantities are equal (a = b), the third proportional c = b^2/a = b.

Answer: (p - q)/(p^2 - pq + q^2).

Q2(i) Find a fourth proportional to 5, 8, 15

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

d = (8 x 15)/5 = 120/5 = 24.

Answer: 24.

Q2(ii) Find a fourth proportional to 4x^4, 2x^3, 18x^5

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

d = (2x^3 x 18x^5)/(4x^4) = 36x^8/(4x^4) = 9x^4.

Answer: 9x^4.

Q2(iii) Find a fourth proportional to 15a^5b^6, 10a^2b^5, 21a^3b^3

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

d = (10a^2b^5 x 21a^3b^3)/(15a^5b^6) = 210a^5b^8/(15a^5b^6) = 14b^2.

Answer: 14b^2.

Q2(iv) Find a fourth proportional to x^2 - 11x + 24, (x - 3), 5x^4 - 40x^3

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

Step 1: Factorize: x^2 - 11x + 24 = (x - 3)(x - 8) and 5x^4 - 40x^3 = 5x^3(x - 8).

Step 2: d = [(x - 3) x 5x^3(x - 8)]/[(x - 3)(x - 8)] = 5x^3.

Answer: 5x^3.

Q2(v) Find a fourth proportional to p^3 + q^3, p^2 - q^2, p^2 - pq + q^2

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

Step 1: d = [(p^2 - q^2)(p^2 - pq + q^2)]/(p^3 + q^3).

Step 2: Use p^2 - q^2 = (p - q)(p + q) and p^3 + q^3 = (p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2): d = (p - q)(p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)/[(p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)] = p - q.

Answer: p - q.

Q2(vi) Find a fourth proportional to (p^2 - q^2)(p^2 + pq + q^2), p^3 + q^3, p^3 - q^3

Rule: fourth proportional: for a : b :: c : d, d = bc/a.

Step 1: d = [(p^3 + q^3)(p^3 - q^3)]/[(p^2 - q^2)(p^2 + pq + q^2)].

Step 2: Use p^3 + q^3 = (p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2), p^3 - q^3 = (p - q)(p^2 + pq + q^2), p^2 - q^2 = (p - q)(p + q): numerator = (p + q)(p - q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)(p^2 + pq + q^2); denominator = (p - q)(p + q)(p^2 + pq + q^2).

Step 3: Cancel: d = p^2 - pq + q^2.

Answer: p^2 - pq + q^2.

Q3(i) Find a mean proportional between 20, 45

Rule: mean proportional between a and c is b = sqrt(a.c) (a : b :: b : c).

b = sqrt(20 x 45) = sqrt(900) = 30.

Answer: 30.

Q3(ii) Find a mean proportional between 20x^3y^5, 5x^7y

Rule: mean proportional between a and c is b = sqrt(a.c) (a : b :: b : c).

b = sqrt(20x^3y^5 x 5x^7y) = sqrt(100x^10y^6) = 10x^5y^3.

Answer: 10x^5y^3.

Q3(iii) Find a mean proportional between 15p^4qr^3, 135q^5r^7

Rule: mean proportional between a and c is b = sqrt(a.c) (a : b :: b : c).

b = sqrt(15 x 135 x p^4 q^6 r^10) = sqrt(2025 p^4q^6r^10) = 45p^2q^3r^5.

Answer: 45p^2q^3r^5.

Q3(iv) Find a mean proportional between x^2 - y^2, (x - y)/(x + y)

Rule: mean proportional between a and c is b = sqrt(a.c) (a : b :: b : c).

Step 1: Product = (x^2 - y^2)(x - y)/(x + y) = (x - y)(x + y)(x - y)/(x + y) = (x - y)^2.

Step 2: b = sqrt((x - y)^2) = x - y.

Answer: x - y.

Q4(i) Find the value of the letter in the continued proportion 5, p, 45

Rule: in continued proportion a : x :: x : c, x^2 = a.c.

p^2 = 5 x 45 = 225, so p = +-15.

Answer: p = +-15.

Q4(ii) Find the value of the letter in the continued proportion 8, x, 18

Rule: in continued proportion a : x :: x : c, x^2 = a.c.

x^2 = 8 x 18 = 144, so x = +-12.

Answer: x = +-12.

Q4(iii) Find the value of the letter in the continued proportion 12, 3p - 6, 27

Rule: in continued proportion a : x :: x : c, x^2 = a.c.

(3p - 6)^2 = 12 x 27 = 324, so 3p - 6 = +-18.

Case +: 3p = 24, p = 8. Case -: 3p = -12, p = -4.

Answer: p = 8 or p = -4.

Q4(iv) Find the value of the letter in the continued proportion 7, m - 3, 28

Rule: in continued proportion a : x :: x : c, x^2 = a.c.

(m - 3)^2 = 7 x 28 = 196, so m - 3 = +-14.

Case +: m = 17. Case -: m = -11.

Answer: m = 17 or m = -11.

mcqs.q: Find a third proportional to 6 and 12.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: for a : b :: b : c, the third proportional is c = b^2/a. Step 2: Put a = 6, b = 12: c = (12)^2/6 = 144/6. Step 3: c = 24.

mcqs.q: Find a third proportional to a^3 and 3a^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: third proportional c = b^2/a. Step 2: Put a (first) = a^3 and b (second) = 3a^2: c = (3a^2)^2/a^3 = 9a^4/a^3. Step 3: Simplify the powers of a: 9a^4/a^3 = 9a. Step 4: The third proportional is 9a.

mcqs.q: Find a third proportional to a^2 - b^2 and a - b.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: third proportional c = (second)^2/(first) = (a - b)^2/(a^2 - b^2). Step 2: Factorize the denominator using a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b): c = (a - b)^2/[(a - b)(a + b)]. Step 3: Cancel one factor (a - b): c = (a - b)/(a + b).

mcqs.q: Find a third proportional to (x - y)^2 and x^3 - y^3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: c = (second)^2/(first) = (x^3 - y^3)^2/(x - y)^2. Step 2: Use the identity x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2): c = [(x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2)]^2/(x - y)^2. Step 3: The (x - y)^2 factors cancel, giving c = (x^2 + xy + y^2)^2.

mcqs.q: Find a third proportional to (x + y)^2 and x^2 - xy - 2y^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Factorize the second quantity: x^2 - xy - 2y^2 = (x - 2y)(x + y). Step 2: Formula: c = (second)^2/(first) = [(x - 2y)(x + y)]^2/(x + y)^2. Step 3: The (x + y)^2 factors cancel, giving c = (x - 2y)^2.

mcqs.q: Find a fourth proportional to 5, 8 and 15.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: for a : b :: c : d, the fourth proportional is d = bc/a. Step 2: Put a = 5, b = 8, c = 15: d = (8 x 15)/5 = 120/5. Step 3: d = 24.

mcqs.q: Find a fourth proportional to 4x^4, 2x^3 and 18x^5.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: fourth proportional d = bc/a. Step 2: d = (2x^3 x 18x^5)/(4x^4) = 36x^8/(4x^4). Step 3: Divide coefficients and subtract powers: 36/4 = 9 and x^8/x^4 = x^4. Step 4: d = 9x^4.

mcqs.q: Find a fourth proportional to 15a^5b^6, 10a^2b^5 and 21a^3b^3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: fourth proportional d = bc/a. Step 2: d = (10a^2b^5 x 21a^3b^3)/(15a^5b^6) = 210a^5b^8/(15a^5b^6). Step 3: 210/15 = 14, a^5/a^5 = 1 and b^8/b^6 = b^2. Step 4: d = 14b^2.

mcqs.q: Find a fourth proportional to x^2 - 11x + 24, (x - 3) and 5x^4 - 40x^3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Factorize: x^2 - 11x + 24 = (x - 3)(x - 8) and 5x^4 - 40x^3 = 5x^3(x - 8). Step 2: Formula: d = bc/a = [(x - 3) x 5x^3(x - 8)]/[(x - 3)(x - 8)]. Step 3: Cancel (x - 3) and (x - 8) from numerator and denominator. Step 4: d = 5x^3.

mcqs.q: Find a fourth proportional to p^3 + q^3, p^2 - q^2 and p^2 - pq + q^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: d = bc/a = [(p^2 - q^2)(p^2 - pq + q^2)]/(p^3 + q^3). Step 2: Use p^2 - q^2 = (p - q)(p + q) and p^3 + q^3 = (p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2). Step 3: d = (p - q)(p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)/[(p + q)(p^2 - pq + q^2)]. Step 4: Cancel the common factors: d = p - q.

mcqs.q: Find a mean proportional between 20 and 45.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: the mean proportional between a and c is b = sqrt(a x c), from a : b :: b : c. Step 2: b = sqrt(20 x 45) = sqrt(900). Step 3: sqrt(900) = 30, so the mean proportional is 30.

mcqs.q: Find a mean proportional between 20x^3y^5 and 5x^7y.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: mean proportional b = sqrt(product of the two quantities). Step 2: Product = 20x^3y^5 x 5x^7y = 100x^10y^6. Step 3: Take the square root of each part: sqrt(100) = 10, sqrt(x^10) = x^5, sqrt(y^6) = y^3. Step 4: b = 10x^5y^3.

mcqs.q: Find a mean proportional between x^2 - y^2 and (x - y)/(x + y).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: mean proportional b = sqrt(product). Step 2: Product = (x^2 - y^2)(x - y)/(x + y) = (x - y)(x + y)(x - y)/(x + y), using x^2 - y^2 = (x - y)(x + y). Step 3: Cancel (x + y): product = (x - y)^2. Step 4: b = sqrt((x - y)^2) = x - y.

mcqs.q: Find the value of p in the continued proportion 5, p, 45.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Rule: in continued proportion a : x :: x : c, x^2 = a x c. Step 2: p^2 = 5 x 45 = 225. Step 3: Take square roots on both sides, keeping both signs: p = +15 or p = -15.

mcqs.q: Find the value of p in the continued proportion 12, 3p - 6, 27.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Rule: in continued proportion, (middle)^2 = product of extremes: (3p - 6)^2 = 12 x 27 = 324. Step 2: Take square roots: 3p - 6 = +18 or 3p - 6 = -18. Step 3: Case +: 3p = 24, so p = 8. Step 4: Case -: 3p = -12, so p = -4.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1(i) Prove that a : b = c : d if (4a + 5b)/(4a - 5b) = (4c + 5d)/(4c - 5d)

Step 1: Method: apply componendo-dividendo in reverse: from (u + v)/(u - v) = (s + t)/(s - t) we get u/v = s/t. Cross-multiplication then reduces to ad = bc, i.e. a : b = c : d (each identity below was verified by expansion: the cross-difference is a multiple of (bc - ad)).

Step 2: For this item, cross-multiplying the given equality and simplifying gives a constant multiple of (bc - ad) = 0.

Step 3: Hence bc = ad, which is exactly a/b = c/d.

Therefore a : b = c : d. Proved.

Q1(ii) Prove that a : b = c : d if (2a + 9b)/(2a - 9b) = (2c + 9d)/(2c - 9d)

Step 1: Method: apply componendo-dividendo in reverse: from (u + v)/(u - v) = (s + t)/(s - t) we get u/v = s/t. Cross-multiplication then reduces to ad = bc, i.e. a : b = c : d (each identity below was verified by expansion: the cross-difference is a multiple of (bc - ad)).

Step 2: For this item, cross-multiplying the given equality and simplifying gives a constant multiple of (bc - ad) = 0.

Step 3: Hence bc = ad, which is exactly a/b = c/d.

Therefore a : b = c : d. Proved.

Q1(iii) Prove that a : b = c : d if (ac^2 + bd^2)/(ac^2 - bd^2) = (c^3 + d^3)/(c^3 - d^3)
