Answer: in-radius

Fill in the blank (xxv) The radius of a circumscribed circle is called ____.

Answer: circumradius

mcqs.q: The circumference of a circle is called its:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (i) keys the circumference as the boundary of the circle: the circumference is the curved boundary line enclosing the circle. A chord is a line segment joining two points of the circle, and a segment is a region cut off by a chord.

mcqs.q: A line intersecting a circle at two points is called a:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (ii) keys a line that cuts the circle at two points as a secant. A tangent touches at only one point, while a chord is the segment of the secant between the two points of the circle.

mcqs.q: The portion of a circle between two radii and an arc is called a:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (iii) keys this region as a sector: it is bounded by two radii and the arc between them. A segment, by contrast, is bounded by a chord and an arc, with no radii involved.

mcqs.q: The angle inscribed in a semi-circle measures:
mcqs.why: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle (Unit 12, Theorem 3). A right angle equals 90 degrees, which in radians is pi/2. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (iv).

mcqs.q: The length of the diameter of a circle is how many times its radius?
mcqs.why: The diameter passes through the centre joining two points of the circle, so it consists of two radii in a straight line: diameter = 2 x radius. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (v).

mcqs.q: The tangent and the radius at the point of contact are:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (vi) keys the tangent as perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. This fact is the basis of the tangent constructions: the tangent at P is drawn perpendicular to radius OP.

mcqs.q: Two circles having three points in common must:
options: Coincide, i.e. be one and the same circle
mcqs.why: One and only one circle passes through three non-collinear points, so two circles sharing three points are the same circle and coincide. The book's fill-in-the-blank (v) of this exercise also gives 'coincide'. Note: the book's printed MCQ (vii) omits this correct option, which is recorded in the flags.

mcqs.q: If two circles touch each other, their centres and the point of contact are:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (viii) keys them as collinear: when two circles touch, the point of contact lies on the straight line joining the two centres, so centres and contact point are on one line.

mcqs.q: The measure of the external angle of a regular hexagon is:
mcqs.why: Formula: external angle = 360 degrees / number of sides. Step 1: For a hexagon, 360/6 = 60 degrees. Step 2: 60 degrees = pi/3 radians. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (ix).

mcqs.q: If the in-centre and circumcentre of a triangle coincide, the triangle is:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (x) keys an equilateral triangle: only in an equilateral triangle do the angle bisectors and the perpendicular bisectors of the sides all meet at the same single point, so in-centre and circumcentre coincide.

mcqs.q: The measure of the external angle of a regular octagon is:
mcqs.why: Formula: external angle = 360 degrees / number of sides. Step 1: For an octagon, 360/8 = 45 degrees. Step 2: 45 degrees = pi/4 radians. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (xi).

mcqs.q: Tangents drawn at the end points of a diameter of a circle are:
mcqs.why: Each tangent is perpendicular to the diameter at its own end point. Two lines both perpendicular to the same straight line are parallel to each other. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (xii), with 'parallel' as the correct option.

mcqs.q: The lengths of the two transverse common tangents to a pair of circles are:
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (xiii) keys them as equal: the two transverse common tangents of a pair of circles have equal lengths, just as the two direct common tangents are also equal in length, as stated in the fill-in-the-blanks of this exercise.

mcqs.q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point outside the circle?
mcqs.why: From an external point P exactly two tangents can be drawn, one touching the circle on each side, as in Construction 13.3(ii-b) using the semicircle on OP. This is the book's keyed answer for MCQ (xiv).

mcqs.q: How many common tangents can be drawn for two touching circles?
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ (xvii) keys 3: two touching circles have two direct common tangents plus the single tangent at their point of contact, making 3 common tangents in total. Disjoint circles have 4 and intersecting circles have 2.

lessons.title: Miscellaneous Exercise 13 - Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Q2(i)(a) Define and draw: the segment of a circle

Definition: The portion of a circle bounded by an arc and its chord is called a segment of the circle. The segment cut off by a chord smaller than a semicircle is the minor segment; the larger one is the major segment.

Figure (in words): Draw a circle, draw a chord AB across it, and shade the region between chord AB and the minor arc AB - that shaded region is the (minor) segment.

Q2(i)(b) Define and draw: the tangent to a circle

Definition: A straight line which touches a circle at exactly one point (the point of contact) is called a tangent to the circle. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

Figure (in words): Draw a circle with centre O, mark a point P on the circumference, join OP, and draw the line through P perpendicular to OP - that line is the tangent at P.

Q2(i)(c) Define and draw: the sector of a circle

Definition: The circular region bounded by an arc of a circle and its two corresponding radial segments is called a sector of the circle.

Figure (in words): Draw a circle with centre O, draw two radii OA and OB, and shade the region bounded by OA, OB and the arc AB - that shaded region is a sector.

Q2(i)(d) Define and draw: the inscribed circle

Definition: The circle which touches the three sides of a triangle internally is called the inscribed circle (incircle) of the triangle; its centre is the in-centre (the meeting point of the angle bisectors) and its radius the in-radius.

Figure (in words): Draw a triangle ABC, bisect two of its angles to meet at O inside, drop a perpendicular from O to a side, and draw the circle with centre O and that perpendicular as radius, touching all three sides from inside.

Q2(i)(e) Define and draw: the circumscribed circle

Definition: The circle which passes through all three vertices of a triangle is called the circumscribed circle (circumcircle) of the triangle; its centre is the circumcentre (the meeting point of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides) and its radius the circumradius.

Figure (in words): Draw a triangle ABC, draw the perpendicular bisectors of two sides to meet at O, and draw the circle with centre O and radius OA passing through A, B and C.

Q2(i)(f) Define and draw: the escribed circle

Definition: The circle which touches one side of a triangle externally and the other two produced sides is called an escribed circle (e-circle) of the triangle; its centre is the e-centre (the meeting point of the bisectors of two exterior angles and the interior bisector of the third) and its radius the e-radius.

Figure (in words): Draw a triangle ABC, produce sides AB and AC, bisect the exterior angles at B and C to meet at I1 outside the triangle, drop a perpendicular from I1 to side BC, and draw the circle with centre I1 and that perpendicular as radius, touching BC externally.

Q2(ii) The length of each side of a regular octagon is 3 cm. Measure its perimeter

Formula: Perimeter of a regular polygon = number of sides x length of one side.

Step 1: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides.

Step 2: Perimeter = 8 x 3 cm = 24 cm.

Q2(iii) Write down the formula for finding the angle subtended by the side of an n-sided polygon at the centre of the circle

Formula: Angle at the centre = 360 deg / n (in degrees) = 2 x pi / n radians, where n is the number of sides of the regular polygon.

Check: for a hexagon (n = 6): 360/6 = 60 deg; for a square (n = 4): 90 deg; for an octagon (n = 8): 45 deg.

Q2(iv) The length of the side of a regular pentagon is 5 cm; what is its perimeter?

Formula: Perimeter = number of sides x length of one side.

Step 1: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides.

Step 2: Perimeter = 5 x 5 cm = 25 cm.

mcqs.q: The segment of a circle is defined as the portion of a circle bounded by:
mcqs.why: By definition, a segment is the region bounded by an arc and its chord. The segment cut off by a chord smaller than a semicircle is the minor segment; the larger region on the other side of the chord is the major segment.

mcqs.q: A tangent to a circle is a straight line which:
options: Cuts the circle at two points
Touches the circle at exactly one point, the point of contact
Joins two points of the circle
mcqs.why: By definition a tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact, and it is perpendicular to the radius at that point. A line cutting at two points is a secant, not a tangent.

mcqs.q: A sector of a circle is the region bounded by:
options: An arc and its two corresponding radii
mcqs.why: By definition, a sector is the circular region bounded by an arc of the circle and the two radial segments (radii) drawn to the ends of that arc, like a slice of the circle with vertex at the centre.

mcqs.q: The inscribed circle (incircle) of a triangle is the circle which:
options: Touches the three sides of the triangle internally
Touches one side externally and the other two produced sides
Has the longest side as diameter
mcqs.why: The incircle touches all three sides from inside the triangle. Its centre is the in-centre, the meeting point of the angle bisectors, and its radius is the in-radius, the perpendicular distance from the in-centre to a side.

mcqs.q: The circumscribed circle (circumcircle) of a triangle is the circle which:
options: Passes through all three vertices of the triangle
mcqs.why: The circumcircle passes through vertices A, B and C. Its centre is the circumcentre, the meeting point of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides, and its radius OA is the circumradius.

mcqs.q: An escribed circle (e-circle) of a triangle is a circle which:
options: Touches one side of the triangle externally and the other two produced sides
Touches only the longest side from inside
mcqs.why: By definition the escribed circle touches one side externally and the extensions (produced parts) of the other two sides. Its centre, the e-centre, is the meeting point of the bisectors of two exterior angles and the interior bisector of the third angle.

mcqs.q: Each side of a regular octagon is 3 cm. Its perimeter is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Perimeter of a regular polygon = number of sides x length of one side. Step 1: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. Step 2: Perimeter = 8 x 3 cm = 24 cm.

mcqs.q: The side of a regular pentagon is 5 cm. Its perimeter is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Perimeter = number of sides x length of one side. Step 1: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides. Step 2: Perimeter = 5 x 5 cm = 25 cm.

mcqs.q: The angle subtended by the side of a regular n-sided polygon at the centre of its circle is given by the formula:
mcqs.why: The n equal central angles around the centre sum to a complete turn of 360 degrees, so each one is 360 degrees / n, equivalently 2 x pi / n radians, where n is the number of sides of the regular polygon.

mcqs.q: Using the central-angle formula, the angle subtended by one side of a regular hexagon at the centre is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Angle at the centre = 360 degrees / n. Step 1: For a hexagon n = 6. Step 2: Angle = 360/6 = 60 degrees. This matches the construction of the inscribed hexagon, where triangles OAB and OAF are equilateral with 60 degree angles at O.
